Irrigation Department, Sri Lanka Mahaweli Authority, Mahaweli Consultancy Services Bureau and the Agrarian Development Department function as the implementation institutions of that programme. “Wari Saubhagya” programme is expected to be completed within three years and therefore, it has been found appropriate to obtain the services of State institutions and Semi-Government institutions for the purpose. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Irrigation to award the construction contracts up to Rs. 50 million of the “Wari Saubhagya” programme also to the Semi-Government institutions such as Sri Lanka Land Development Corporation, State Development and Construction Corporation, National Equipment and Machinery Organization, Central Engineering Services Corporation, Mahaweli Consultancy Services Bureau and the Maga Neguma Department by following the direct contract awarding procedure, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Utilization of Warehouses/Buildings belonging to the Cooperative Wholesale Establishment for effective activities
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-11-01
decision_details_body: - The warehouses/building premises belonging to the Cooperative Wholesale Establishment (CWE) have been provided to public institutions and also to the private sector. The Board of Directors of CWE has proposed to provide the warehouses/building premises not in use belonging to the said Corporation to private sector institutions on rent basis for shorter span, following the Government Procurement process. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade to rent the said warehouses/building premises to private sector institutions on rent basis for the value assessed by the Government Chief Valuer and provide such warehouses/building premises suitable for Public‑Private Partnership Investment Projects on long term lease basis by calling for Expressions of Interest (EoI), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing a land located in Thalapathpitiya, belonging to the Urban Development Authority on lease basis for the implementation of a Mixed Development Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-11-01
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2020‑10‑19 to call for proposals for the implementation of a Mixed Development project on a land in the extent of 2 acres 6.32 perches located in Thalapathpitiya belonging to the Urban Development Authority (UDA). Accordingly, proposals have been called on Design, Build, Finance, Operate Transfer basis from investors on competitive basis. Three investors have submitted proposals for the purpose and the Standing Cabinet Appointed Negotiation Committee has recommended the proposal submitted by 'M/s International Construction Consortium (Pvt.) Ltd.'. Concurrence of the Board of Management of the UDA has also been granted for the said recommendation. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing to provide the relevant block of land to 'M/s International Construction Consortium (Pvt.) Ltd.' on long term lease basis for the implementation of the said project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: General Policy Guidelines pertaining to the Electricity Industry
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-11-01
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2021‑09‑13 for the major policy targets such as achieving 70% of the electricity generation from the renewable sources by the year 2030, not establishing new coal power plants in future and neutralizing the Zero Carbon Emission that takes place in power generation by the year 2050. And also, it has been decided at the said Cabinet meeting to issue the 'General Policy Guidelines' for the Power industry in terms of the said Cabinet decision and to formulate the Least Cost Long Term Generation Plan by the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) pertaining to the period of 2022‑2041 in accordance with the said guidelines. As such, approval of the Cabinet was granted for the 'General Policy Guidelines for Electricity Industry' prepared in terms of the provision of section 5 of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act, No.20 of 2009 and to table the said guidelines, as proposed by the Minister of Power.

description: Implementation of a concessionary loan scheme for intensification of Shrimp Farming with the objective of increasing production and exports
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-11-01
decision_details_body: - The National Aquaculture Development Authority of Sri Lanka (NAQDA) has planned to increase the country's shrimp production of around 8,000 MT in the year 2020, up to 50,000MT by 2025. With a view to increasing the shrimp production in the years 2019 and 2020, farming of Vannamei shrimps has been introduced. There is a possibility of obtaining a higher production for the reasons of their faster growth, lower susceptibility to diseases and the potential of farming under high stocking densities in farming them in ponds. It is also possible to farm the said type of shrimps under three cycles per year. However, in view of carrying out the farming of shrimps under high density and easing the removal of higher amount of organic waste accumulated in the pond on the said reason, it is essential to lay High Density Poly Ethylene (HDPE) to cover the traditional shrimp farming ponds with mud bottom being used for farming and modernize them. And also, in parallel with this, it is essential to increase the capacity of the shrimp processing plants to store the increasing production of shrimps for export purposes and produce value‑added products and to modernize them by using the state of the art technology. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Fisheries to implement a concessionary loan scheme through the State Banks to secure the required capital for encouraging the shrimp farmers to engage in Vannamei shrimp farming, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Agreement between the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University (KDU) and the Duke University (DUKE), USA
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-11-01
decision_details_body: - Melioidosis, which is a bacteria infection, appears mostly in the tropical areas of the world. It has been proposed to enter into a Research Agreement between the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University (KDU) and the Duke University (DUKE), USA, in view of early detection of the said disease in the country, understanding and controlling of the disease. Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E. The President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence to enter into a Sub‑Award Agreement and a Material Transfer Agreement for the implementation of the proposed Research Agreement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Debt Conciliation Ordinance
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-25
decision_details_body: - The Debt Conciliation Board expects to protect the rights of the debt-ridden people. It has been identified necessary to amend the Debt Conciliation Ordinance to suit the present needs, enabling the effective performance of the said task. For the purpose, the Advisory Committee to review the Debt Conciliation Ordinance appointed by the Minister of Justice, has formulated a preliminary draft. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to amend the Debt Conciliation Ordinance based on the said preliminary draft and instruct the Legal Draftsman to formulate a draft Bill for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the Long Term Contract for the importation of Gasoline within a period of eight months from 2022-01-01 to 2022-08-31
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-25
decision_details_body: - Bids have been called from the bidders registered at the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) to award the Long Term Contract for the importation of 1,341,000 Bbls +10/- 5% of Gasoline (92 Unl) and 459,000 Bbls +10/- 5% of Gasoline (95 Unl) within a period of eight months from 2022‑01‑01 to 2022‑08‑31. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Energy to award the relevant procurement to M/s Vitol Asia Pte. Ltd., Singapore, as recommended by the Special Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SSCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the Long Term Contract for the importation of Diesel within a period of eight months from 2022-01-01 to 2022-08-31
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-25
decision_details_body: - Bids have been called from the bidders registered at the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) to award the Long Term Contract for the importation of 1,137,500 Bbls +10/- 5% of Diesel (0.05% MS) and 262,500 Bbls +10/- 5% of Diesel (0.001% MS) within a period of eight months from 2022‑01‑01 to 2022‑08‑31. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Energy to award the relevant procurement to M/s Vitol Asia Pte. Ltd., Singapore, as recommended by the Special Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SSCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Rapid completion of the North Central Maha Ela Project being constructed under the Mahaweli Water Security Investment Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-25
decision_details_body: - The 'Mahaweli Water Security Investment Porgramme' under the Ten Years Financing Facility of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) is being implemented as a major investment in the field of irrigated and drinking water under the Medium Term Development Approach of the Government. It has been planned to invest a sum of USD966 million for the project. Under the said project, the construction work of the North Central Maha Ela, North Western Maha Ela, Minipe Maha Ela and the water storage reservoirs of Meegahakirula and Mahakithula are being carried out to meet the acute drinking and irrigated water requirement in the Northern, North Central, North Western and Central Provinces. As such, it is expected to use the excess water stored in the Moragahakanda and Kaluganga reservoirs through the North Central Maha Ela Phase 1 and Phase 2 under construction, for 73,800 hectares of irrigated lands which are capable of cultivating the two seasons in the Northern and North Central provinces and to supply drinking water to 250,000 families. The construction activities which had been planned to be completed within 06 years, now have been planned to be completed within 04 years which is in 2025, as per the Government policy decision. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Irrigation to take necessary action to revise the relevant contract appropriately and accelerate the said construction, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement of Tyre Kits for the Sri Lanka Transport Board
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-25
decision_details_body: - Open Competitive Bids have been called for the procurement of 21,600 new Tyre Kits to meet the annual requirement of the Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB) and 02 bids have been received for the same. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport to award the relevant procurement to M/s CEAT Kelani International Tyres (Pvt) Ltd., the substantially responsive lowest bidder, as per the recommendation of the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining a Geographical Indication (GI) for 'Ceylon Tea'
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-25
decision_details_body: - In terms of the Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) Agreement, the indication which identifies a Good as originating in the territory of a member or a regional locality in the said territory is known as the Geographical Indication (GI),. A GI protects the relevant product against misuse or imitation of the registered name and safeguards consumers guaranteeing the true origin of the product to the consumer. Accordingly, the Agence Française de Développement (AFD) has agreed to provide technical assistance to the Sri Lanka Tea Board (SLTB) through the Centre de Coopération Internationale en Recherche Agronomique pour le Développement (CIRAD) and the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), to ease the registration process of GI for 'Ceylon Tea'. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Plantation to enter into a Tripartite Agreement between the Agence Française de Développement (AFD), Centre de Coopération Internationale en Recherche Agronomique pour le Développement (CIRAD) and the Sri Lanka Tea Board (SLTB), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of a Center for Containerized Cargo Inspection at Kerawalapitiya
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-25
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Customs carries out the containerized cargo inspection at 03 yards belonging to private sector located at Orugodawatta and Grandpass. Due to the limited space and facilities available in those yards, the Officers of the Department of Customs engaged in such activities as well as clients visiting the place are faced with hardships. Further, transportation of containers to those yards causes heavy traffic congestion in the Colombo area. Taking into consideration this situation, a Feasibility Study has been carried out with the technical assistance of the Asian Development Bank to identify the most appropriate place from among the alternative sites of Bloemendhal, Peliyagoda and Kerawalapitiya and accordingly, the block of land in extent of 19 acres and 9.26 perches located in close proximity to the Kerawalapitiya Interchange belonging to the Sri Lanka Land Development Corporation has been identified as the most appropriate place for the construction of the proposed Customs Verification Center. As such the proposal made by the Minister of Finance to take action to allocate the relevant block of land for the said purpose and to take action to establish the proposed Customs Verification Center, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Project for the construction of a Faculty of Medicine for the University of Moratuwa
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-25
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has previously been granted to establish a Faculty of Medicine for the University of Moratuwa and the Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development has agreed to grant funds required for the same. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Finance to enter into an Agreement to obtain Kuwait Dinars 10 million (approximately US$ 33.2 million) for the proposed Project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the SPMC Lotus Pharma Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-25
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet at its meeting held on 08 March 2021 has granted approval for the establishment of a Pharma Zone at Millewa, Horana and to appoint a Steering Committee to operate the activities pertaining to the implementation of the project, the approval of the Cabinet has been granted on 02 August 2021 to allocate a block of land in extent of 65 acres for the implementation of the said project. As such, the proposals made by the Minister of Health to take action to name the proposed Pharma Zone as 'SPMC Lotus Pharma Project' as per the recommendation of the Steering Committee appointed for the implementation of the said project and to select a suitable Consultancy Firm following the International Competitive Bidding Process for the same and to establish 03 factories to manufacture orthopedic and neurosurgical implants, anti-cancer medicines and oral solid dosage - general products by calling Expressions of Interest, were approved by the Cabinet.

description: Global Energy Compact for ''No New Coal'' Global Clean Power Transition Statement
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-25
decision_details_body: - The 26th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change has been scheduled to be held from 31st October 2021 to 12th November 2021 in Glasgow, Scotland in the United Kingdom. At this Conference, It is anticipated to review the implementation of the Convention on Climate Change, the Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement and to arrive at necessary decisions to further develop and implement those agreements. The United Kingdom that holds the Presidency of this Conference, in collaboration with the United Nations and several other member countries has planned to set up a “No New Coal Power Compact” to commit for a clean energy agenda. The signatories of the said Compact will abide to immediately cease the issuance of new permits for unabated coal-fired power generation projects and to cease new construction of unabated coal-fired power generation projects as of the end of the year. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Power to extend the support for the said Compact, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Transferring a Block of Land to Sri Lanka Institute of Biotechnology (Pvt) Ltd. in Homagama Pitipana area
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-25
decision_details_body: - The Urban Development Authority has acquired a block of land in extent of 220 from Mahenwatta area in Pitipana, Homagama for the implementation of development projects on science, technology and related activities. At present, blocks of land from the said land have been allocated for various projects and a block of land in extent of 13 acres has been allotted from the same land for the construction of a Biotechnology Innovation Park. Nevertheless, constructions of the said Park has not yet been commenced. Sri Lanka Institute of Biotechnology (Pvt.) Ltd. a fully government owned Institution, coming under the purview of the State Ministry of Digital Technology and Enterprise Development has planned to establish a Technology Innovation Park and accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Urban Development and Housing to have the above block of land allocated to that purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Demand, Consumption and Abundance of Food Crops in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-18
decision_details_body: - A Comparative Study Report has been prepared on the Demand, Consumption and Abundance of Food Crops in Sri Lanka with the intervention of the Presidential Task Force for Economic Revival and Poverty Alleviation and with the contribution of the Department of National Planning, Department of Census and Statistics and the Ministries, State Ministries and Departments relating to agriculture, livestock and fishery sections associated with food crops production, with a view to enhancing the productivity of local food production. The Presidential Task Force for Economic Revival and Poverty Alleviation has issued necessary instructions to the District and Divisional Agriculture Committees and Chairpersons of the Divisional Livelihood Committees, District Secretaries/ Government Agents and Divisional Secretaries to study this Report prepared including basic food categories such as paddy, grain including Legumes, vegetables, fruits, coconut cultivation, fishery and animal products and to prepare and implement an Action Plan including foods crops targets within the period of 2022-2024 as per the guidance of the said Report. Accordingly, the Minister of Finance informed the Cabinet of the said programme and the Cabinet granted its concurrence for the implementation of the said programme as scheduled.

description: Amendment to the Kandyan Marriage and Divorce Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-18
decision_details_body: - Section 22 of the Marriage Registration Ordinance has been amended by the Marriage Registration (Amendment) Act No. 12 of 1997 whereby marriage of minors requires the consent of parents accordingly. No party under the age of 18 could contract a valid marriage in Sri Lanka as per In Gunarathnam v Registrar General 2 Sri LR 302. Parental authority or consent to such marriage would be invalid in law. As per the said judgment, it is required to repeal the relevant sections of the laws that authorize the marriage of a minor with the consent of competent authority. Accordingly, action has already been taken to prepare a draft Bill to amend the Muslim Marriage and Divorce Act and the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to remove the relevant inconsistencies of the Kandyan Marriage and Divorce Act and to instruct the Legal Draftsman prepare a draft Bill for the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-18
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet at its meeting held on 2021‑07‑19 has granted approval to amend the Notaries Ordinance. In view of taking action in keeping with the said amendments, it has been found necessary to make a consequential amendment to the second section of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance and to amend the sections 4 and 7 therein as well. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to amend the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance and to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a draft Bill for the same , was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Penal Code consequential to the Prohibition of Obscene Publications
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-18
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet at its meeting held on 2021‑10‑05 has granted approval to submit the Obscene Publications Bill to Parliament and the clearance of the Attorney General has been received to the draft Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman to repeal section 285, 286 and 289A of the Penal Code in parallel to the introduction of the said new law. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to publish the said Bill in the Government Gazzette and to present the same thereafter in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance to enforce and 	regulate the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of 	Wild 	Fauna and Flora (CITES) in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-18
decision_details_body: - Sri lanka has signed the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora on 1979‑05‑04 as a member country of the said Convention. The Cabinet at its meeting held on 2016‑09‑06 has granted approval to amend the Fauna and Flora Protection Act No. 22 of 2009 to enable to enforce the provisions of the said Convention locally. Accordingly, the clearance of the Attorney General has been received to the amended Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Wildlife and Forest Conservation to publish the said Bill in the Government Gazzette and to present the same thereafter in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Urban Settlement Development Authority Act No. 36 of 2008
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-18
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted on 2019‑02‑05 to amend the Urban Settlement Development Authority Act No. 36 of 2008 enabling to properly execute the activities of the Urban Settlement Development Authority. Few more amendments to be made to the said Act have been later identified in order to maintain the activities of the said Authority in a more formal way. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development and Housing to amend the Urban Settlement Development Authority Act No. 36 of 2008 incorporating the said amendments and to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare an amended Bill for the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Banning Cattle Slaughter in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-18
decision_details_body:
- The Cabinet at its meeting held on 2020‑09‑28 has granted approval to ban cattle slaughter for enhancing local agriculture and local milk production and to amend the laws and regulations related thereto and the by-laws passed by Local Authorities pertaining to the cattle slaughtering. Accordingly, Legal Draftsman has prepared Bills to amend the following Acts/ Ordinances.

    • the Butchers Ordinance No. 9 of 1893 (Chapter 272)

    • the Animals Act No. 29 of 1958	

    • the Municipal Councils Ordinance (Chapter 252) 

    • the Urban Councils Ordinance (Chapter 255) 

    • the Pradeshiya Sabhas Act No. 15 of 1987

The Attorney General has confirmed that the above Bills are not inconsistent with the provisions of the Constitution. Accordingly, the joint proposal made by the Prime Minister; the Minister of Public 	Service, Provincial Council and Local Government and the Minister of Agriculture to publish the said Bills in the Government Gazette and submit the same thereafter in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Deployment of Ceylon Shipping Cooperation Limited Carrier Ships during the South-West Monsoon Period in 2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-18
decision_details_body: - Expressions of Interest (EoI) have been called from local and international 'Charterers' and 'Commercial Management Companies' to select a suitable Charterer to be deployed in the ships, Mv. Ceylon Breeze and Mv. Ceylon Princess owned by the Ceylon Shipping Corporation Ltd. (CSC)  during the South‑West Monsoon period in 2021/2022 (from mid April to mid September). Four (04) institutions have submitted their EoI for this procurement. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports & Shipping to award the Commercial Management Contract of both Mv. Ceylon Breeze and Mv. Ceylon Princess, to M/s Wallem Shipping (Singapore) Pvt. Ltd., as recommended by the Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Revision of the Policy of  permitting only one Heavy Industry of a kind in One Sea Port
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-18
decision_details_body: - The policy of permitting only one Heavy Industry of a kind in One Sea Port is in force. The Trincomalee Port Development Plan has been prepared to develop as a hub port in the Bay of Bengal Rim Region along with the accelerated economic growth in Bangladesh, East Coast of India, Myanmar and Sri Lanka. In planning the said Plan, matters such as natural location of the Trincomalee Port, the land in the extent of 2,000 acres closer to the Port belonging to the Ports Authority and the existing infrastructure facilities for the supply of services to the said Port have been taken into consideration. Further, with a view to developing the Port, it has been identified that it would be appropriate to provide opportunities to investors for establishing industries without imposing special limitations. Accordingly, in view of attracting investors showing an interest to commence Port related Heavy Industries, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports & Shipping to revise the existing policy of one Heavy Industry of a kind in One Sea Port, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of a Mixed Development Project in the Mahara Quarry land belonging to the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-18
decision_details_body: - The National Port Master Plan of the Sri Lanka Ports Authority has identified the urgent requirement of development of port logistics activities. Accordingly, the Ports Authority has planned to implement a port related logistics section in Bloemendal area. The official quarters of the Sri Lanka Ports Authority in Bloemendal area have to be set up on a suitable land, in the implementation of the said project. A block of land in the extent of 08 hectares in Mahara, Ragama belonging to the Sri Lanka Ports Authority has been maintained as a metal quarry during the period of construction of the Colombo Port and the said land is not being used for any productive purpose. Further, since  the said land is now filled with rain water, it has been identified as suitable to implement a water front development project. Accordingly, it has been planned to develop the said block of land as a Mixed Development Project with residential, urban, cultural, institutional and entertainment facilities. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports & Shipping to implement the said project as a Public‑Private Partnership Project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Re-construction of the Mahamodara Maternity Hospital
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-18
decision_details_body: - The Government of Sri Lanka and the KfW Bank of Germany have signed a Loan Agreement of Euro 28 million to finance the Mahamodara Maternity Hospital Project and an additional Loan Agreement has been entered into with the said Bank thereafter, to obtain a  Supplementary Loan of another Euro 13 million for the said project. The Government of Germany has agreed to convert the Supplementary Loan of Euro 13 million subsequently obtained, to a Grant, to enable to complete the activities of the project expeditiously. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Finance to authorize the Secretary to the Ministry of Finance to enter into the relevant Grant Agreement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of an Industrial Zone at Welipitiya Divisional Secretariat Division of Matara district
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-18
decision_details_body: - In view of promoting regional level manufacturing industries, the Ministry of Industries implements the Regional Industrial Estate Development Program. It has been planned to establish a new development zone in a block of land in extent of 200 acres in the core of Charley Mount Estate/Hallalawatta in the Welipitiya Divisional Secretariat Division, focusing on the industries in Matara district parallel to the recently implemented infrastructure development projects in the Southern Province. Accordingly, taking into consideration a proposal made by the Minister of Industries, approval of the Cabinet was granted in principle to implement the said project and pursue action to allocate the blocks of land required for the said project and the identified priority projects for the development of the area as well, from the blocks of land in the relevant estate belonging to the Land Reform Commission that cannot be used for economically effective cultivation.

description: Completion of the construction of the partly built Ward Complex at the Provincial General Hospital, Kurunegala
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-18
decision_details_body: - The Provincial General Hospital of Kurunegala consists of 2,355 beds, 57 wards and 28 specialized units. Even though it had been planned to construct a five‑storey building in phased out manner to establish the new wards during the period of 2007‑2009 as per the development plan of the said Hospital, it is only up to the second floor has been completed out of the said construction. In accordance with the Last Will of late Mrs. Eileen De Mel, funds have been left to construct a ward or wing of the Kurunegala Hospital and the party appointed on behalf of her estate has agreed to have the construction of the said five‑storey building completed. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to enter into an Agreement with the party appointed on behalf of estate of late Mrs. Eileen De Mel, to implement and complete the Project within 02 years as per the said agreement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Program on Budget Debate for the Financial Year 2022
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-11
decision_details_body:
- Cabinet noted the following matters submitted by the Hon. Prime Minister to the effect that arrangements have been made to conduct the Program on Budget Debate pertaining to the financial year 2022 as follows.

*	to commence the Budget Debate after the submission of budget proposals on 2021‑11‑12 and continue the said Debate up to 2021‑11‑22.

*	to commence the Committee Stage Debate of the Budget on 2021‑11‑23 and continue the same up to 2021‑12‑10.

*	to conduct the Vote on Third Reading Stage on 2021‑12‑10 at 5.00 p.m.

description: Amending the Civil Procedure Code (Chapter 101)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-11
decision_details_body: - The Civil Law Reforms Sub‑Committee appointed by the Minister of Justice has recommended the necessity of amending the existing provisions on issue and service of Summons and attention has been paid to the requirement of using commonly used communication methods at present such as E-mail and SMS, to serve Summons to the parties to a case. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to formulate an amending Bill incorporating the amendments recommended by the said Committee, to amend the Civil Procedure Code (Chapter 101), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Legalizing the Minimum Age of Retirement for the Private Sector Employees
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-11
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet was granted at its meeting held on 2021‑03‑23 to draft a Bill to revise the existing age limit of retirement for the Private Sector employees. As such, the drafted preliminary Bill was taken up for further discussion at the meeting of the Committee for the study of policy and legal matters affecting the apparel industry and trade sector appointed under the patronage of the Hon. Prime Minister with the participation of all the relevant stakeholders. As such, up on the consensus reached at the meeting of the said Committee, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour to submit the Minimum Retirement Age of Workers in the Private Sector Bill drafted by the Legal Draftsman, incorporating the provisions enabling to extend the age of retirement of workers who have not reached 52 years on the effective date of the proposed Act up to 60 years and to employ the workers of 52 years or above on the effective date of the Act, up to the maximum of 59 years under three categories in terms of their age, in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Formulation of legislation on Cyber Security
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-11
decision_details_body:
- (a) 	Drafting of an Act titled as Defence Cyber Command Act -

With the development of electronic communication, terrorist groups and criminals have been likely to use cyber space and electronic communication for terrorist activities, organized crimes and anti‑social activities. It has been recognized that the electronic communication through the cyber space is a factor which may directly influence the national security. Hence, there is a stringent need of formulating new legislation covering every field for ensuring the national security, incorporating the provisions required for formal and efficient performance of operations conducted by the Cyber Security Units established by the Tri‑Forces, Police and other agencies at their institutional levels.

(b) 	Formulation of a Bill for enactment of Cyber Security laws ‑ 

The Ministry of Technology has been vested with the responsibility of cyber security and establishing an institutional structure for the purpose. As such, it has been decided appropriate to formulate a separate Bill as indicated under (a) above, including the provisions on cyber security pertaining to the field of defence, subsequent to the discussions held among the Ministry of Defence, the Ministry of Technology and other relevant stakeholders on the draft Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman. The need of introducing new laws has arisen to achieve the objectives of designing a regulation framework, for the implementation of the National Information and Cyber Security Strategy, providing provisions for the establishment of the Cyber Security Agency of Sri Lanka to associate with the other supporting institutions for the purpose, introducing the legal requirements for the protection of critical information infrastructure within the country, preventing the insecure activities on cyber security and creating a formal cyber security environment within the country, apart from the matters pertaining to the national security.

As such, taking into consideration the proposals made by H. E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence and Minister of Technology, approval of the Cabinet was granted to draft two bills as mentioned above.

description: Submission of a suitable methodology for the specific determination and identification of National Heritage in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-11
decision_details_body: - Cabinet, having considered the issues arisen due to the absence of criteria or a mechanism for the specific identification of National Heritage in Sri Lanka, granted approval on 2021‑11‑16 to appoint a Committee comprising the experts/scholars in the relevant subject fields, to seek views of the public and formulate a mechanism for the identification of tangible and intangible national heritage which establishes the Sri Lankan cultural identity. The Committee has submitted its Report as per the said decision and it has been pointed out by the Report the necessity of establishing a central independent institutional structure for the proper management of the activities such as identification, documentation, declaration, curation, monitoring and acquisition of national heritage belonging to Sri Lankans and conducting researches thereon. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious & Cultural Affairs to pursue action as per the recommendations of the said Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Smart Sri Lanka Initiative - Digitalization, Blockchain Technology, Cryptocurrency mining and providing required services to Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-05
decision_details_body: - Developing an integrated system including Digitalization, Blockchain Technology, Cryptocurrency mining and provision of other required services has been identified to facilitate the creation of a digital business ecosystem. Many other countries in South Asia have already initiated measures to evaluate and develop related fields expeditious attention should be focused to competent with such countries. Accordingly, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Development Co-ordination and Monitoring to appoint a committee comprising of professionals in both Government and private sector to submit information to the Cabinet on the possible regulations, acts and laws to attract investors engaged in those fields, and to take necessary action to permit Cryptocurrency mining companies to invest in Sri Lanka, subject to the provisions of the Act No.4 of 1978 and its subsequent amendments.

description: Prohibition of Obscene Publication Bill
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-05
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2020‑09‑21 to draft a bill to introduce a new law to take action with regard to the obscene publications produced through information technology and other means. Accordingly, the clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the draft bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice, to submit the said Bill in the Government Gazette, and thereafter present the same in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Partition Act Law
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-05
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by the Minister of Justice to amend the existing Partition Act Law, based on the recommendations of the Advisory Committee on Partition Act Law appointed by the Minister of Justice to submit recommendations on the Partition Act Law to amend the Partition Act to meet the present day requirements by preserving the rights of the co-owners of a land and also preventing undue delays and to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft legislation for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entry of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation into Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) Business
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-05
decision_details_body: - The Sapugaskanda refinery of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) produces around 70 to 90 Metric tons of LP gas per day which is approximately 5% of petroleum demand of the country. A feasibility study is being conducted to establish a new refinery with the capacity of 100,000 barrels per day as well as to upgrade the existing refinery. Further, plans are also being designed to expeditiously implement such projects. The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation has found the significance of entering a third competitor into the LPG market. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Energy to establish a subsidiary company under the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation so that LPG business could be commenced using the refinery production, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of a Higher Education Research and Training Institute as “Sri Lanka Charted Institute of Journalists”
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-05
decision_details_body: - The need has been found to establish an institute with the state sponsorship to ensure the growth and international standards of the media education sector, having found the issues in the media sector. There are a considerable number of students undergoing media education within the school system, in particular. However, sufficient number of higher educational institutes have not yet been established to cater their necessity. Although there are few mass communication degree programmes conducted within universities, it has been observed that, such courses do not provide sufficient practical and technological knowledge to create a professional journalist. Therefore, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Mass Media to establish a Higher Education Research and Training Institute as “Sri Lanka Charted Institute of Journalists to make available educational opportunities from courses of certificate level to degree and post graduate degree level on mass media, with the objective of providing opportunity to the media personnel already engaged in the service, media managers and school students who intend to enter the field to study the field of mass media, to obtain required practical training as well as to enhance professionalism through capacity development and aiming to create journalists needed to create a media culture with moral autonomy.

description: Constructing Smart Class Rooms and Modern Computer Labs for 200 Schools in Galle District with the assistance of the Republic of India
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-05
decision_details_body: - Having found the timely requirement of granting children a fair access to qualitative education opportunities mixed with modern technological aspects in order to minimize the gaps of digital technology, the Government of India has agreed to grant a financial assistance of Rs.300 million to construct Smart Class Rooms and Modern Computer Labs for 200 Schools in Galle District as stated in the Memorandum of Understanding on 'High Impact Community Development Projects'. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to sign the a Memorandum of Understanding between the Republic of India and the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka to obtain the said grant assistance, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Identifying as a Strategic Development Project, the Project to develop software and to provide IT related services for Export Market - HCL Technologies Lanka (Pvt.) Limited
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-05
decision_details_body: - HCL Technologies Lanka (Pvt.) Limited is a fully owned subsidiary of HCL Technologies in India. The said Company has signed an agreement with the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka (BOI) on 08‑01‑2020 to implement a project for software development and provide information technology related services with an investment of US$ 10.5 million, creating employment opportunities for 2,450 Sri Lankans and 1,050 foreigners. The commercial operations of the Project have commenced on 2020‑10‑29. The said Company has made a request to identify the relevant project which falls under the Strategic Development Projects Act and the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka has agreed with the said request. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Economic Policies & Plan Implementation to identify the above project that has been commenced by HCL Technologies Lanka (Pvt.) Limited, as a project under the Strategic Development Projects Act, No.14 of 2008, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Acquisition of lands to the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka (TRCSL) for the Colombo Lotus Tower Project Complex
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-05
decision_details_body: - The construction activities of the Lotus Tower project are near full completion by now and necessary action is being taken by the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka (TRCSL) to plan its commercial and operational activities. It has been identified that the development activities should be further carried out such as construction of a state‑of‑the‑art water show on Beira Lake closer to the Lotus Tower to attract local and foreign spectators (visitors), setting up food outlets, construction of offices, accommodation and infrastructure facilities in the premises for the staff members expected to be employed in the said Tower and further expansion of the car park that has already been planned. Accordingly, the proposal made by H. E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Technology to vest the block of land of 4 acres 3 roods 24.47 perches in extent located in the proximity of the project premises, belonging to the Urban Development Authority (UDA), with the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka for carrying out the said development activities, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The 'Gamata Sanniwedanaya' (Connect Sri Lanka) National Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-05
decision_details_body: - The 'Gamata Sanniwedanaya' (Connect Sri Lanka) Project launched by the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka (TRCSL) in 2019, has conducted a survey on the lack of broadband connectivity covering 14,000 Grama Niladhari Divisions in the 25 districts. The project that has been initiated by the said Commission, based on its outcome, in association with the Telecommunication Service providers to cover Ratnapura district with broadband connectivity is to be completed in October, 2021. The Government has already planned to expand the said project as a national project, enabling to cover the entire island with broadband internet facilities by improving the infrastructure facilities required for digitalization. It is expected to secure the funds required for the purpose from the Telecommunication Development Fund. As such, the proposal made by H. E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Technology to implement the said Project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Memorandum of Understanding between the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University and the Massey University of New Zealand
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-05
decision_details_body: - A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) has been signed between the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University and the Massey University of New Zealand on 12th August 2012, for a period of five (05) years, for mutual co‑operation between the two parties in the field of Higher Education. Necessary action has not been taken to extend the said MoU at expiration of the said period. As per the discussions held between the two parties, it has been agreed to extend the said MoU for a period of five (05) years with effect from 21st August 2021. Accordingly, the proposal made by H. E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence to sign the said MoU, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Exploitation of Geological Resources for Development Priorities
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-10-05
decision_details_body: - The Presidential Task Force on Geological Resources has been established with the objectives of assessing the quantities of metal, sand, earth, gravel and clay required for the development projects of the Government within the next five years, identifying the methodologies of supplying of geological resources for the said projects, simplifying the licensing process adapted in the use of geological resources required for the other projects in the field of construction and smallish economic livelihoods and identifying the lands to be used for different development activities. The said Task Force, in its preliminary report, has submitted the recommendations for easing the mining licensing procedure to the public and clients in obtaining metal, sand, earth/gravel and clay required for the construction industry. As such, the proposal made by H. E. the President, taking into consideration the said recommendations to issue a circular containing the necessary orders to all Heads of Institutions connected with the procedure to ease the relevant procedure and to issue a manual on the mechanisms to be adapted by the Public Institutions in issuing licenses on mining, transportation and trading of minerals used in the construction industry, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Civil Procedure Code (Chapter 101)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - Although new provisions have been introduced to the Civil Procedure Code on the ''Pre-Trial Process'' by the Civil Procedure Code (Amendment) Act, No.8 of 2017 in order to expedite legal proceedings and reduce the time consumed in adjudication, in 2017, objectives anticipated by such amendments have not been achieved. Therefore, it has been identified that further amendments are needed to be made to the ''Pre-Trial Process'' enabling to achieve the expected outcome. Accordingly, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to amend the Civil Procedure Code as recommended by the Committee appointed by the Minister of Justice to study matters relating to the Pre‑trial and establishment of Small Claims Courts and submit recommendations and thereafter get drafted the bill for the purpose by the Legal Draftsman.

description: Shortage of Rice in the Market
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - Attention of the Cabinet was drawn to the existing shortage of rice in the domestic market. Considering the prevailing situation, cabinet decided to import 100,000 MT of rice immediately, enabling to supply the consumers with adequate quantities of rice without a shortage and to maintain a buffer stock of rice with the Government. It was also decided to cancel the existing maximum price limits of rice with immediate effect.

description: Amendment to the Rent Act No.7 of 1972
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - Although the Rent Act No.7 of 1972 was introduced to ensure the housing requirements of the needy people and to protect poor tenants, provisions of the said Act have gone outdated at present causing adverse impacts to the housing sector, rented complexes as well as such property transactions. Therefore, it has been identified that the aforesaid Act needs to be amended to cater to the present day requirements. An interim report on the Amendment of the Rent Act has been submitted by the Rent Law Advisory Committee. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to amend the Rent Act by including the amendments proposed by the aforesaid Committee, and to advise Legal Draftsman to draft amending legislation for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Recovery of Possession of the Premises Given on Lease (Special Provisions) Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - Considering the key areas such as renting out a premises, development of the premises given on rent basis and its impact on the economy of the country in general, the Rent Law Advisory Committee, appointed by the Minister of Justice has prepared an initial draft for the enactment of laws for the recovery of possession of the premises given on lease, expeditiously. The enactment of new law would prevent the prolonged delays of law in the cases related to ordinary rent and and ejectment action under regular procedure and grant relief to the lessor within a very short period. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to instruct the Legal Draftsman, to draft legislation for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No.15 of 1979
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2020‑09‑28 to amend the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No.15 of 1979 to make new provisions to Section 144A to set down a procedure which does not require a suspect or an accused person to be produced in person before the Magistrate for the purpose of the extension of an order relating to the committal to remand custody and to Section 241A to set down a procedure which does not require the accused in respect of whom a trial is pending or has commenced in the High Court to be produced in person before the High Court Judge, provided special circumstances at present. Accordingly, the relevant Bill has been drafted by the Legal Draftsman and clearance of the Attorney General has also been received for the same. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to publish the said Bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter present the same in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Civil Procedure Code (Chapter 101)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - With the introduction of a special procedure of the Small Claims Courts, a consequential amendment is required to be made to repeal Chapter LXVI of the Civil Procedure Code which makes provisions for the purpose. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to amend the Civil Procedure Code and to instruct the Legal Draftsman draft legislation for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the High Court of the Provinces (Special Provinces) Act, No.19 of 1990
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2021‑06‑14 to draft a new law to make provisions for special procedure of Small Claims Courts and to amend the Judicature Act No.2 of 1978 in order to establish a Small Claims Courts. The need has been identified to amend Section 5 (A) of the said Act to include the Small Claims Courts in the list of Primary Courts mentioned in the High Court of the Provinces (Special Provinces) Act, No. 19 of 1990 in order to be able to comply with the new law and the proposed amendment. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft legislation to amend the said Act, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending Hazardous Occupations Regulations under the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act No.47 of 1956
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act No.47 of 1956 was introduced to regulate the employment of women, young persons and children and to ensure their job security. The minimum age for employment of children has been raised to 16 years from January 2021. The Minister of Labour has issued a Hazardous Occupations Order in accordance with the amendments made to the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act No. 24 of 2006 following the ratification of the International Labour Organization (ILO) Minimum Age Convention by Sri Lanka. Accordingly, 51 hazardous jobs have been introduced for young people between the ages of 16-18 and employing them in such jobs has been declared a punishable offense by law. The orders, which was introduced about 10 years ago, has been further reviewed and identified 20 new periodically hazardous jobs, including domestic service, beauty culture and jobs related to computers and electronics. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour to publish the regulations made by the Legal Draftsman having expanded the list of hazardous jobs up to 71, in the Government Gazette and thereafter present the amended regulations in Parliament, for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Production and supply of organic fertilizer and natural minerals and chelated micro-elements
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2021‑05‑31 to import organic fertilizer and natural minerals and chelated plant micro-elements for the Maha season 2021/2022. Accordingly, arrangements have been made to import organic fertilizer required for paddy cultivation by the State Fertilizer Companies and to supply stocks of organic fertilizer required for other crops by licensed fertilizer companies at competitive prices. Accordingly, Cabinet approved the proposal made by Minister of Agriculture to import the stocks of organic fertilizer required for other crops by the two State Fertilizer Companies, enabling to supply organic fertilizer required for other crops at competitive prices, without any delay.

description: Submission of the Appropriation Bill for the Financial Year 2022 in Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2021‑07‑26 to draft the Appropriation Bill for the year 2022. The clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the bill drafted accordingly by the Legal Draftsman. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Finance to publish the said bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter present the same in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Attracting Airlines to the Mattala Rajapaksa International Airport (MRIA) to commence Scheduled Operations
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Tourism to complete waiver of the embarkation levy for a period of two (02) years from the date of commencement of operations by international airlines and to offer discounts of landing and parking for the period of next four (04) years, with the objective of promoting the operations of the Mattala Rajapaksha International Airport (MRIA).

description: Allocating the land called Weheragoda Watte located in Weeraketiya Divisional Secretariat Division in the Hambantota District to Sri Jinarathana Educational Institute for Agricultural Vocational Trainings, on lease basis
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - The land called Weheragoda Watte of 131 acres 2 roods and 29 perches in extent located in the Weeraketiya Divisional Secretariat Division of Hambantota District has been vested with the Land Reform Commission. The Board of Management of Sri Jinarathana Educational Institute has made a request to grant the above land which contains a barren coconut plantation with no proper maintenance to be utilized for agricultural vocational trainings. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Lands to grant the above land to the Board of Management of Sri Jinarathana Educational Institute, on lease basis for a period of 30 years, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Allocation of block of lands from Regional Industrial Estates for the establishment of Industries
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - Regional Industrial Estates Development Programme is a main programme implemented with the objective of promoting industries at regional level. Selection of investors for the above purpose is carried out following a full assessment of project proposals by ‘Regional industrial Services Committee’ established under the Industries Promotion Act No. 40 of 1990 and the ‘Project Evaluation Committee of the Ministry’ appointed by the Secretary, Ministry of Industries. Accordingly, the above Committees having examined 24 project proposals, has recommended to allocate blocks of land from 10 Industrial estates for the implementation of those projects. The proposal made by the Minister of Industries to allocate land blocks to the relevant investors on long - term lease basis of 35 years, as per the recommendations of the above Committees, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Removing sand, soil and organic materials deposited in small/medium size tanks for the enhancement of water retention capacity
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - A programme for rehabilitating 5000 irrigated tanks and anicuts is being implemented to strengthen the rural agricultural economy. It is a prime request of farmers engaged in farming activities using these tanks to increase the capacity of the said tanks by excavating those filled due to prolonged soil erosion, growth of aquatic plants and weeds, and decaying the same. For the said purpose, the sediment deposited in those tanks should be removed and transported and there is a possibility of using sediment so removed as row materials in the industries such as pottery, sand extraction, production of organic fertilizer and road development. Therefore, Government has space to increase the water retention capacity of those tanks without being any burden to the Government whereby the Government could gain an income as well, by allowing entrepreneurs who use such row materials to remove those under certain restrictions. It has been planned to obtain the service of the National Equipment and Machinery Organization, State Development and Construction Corporation, Central Engineering Services (Pvt.) Ltd and Maganaguma Institution, since technical staff in the Department of Agrarian Development is not adequate for this purpose. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Irrigation to obtain the contribution of the private sector to remove the materials deposited in the tanks as beneficial to the Government and in conformity with the proper standards under the supervision of the Department of Agrarian Development and take necessary action to clean the bottoms of 2,000 tanks within the period of next three years and increase their capacities, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Performing Cardiac Surgery for children with heart diseases 	through the Amrita Institute of Medical Sciences (Amrita 	Hospital), 	Kochi, India
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - Approximately 3,000 children are born with heart diseases every year and 1,500 – 2,000 out of them require surgical treatment. Although, such children are directed to the Lady Ridgeway Hospital in Colombo from most of the hospitals in the country, the said hospital could only perform nearly 900 surgeries per year according to the facilities available with that hospital. Therefore, until necessary actions are taken to provide adequate facilities for operating theatres and cardiac emergency treatments under the 'Little Hearts' project which is in operation at present, the Rotary International District 3201, India and the Rotary Club of Colombo West, RID 3220 have agreed to implement a project at the Amrita Institute of Medical Sciences located in Kochi, India under Rotary funds for a period of two years to facilitate performing serious Cardiac surgeries for children with a view to relieving the congestion associated with Cardiac surgeries. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to sign a Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Health, Rotary International District 3201, India and the Rotary Club of Colombo West, RID 3220 to implement the relevant programme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of a Board of Trustees for the maintenance and administrative activities of Sandahiru Seya Stupa
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - The Sandahiru Seya Stupa, 282 feet and 6 inches in height, is being erected in Anuradapura sacred area under the overall supervision of the Ministry of Defence in commemoration of war heroes and civilians who sacrificed their lives to end terrorism which prevailed over 30 years and to invoke merit for them. As such, the proposal made by H.E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence to appoint a Board of Trustees for the maintenance and administrative activities of this Stupa, after completing its constructions and to establish a charitable trust to accumulate and maintain the donations made by local and foreign devotees for the Stupa, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Agreement entered into between the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Government of Bahrain on Mutual Visa Exemption for holders of Diplomatic, Special and Official Passports
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-27
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet at its meeting held on 2019‑05‑07 has granted approval to enter into an Agreement between the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Government of Bahrain on Mutual Visa Exemption for holders of Diplomatic, Special and Official Passports. Nevertheless, the relevant Agreement could not be signed within the due time frame. Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence to enter into the relevant Agreement between the two countries, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendments to the Appropriation Act No. 07 of 2020
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-21
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted by the Appropriation Act No. 7 of 2020 for a borrowing limit of Rs. 2,997 billion for the year 2021. Nevertheless, the borrowing limit approved for the year 2021 had to be increased due to the reasons such as decrease of the government revenue due to the situation that has arisen in the wake of COVID - 19 pandemic, expenses in the health sector and ensuring the social security of those who lost their income, that additional provisions had to be made for the payment of salaries and other expenses of the institutions of which those had been paid by their own income and the increase of expenses in other several areas. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Finance to revise the borrowing limit of Rs. 2,997 billion approved by the Appropriation Act No. 7 of 2020, to Rs. 3,397 billion by Rs. 400 billion and to take necessary action to amend the said Appropriation Bill for the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: ''Hope for Youth'' - National Youth Development Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-21
decision_details_body: - The total youth population in Sri Lanka between the ages of 15-29 is 23.2% and it is approximately 5.6 million in numbers. A National Youth Development Programme called as Hope for Youth has been scheduled to be implemented by the Ministry of Youth and Sports, enabling to address the challengers encountered by youths and their expectations with a view to attracting youths actively to the development process of the country. The prime objective of this programme is to reduce the unemployment of youth which prevails 28% at present to 12%. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Youth and Sports to implement the 'Hope for Youth' programme from 2021 onwards instead of Yovunpuraya programme which was implemented up to 2019, through the National Youth Services Council targeting each Divisional Secretariat Divisions, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Transfer of the ownership of the land belonging to the Sri Lanka Ports Authority located at Aluth Mawatha, Colombo 15 to the Ceylon Shipping Corporation Limited (CSC)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-21
decision_details_body: - Ceylon Shipping Corporation Limited, in the year 1979 has purchased a plot of land located at 18th lane, Aluth Mawatha, Colombo 15, belonging to the Sri Lanka Ports Authority, having paid the then estimated value of the land to the Port Commission. In the year 1982, at the expense of the Ceylon Shipping Corporation, 05 apartments were constructed in the said land and out of which 03 apartments have been used by the Sri Lanka Ports Authority whereas remaining 02 apartments have been used by the Ceylon Shipping Corporation. Although Ceylon Shipping Corporation Limited had paid the government estimated value for the said land, the possession of the said land has not been legally transferred. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports and Shipping to transfer the said plot of land of 29.53 perches to Ceylon Shipping Corporation limited, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Galle Port Development Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-21
decision_details_body: - Development of Galle port has been found vital on the theme “tourist destination and safe haven” so as to maintain it as a regional commercial port. Accordingly, the Ministry of Ports and Shipping has planned to implement a project to develop Galle port under public-private partnership, without restricting traditional port services but attracting investments from the private sector. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports and Shipping to take necessary action to implement the said project as proposed, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of an Action Plan for the years 2022-2024 under the Memorandum of Understanding for the Agricultural Development Cooperation between Sri Lanka and Vietnam
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-21
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka and Vietnam have entered into a Memorandum of Understanding in 2006, in order to promote mutual cooperation in the field of agriculture. In terms of the provisions of the said agreement, the International Cooperation Department of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Department of Vietnam and Sri Lanka Council for Agricultural Research Policy should formulate an action plan on the concurrence of both parties and implement the same. Accordingly, action plans have been formulated and implemented for the years 2010-2011 and 2017-2019. Taking into consideration the importance of agricultural cooperation between the two countries, a new action plan has also been formulated for the year 2022-2024, on mutual consultation of both parties. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, to implement the said action plan and to sign for the said agreement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Management of recyclable waste generated from agricultural inputs in the North Central Province
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-21
decision_details_body: - Many of the packagings used for agricultural inputs are made of polyethylene terephthalate, glass, high-density polyethylene and polypropylene. Haphazard disposal of these into environment and burning such things on farmlands and in households have caused environmental pollution and therefore a programme had been organized by the Ministry of Environment to recycle them in a proper manner. In the first instance, it has been planned to implement the proposed programme as a pilot project in the North Central Province in collaboration with the farmer organizations, Regional Offices of the Department of Irrigation and the Divisional Management Offices of Sri Lanka Mahaweli Authority by further expanding the programme to collect and recycle discarded empty containers (plastic and glass), which is being implemented since 2016 by the Central Environmental Authority, the Office of the Registrar of Pesticides and Croplife-Sri Lanka Private Limited under the guidance of the Ministry of Environment. Measures have been taken to secure provisions under the Food Security and Climate Change Mitigation Assistance Programme of the World Health Organization for the purpose. Accordingly, the Cabinet approved the joint proposal made by the Minister of Environment and the Minister of Agriculture to declare the second week of March of each Yala season and the third week of September of each Maha season commencing from the year 2022, as empty plastic and glass container collection weeks under the said programme and to implement the said programme with the assistance of the Officers in the field of Agriculture and farmer organizations.

description: Implementing Four (04) Projects on Pollution Control
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-21
decision_details_body: - The Institutions and organizations such as the Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation - NORAD, Specific International Programme belonging to Minamata Convention, the United Nations Environmental Development Programme (UNDP), the Government of Switzerland and the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) have agreed to provide funds required for the implementation of four (04) projects in the field of environmental pollution and chemical management, in the year 2021 as two project proposals for plastic waste management covered by the Basel Convention and as two project proposals for making guidelines and awareness pertaining to the mercury management covered by Minamata Convention. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to implement the said projects and to enter into the relevant Agreements, for the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining an Additional Loan of US$ 100 million under the COVID - 19 Strategic Preparedness and Response Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-21
decision_details_body: - The National Task Force for COVID - 19 Management has decided to expand the initial target of vaccinating 60% of the population in Sri Lanka as outlined in the National Deployment and Vaccination Plan for Covid -19. The World Bank has agreed to grant an additional loan of US$ 100 million for the Sri Lanka COVID-19 Emergency Response and Health Systems Preparedness Project under the COVID-19 Strategic Preparedness and Response Programme (SPRP). It has been planned to use the said additional loan for the purchase of 14 million doses of Pfizer vaccine and for financing other expenditure pertaining to the vaccination task. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to obtain the relevant additional financing facility, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Programme for stabilizing prices of essential consumer goods by creating competitiveness in the market through the Forward 	Exchange Agreement
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-21
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet at its meeting held on 2021‑04‑27 has granted approval to implement a programme of purchasing essential consumer goods to Lanka Sathosa Limited at fixed prices under the Forward Exchange Agreements. Under the said programme, agreement will be reached with the selected suppliers through the Forward Exchange Agreements for a period of three months. Expression of Interest has been invited from the suppliers having published notices with a view to implementing the third phase of the above programme within the period of next three months. Accordingly, the Cabinet decided grant its concurrence for the matters submitted by the Minister of Trade on actions intended to be taken for the implementation of the relevant programme along with the selected suppliers from the Expression of Interest so received.

description: Implementation of ''Colombo Bird Park'' Project, Madiwela, Sri 	Jayawadenepura
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-21
decision_details_body: - Proposals have been invited under the Competitive Procurement Procedure to implement a Bird Park Project and related infrastructural facilities on Design, Construction, Financing, Operate basis at a block of land in extent of 37 acres 01 rood and 20.44 perch located at Madiwela, Sri Jayawadenepura belonging to the Urban Development Authority. The Standing Cabinet Appointed Negotiating Committee has recommended the proposal submitted by Colombo Bird Park (Pvt) Ltd. and approval of the Board of Management of Urban Development Authority has been received for the same. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development and Housing to lease out the the relevant block of land to Colombo Bird Park (Pvt) Ltd. for a period of 30 years, was approved by the Cabinet.
