description: Paddy Purchasing Programme in the Yala Season - 2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-13
decision_details_body: - Paddy harvesting in the Yala Season ‑ 2021 has been commenced by now and the Cabinet decided to take action to purchase Nadu paddy at Rs.55/- per kg by the Paddy Marketing Board with a view to purchasing paddy harvest of the farmers at a competitive price and to convert the stocks of paddy so purchased to rice and sell to the consumers at a reasonable price through the outlet network of Lanka Sathosa Limited.

description: Establishment of Diplomatic Relations with Timor-Leste (East Timor)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-13
decision_details_body: - The Government of Timor-Leste (East Timor) has conveyed its consent to formally establish diplomatic relations with Sri Lanka. A number of Asian countries including India, China, Japan and South Korea have built up diplomatic relations with the said country at present. Establishing diplomatic relations with the Timor-Leste would be significant in economic and political fronts as well as Sri Lanka's intervention in international platforms to receive its support. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Foreign Minister to develop formal diplomatic relations with that country, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of Elevated Expressway from New Kelani Bridge to Athurugiriy Interchange of Outer Circular Expressway Via Rajagiriya - Obtaining Consultancy Services for Monitoring the Construction and Maintenance
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-13
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet at its meeting held on 2021‑05‑24, has granted approval to award the contract for constructing the above Expressway on Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) basis, to the M/s China Harbour Engineering Corporation. Accordingly, the relevant Expressway is to be constructed within 03 years. An independent Engineer is required to be appointed for monitoring the constructions and maintenance to ensure the standard of the proposed Expressway and completion of the constructions within the stipulated time frame. The Road Development Authority should function as the Employer of the said consultancy company. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Highways to take necessary action to select a suitable Institution for the same, following the formal procurement process, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Civil Procedure Code (Chapter 101)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-13
decision_details_body: - The Civil Law Reforms Sub-Committee appointed by the Minister of Justice has recommended that it would be appropriate to introduce to the Civil Procedure Code (Chapter 101), that it shall not be necessary to adduce formal proof of the execution or genuineness of any deed or document not being a will, which is attested and which on the face of it appears to be duly attested unless in the pleadings or further pleadings the execution or the genuineness thereof is specifically impeached and raised as an issue, or unless the Court requires such proof. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to introduce necessary amendment for the Civil Procedure Code to provide for the said purpose and to prepare draft Bill for the same by the Legal Draftsman, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to Section 88(2) of the Civil Procedure Code
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-13
decision_details_body: - The Civil Procedure Code includes provisions pertaining to set aside the judgment given by a court of law upon a request made by a defendant to the court of law with notice to the plaintiff stating that he has reasonable grounds for such default, within 14 days of the decree entered against him for default. It has been observed that by taking advantage of these provisions, it has enabled the defendant to employ delaying tactics and to resist a just claim of the plaintiff. Therefore, the approval of the Cabinet has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2021‑02‑01 to amend the section 88(2) of the Civil Procedure Code, enabling to prevent such adverse conditions. Accordingly, the Attorney General has assured that the draft Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman is in conformity with the provisions of the Constitution. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to present the said Bill in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of a mechanism for the utilization of currently identified and untapped minerals
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-13
decision_details_body:
- Of the currently identified mineral resources in the country, economically valuable minerals are divided under four main categories as follows;

    • Energy Minerals
    • Ferrous & Ferro alloy Group minerals
    • Non-Ferrous Group
    • Non-Metallic Group Minerals
Mining, refining and exporting of minerals such as Ilmenite, Zircon, Rutile and Graphite are carried out by the Ceylon Mineral Sands Company and Kahatagaha Granite Lanka Limited at present and the Gem and Jewellery Authority and Gem and the Jewellery Research Centre involve in gem and jewellery related works. It has been observed that no adequate Government's intervention has been made to utilize the currently identified minerals apart from those mentioned above. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries to appoint Committee comprising of the experts in the field to conduct a detailed study on the areas where the said minerals reserves are located, quantities thereof and the products that can be made utilizing them with a view to launching a programme to utilize the said minerals economically valuable purposes and to implement the relevant programme as per the recommendations of the said Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Declaration of the Policy Objective of Renewable Energy Development
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-13
decision_details_body: - In accordance with the National Policy Framework, “Vistas of Prosperity and Splendour”, it has been focused on getting the maximum of the electricity demand in the country through the renewable energy sources by 2030 and accordingly, the Government has taken a policy decision to pursue necessary action to meet 70% of the total electricity demand of the country from the renewable energy by 2030 and to reach Carbon Neutrality in electricity generation by the year 2050. The Ceylon Electricity Board should prepare 'Least Cost, Long Term Generation Plan' within the said policy framework as per the Electricity Act No. 20 of 2009 and Amendments related thereto. The Minister of Power should submit General Policy Guidelines to the Ceylon Electricity Board to prepare the said Generation Plan in terms of the provisions of section (5) of the said Act. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Power to issue the relevant guidelines, was approved by the Cabinet.

description:
Measuring and Developing the Character Strengths of Wisdom:
Research Project on new approaches in Sri Lanka and Philippines
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-13
decision_details_body: - It has been proposed to implement a Joint Research Project on new approaches in Sri Lanka and the Philippines pertaining to measuring and developing the character strengths of wisdom. The aforesaid Research Project has been planned to be implemented by the University of Colombo and the De La Selle University in Philippines, Waterloo University in Canada and Wake Forest University in America. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to implement the said Research Project and to enter into Agreements with the relevant Universities for the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Increasing the number of “Nenasa” Educational TV Channels for continuation of the Learning - Teaching Process in the Education System during the COVID-19 Pandemic
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-06
decision_details_body: - A project named ''Nenasa'' has been implemented by Dialog Axiata PLC through satellite technology since 2018 via two Sinhala and Tamil media channels dedicated for education. Under the programme, Dialog Axiata PLC has provided Televisions and Dialog connections to nearly 2,200 schools and no monthly charge is levied for the said connections. Dialog Axiata PLC has agreed to implement the ''Nenasa'' project via 04 channels including 02 new channels with effect from 07th September 2021 for continuation of the Learning‑Teaching Process in the education system during the COVID‑19 Pandemic and to increase the total number of channels up to 10 by 01st January 2022. As such, it was decided to grant the concurrence of the Cabinet of Ministers for the proposal made by the Minister of Education to implement the said project.

description: Establishment of Techno Parks
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-06
decision_details_body: - It has been proposed by the Budget ‑ 2021 to establish 05 Techno Parks in the districts of Galle, Kurunegala, Anuradhapura, Kandy and Batticaloa. As such, the Ministry of Technology, having taken into consideration the connectivity to the Expressway Network, tourism attraction, availability of the requisite Human Resources and other requirements, has identified the appropriate locations to establish the said relevant Techno Parks. It has been planned to establish a Company as ''Techno Park Development Company'' to be fully owned by the Secretary to the Treasury, to enable the said Company to implement the proposed projects as Commercial Enterprises, register the said Company in the Colombo Stock Exchange in future and provide the opportunity to the Private Investors also to take part in the relevant project. Accordingly, the proposal made by H. E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Technology to pursue action for the implementation of the proposed project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing financial sponsorship for the Athletes who won Gold and Bronze Medals at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-06
decision_details_body: - Mr. Dinesh Priyantha Herath has been successful in winning the Gold medal of the Men's F46 category Javelin Throw along with a new World Record and Mr. Samitha Dulan Kodituwakku in winning the Bronze medal of the Men's F64 category Javelin Throw and they have brought extraordinary achievements to their motherland. The National Sports Council established as per the provisions of the Sports Act, No. 25 of 1973, has recommended the criteria on awarding cash prizes for the acclaimed International games victories and the receivable cash prizes. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Youth & Sports to award the cash prizes to the above two victorious athletes and their two coaches, as per the recommendations of the National Sports Council, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Prohibition of Anti-Personnel Mines Bill
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-06
decision_details_body: - An agreement has been reached on a Convention on the Prohibition of the Use, Stockpiling, Production and Transfer of Anti‑Personnel Mines and on their destruction, at the Diplomatic Conference on an International Ban on Anti‑Personnel Land Mines held at Oslo on 18th September, 1997. Accordingly, Sri Lanka has acceded to the said Convention on 13th December 2017 and the Government of Sri Lanka is bound to enact the relevant legislation for the purpose. Clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman for the purpose. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to publish the said Bill in the Government Gazette and present the same thereafter, in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Alienation of lands to Private Sector Investors on Long Term Lease basis to establish large scale Commercial Dairy farms
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-06
decision_details_body:
- Around 40% of the liquid milk requirement in Sri Lanka is manufactured locally and about Rs.50 billion is spent annually for the importation of the balance quantity. Therefore, the Presidential Task Force for Economic Revival & Poverty Alleviation has submitted proposals to the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka to encourage the local and foreign investors for developing the local milk production. As such, the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka has called for proposals from the interested investors and the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture to alienate the unused farm lands belonging to the National Livestock Development Board (NLDB) and those other belonging to the Government, to the investors who have submitted project proposals which have been recommended by the Technical Evaluation Committee of the said Board, on Long Term Lease basis, for a period of 30 years, to improve them as modern dairy farms.

*	Alienation of 700 acres and 60 acres from the farm in Nikaweratiya belonging to the National Livestock Development Board, to HBKLR International Investments/Acces Agro (Pvt.) Ltd. and Pehesara Logistics respectively.

*	Alienation of 811 acres from the Galabodawatta estate and Mount Jean estate belonging to the Janatha Estate Development Board, to Farm's Pride (Pvt.) Ltd..

*	Alienation of 200 acres and 150 acres from the Delthota estate and Great Valley estate respectively, belonging to the Janatha Estate Development Board, to Hillside Agro (Pvt.) Ltd.

*	Alienation of 250 acres from the Kottukachchiya farm belonging to the National Livestock Development Board, to Gamma Pizzakraft Lanka (Pvt.) Ltd.

description: Providing relief for the difficulties faced by the Small and Medium Scale Enterprises
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-06
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet was granted at its meeting held on 2020‑10‑26 to appoint an Officials' Committee to identify the difficulties faced by the Small and Medium Scale enterprises and submit recommendations on the relief to be provided to them and to propose  a mechanism for preparing a data base on the small and medium scale entrepreneurs. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries to implement the recommendations submitted by the said Officials' Committee on the appropriate relief to be provided to the Small and Medium Scale entrepreneurs affected due to the COVID‑19 Pandemic and Easter Sunday Attack, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Declaration of the lands under the Wayamba Maha Ela and Deduru Oya Irrigation Development Projects as a Mahaweli Special Economic Zone
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-06
decision_details_body: - The Mahaweli Water Security Investment Programme has been implemented as a priority project, with the aim of utilizing the excess water of the Mahaweli River Basin for the agro‑economic activities of the rural communities living in the sub‑river basins in the North Western, North Central and Northern provinces and meeting the drinking and industrial water needs of the said areas as well. Under the said Project, it has been planned to construct the artificial canal systems of the North Western Main Canal of 88.9km in length and the North Central Main Canal of 95.7km in length within the next four (04) years and feed 1,500 rural tanks by new 07 reservoir tanks. And, work of the new Deduru Oya Reservoir constructed crossing the Deduru Oya and the construction activities thereunder have been completed and under this project, it is expected to provide irrigation facilities to cultivate 25,000 acres of lands by 200 small tanks in the two seasons, provide drinking water facilities to around 50,000 new consumers and to generate electricity through a Renewable Energy Project of 1.5MW. Under the above two projects, it has been identified to develop less developed lands in the districts of Kurunegala, Puttalam, Anuradhapura and Matale covering 26 Divisional Secretariat Divisions through an Accelerated and Integrated Rural Development Initiative. Accordingly, it has been planned to formulate an Integrated Investment Plan for the Zone with the contribution of all the relevant Ministries and Institutions and implement the said plan in the next three years. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Irrigation, to declare the geographical area comprising 410 Grama Niladhari Divisions covering 26 Divisional Secretariat Divisions in the districts of Kurunegala, Puttalam, Anuradhapura and Matale, as a Special Mahaweli Jurisdiction under the Mahaweli Authority of Sri Lanka Act, No.23 of 1979 and develop the said area under an Integrated Rural Development Process, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Relocation of the Foreign Ministry in One House Building
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-09-06
decision_details_body: - Since sufficient space is not available in the Republic Building where the Foreign Ministry is presently located, some divisions of the said Ministry are maintained at different other locations outside its main office. Several administrative issues have been encountered owing to this reason. Further, it has been identified the necessity of constructing a building with sufficient space for the Foreign Ministry to suit the present requirements. Accordingly, the Cabinet of Ministers granted its concurrence to the proposal made by the Foreign Minister to get a block of land necessary for the construction of a new building allocated from the land located in Vidya Mawatha, which belongs to the Urban Development Authority and is presently being occupied by the Industrial Technology Institute (ITI).

description: Calling for Expression of Interest (EOI) to implement Renewable Energy Projects under Private Sector Investments
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-30
decision_details_body: - It has been aimed at meeting 70% of the electricity requirement in the country from the Renewable Energy sources by the year 2030. Since the hydro‑electricity development in the country has reached its peak, more attention has to be paid towards Solar Power and Wind Power for the purpose. In order to reach the expected goal, the established Solar Power capacity of 458MW and the established Wind Power capacity of 248MW have to be improved by another 4,800MW and 3,500MW, respectively. Further, the National Transmission System needs to be renovated, enabling to receive the electricity so generated, to the said Transmission System. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Power, to call for Expression of Interest (EoI) from local and foreign investors showing interest to finance the said Projects, through Print and Electronic media, giving priority to the identified Projects above 50MW, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Project to provide Indigenous Medicine to the public to control COVID-19 Pandemic
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-30
decision_details_body: - In view of controlling the COVID‑19 pandemic prevailing island‑wide, it has been planned to implement a programme to provide local immunity boosting medicines and immunity boosting herbal gruel, covering all families in the country. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to provide a casket of medicines approved by the Formula Committee of the Department of Ayurveda, to every family in the country and to implement the same for 2.5 million families who have lost income during the Quarantine Curfew period under the First Stage and for all remaining families under its Second Stage, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Alienation of lands to Aura Lanka Herbals Private Limited, on Long Term Lease Basis, to implement a Project to manufacture Herbal Products from Aloe vera plant for export purpose
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-30
decision_details_body: - Aura Lanka Herbals Private Limited has submitted a project proposal as 'Dry Zonal Rural Economic Development Aloe Vera Project', to commence a manufacturing industry of herbal products from Aloe Vera plant in Anuradhapura district, for export purpose under the organic cultivation method. Under the said Project, it is expected to manufacture energy booster drinks, herbal tablets, lotions, inhaler capsules and hair oil using roots, stem, gel and outer leaves of Aloe vera plant. The total investment of the Project is US$ 783 million and the investor has planned to invest US$ 300 million as the initial investment. Under this Project, it is expected to use 2,000 acres located in the Divisional Secretariat Divisions of Rajanganaya and Nochchiyagama to set up nurseries for producing Aloe vera seedlings and 102,000 acres located in the district of Anuradhapura for cultivating Aloe vera by using the saplings produced by the said nurseries. It is proposed to have the families owning lands on Grants and Licenses and those enjoying the State lands for cultivation purposes, participated in this Project. Accordingly, the joint proposal made by the Minister of Finance and the Minister of Lands to alienate a block land approximately 66 acres in extent on Long term Lease basis for a period of 30 years as per the provisions of the State Land Ordinance, to construct and maintain the factory and operational office premises of the said Project and for its storage and operational activities, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Climate Resilience Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (CresMPA)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-30
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet was granted at its meeting held on 2021‑05‑10 to implement the relevant projects within the purview as amended under the Climate Resilience Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (CresMPA). Accordingly, negotiations have been conducted with the relevant stakeholders to secure funds required for the implementation of the project at the total estimated cost of US$ 434 million under 3 phases. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Finance, to enter into an Agreement with the IBRD of the World Bank Group to secure funds of US$ 92 million for the Phase 1 of the said programme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the recommendations of the Cabinet Sub-Committee on ''Removal of Salary Anomalies in the Teachers' and Principals' Services'' appointed by the Cabinet of Ministers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-30
decision_details_body:
- Cabinet, having considered the recommendations submitted thereto, subsequent to the negotiations conducted between the representatives of 33 Teachers', Principals' and Teacher Advisors' Unions and the Cabinet Sub-Committee appointed to examine the matter of removal of salary anomalies in the Teachers' and Principals' Services and submit recommendations to the Cabinet, decided as follows:

*	Granting approval in principle, to implement the recommendations of the Cabinet Sub‑Committee.

*	Declaring the Teachers' Service, Teacher Advisors' Service and Principals' Service as one Closed Service by a Gazette Notification prior to 2021‑11‑20.

*	Taking necessary action to implement the salary revisions proposed by the Cabinet Sub‑Committee for the removal of salary anomalies in the Teachers' and Principals' Services by a budget proposal‑2022, in a phased out manner.

*	Payment of a special allowance of Rs.5,000/- each for the Teachers and Principals engaged in their duties, for the months of September and October, 2021.

*	Taking necessary action to implement the other proposals of the Cabinet Sub‑Committee by the Ministry of Education, in association with the Provincial Councils and other relevant authorities within 06 months.

description: Further extension of the benefits under the Agrahara Insurance Scheme, which is being implemented for the retired Public Officers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-30
decision_details_body: - Provisions have been made under the existing Agrahara Insurance Scheme to provide benefits to those who retired from the Public Service after 01‑01‑2016, until they reach the age of 70. Approval of the Cabinet was granted at its meeting held on 2020‑07‑22 to amend the Agrahara Insurance Scheme, enabling to provide the relevant benefits also to those who have retired from the Public Service prior to the said date. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Public Services, Provincial Councils and Local Government to implement the Agrahara Insurance Scheme making applicable to all those who have retired from the Public Service, further widening the existing benefits, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Employees' Provident Fund Act, No. 15 of 1958 to enter into a Bilateral Social Security Agreement between Sri Lanka and India
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-30
decision_details_body: - Approval was granted by the Cabinet at its meeting held on 27‑02‑2018 to amend the Employees' Provident Fund Act, enabling to sign a bilateral Social Security Agreement between the two countries, with the objectives of exemption of Sri Lankans serving in India from the requirement of contributing to the Social Security Fund of India and Indian nationals serving in Sri Lanka from the requirement of contributing to the Employees' Provident Fund. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour, to publish the Employees' Provident Fund (Amendment) Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman in the Government Gazette and submit the same thereafter, in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining the service of a Self-Propelled Barges (SPBS) supplier for lightering (Barging) Coal from the ships to the Jetty of the Lakvijaya Power Station
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-30
decision_details_body: - Competitive bids have been called for selecting a suitable service supplier for the transportation of coal by barges to the Jetty of the Lakvijaya Power Station. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports & Shipping to award the relevant service contract to M/s Shreeji Shipping Limited, as per the recommendation of the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Updating the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Sri Lanka and the United Kingdom on Certificate of Recognition issued to the Seafarers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-30
decision_details_body: - It is mandatory for a seafarer holding a Foreign Maritime Certificate of Competency to obtain an equivalent Certificate (Certificate of Recognition) from the State in which the said ship is registered, to serve in a ship registered under another State. The Merchant Shipping Secretariat has already entered into Memoranda of Understanding with 33 countries pertaining to the acceptance of such Certificates and this has provided employment opportunities for a large number of Sri Lankan seafarers in foreign vessels. Sri Lanka entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with the United Kingdom to accept such Certificates in 2007 and both parties have agreed to sign an updated Memorandum of Understanding amending  the provisions of the said Memorandum of Understanding, enabling the Sri Lankan seafarers to have more employment opportunities. Clearance of the Attorney General and the Foreign Ministry has been received for the draft Memorandum of Understanding. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports & Shipping to sign the updated Memorandum of Understanding, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Provision of additional allocations for the payment of Widows, Widowers and Orphans Pension
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-30
decision_details_body: - The General Treasury is to incur a sum of around Rs.300,000 million for the retirement benefits of the Public Servants for the year 2021 and under this, provision of Rs.35,500 million has been allocated solely for the payment of Widows, Widowers and Orphans Pension. Of the said sum, Rs.26,367 million has been spent by 30th June 2021 and an additional provision of Rs.19,000 million is required for the balance period of the year. The required provisions for the payment of Widows, Widowers and Orphans Pension is allocated under the 'Special Law Provisions' and the power for the same is vested in the Minister of Finance in terms of Article 150(2) of the Constitution. As such, the Cabinet of Ministers noted that action has been taken to provide Rs.19,000 million under the Expenditure Head of the Department of Pensions, through the Special Law Warrant (Supplementary) signed by the Minister of Finance.

description: Entering into an Agreement between the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Kingdom of Cambodia on the exemption of Visa requirement for holders of Diplomatic and Service & Official Passports
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-30
decision_details_body: - It has been agreed by the two parties to enter into an Agreement between Sri Lanka and the Kingdom of Cambodia on the exemption of visa requirements for holders of Diplomatic and Service & Official Passports. The clearance of the Attorney General and concurrence of the Foreign Ministry have been received for the draft Agreement. Accordingly, the proposal made by H. E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence to sign the said Agreement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: 11.	Importation of 300,000 litres of Liquid Medical Oxygen required for the treatment of COVID 19 patients
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-23
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2021 05 24 to import 120,000 litres of Oxygen monthly to ensure the supply of Liquid Medical Oxygen for the patients with severe COVID 19 conditions. As the number of patients who are being supported with Oxygen has increased due to the outbreak of the new COVID-19 variant, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to import 300,000 litres of Medical Oxygen weekly, in lieu of the 120,000 liters of Medical Oxygen being imported monthly to keep a sufficient storage of Oxygen in the country, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Payment of an allowance of Rs.2,000/- to the families whose livelihoods have been lost due to temporary lockdown of the country to control the outbreak of COVID 19
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-23
decision_details_body: - It has been recognized that it is appropriate to pay an allowance of Rs.2,000/- to the families whose livelihood have been lost, yet do not receive any allowance from the Government, due to temporary lockdown of the country to control the outbreak of COVID 19. Accordingly, the required funds will be released to the District Secretaries and the relevant allowance will be paid to the selected families by the Divisional Secretaries. The Presidential Task Force for Economic Revival and Poverty Eradication will issue the guidelines required for the purpose. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Finance, to release the additional provisions required for the payment of the said allowance, to the District Secretaries, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Presenting the Regulations promulgated for the revision of fees as per the provisions of the Civil Procedure Code, in Parliament for approval
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-23
decision_details_body: - In accordance with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Code, all the rates whether between a party or parties or between a Registered Attorney and a client should be taxed by the Registrar of the Court. The Gazette Notification No.2234/67 dated 2021¬07 02 has been published enacting Regulations for amending the rates referred to in the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.994/7 dated 1997 09 24, which had promulgated the said rates previously, to suit the present needs. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice, to present the said Regulations in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Presenting the Regulations promulgated under the National Gem and Jewellery Authority Act, No.50 of 1993, in Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-23
decision_details_body: - The demand on Gems in the International Gem Market has dropped alarmingly, owing to the present COVID 19 pandemic situation which has spread all over the world. Therefore, several requests have been made by Gem industrialists to provide some relief against the fees levied by the National Gem and Jewellery Authority in its Gem export activities and to arrange facilities to conduct online Gem export activities as the aviation services have been disrupted. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries, to present the Regulations published in the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.2232/36 dated 2021 06 18 under the National Gem and Jewellery Authority Act, No.50 of 1993, to revise the relevant fees and to provide the relevant facilities to conduct online Gem and Jewellery exports, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Purchasing of Local Organic Fertilizer - Maha Season 2021/2022
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-23
decision_details_body: - In terms of the approval granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2021 07 08, prices have been called from the Licensed Local Fertilizer Producers of the National Fertilizer Secretariat to purchase organic fertilizer required for the Maha Season 2021/2022. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, to award the procurement for securing the stocks of fertilizer required for Ceylon Fertilizer Company Ltd. and Colombo Commercial Fertilizers Ltd., to the selected local organic fertilizer producers, as recommended by the Cabinet Appointed Negotiation Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Renovation of the Samanalawewa Tank Bund
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-23
decision_details_body: - The construction activities of the Samanalawewa Power Plant Project with the capacity of 120MW was commenced in the year 1986 and filling the reservoir was carried out in the year 1992. It was identified a water leakage at the reservoir in the same year and even though a number of studies have been conducted in this regard, it has not been possible to detect the exact way of water leakage. The volume of the reservoir has been limited only to 288 million cubic meters due to the said water leakage. Therefore, the expected annual electricity generation capacity of 405 Gwh of the Samanalawewa Power Plant has been reduced by around 70GWh. It has been recognized that there is a layer of limestone which is highly degraded and porous, possible water leakage in the right bank of the reservoir and it has been clear that there is a possibility of further widening of the water leakage way leading to a disastrous situation. Taking into consideration these matters and examining the previous remedial measures, approval of the Cabinet was granted to implement the project which has been presented by the Ceylon Electricity Board, to seal the places of water leakage by using the appropriate raw materials, after removing the water from the reservoir totally and examining the same completely.

description: Progress of the Mega Scale Development Projects by the end of Second Quarter  2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-23
decision_details_body:
- The following information pertaining to the Mega Scale Development Projects island wide was brought to the notice of the Cabinet by the Minister of Finance:

*	319 Mega Scale Development Projects exceeding the total cost of Rs.1000 million are being implemented within the purview of 43 Ministries.

*	The total value of those projects which will be implemented up to the year 2030 is approximately Rs.7.1 trillion.

*	By now, Rs.1.75 trillion has been incurred and the provision of Rs.745 billion has been allocated for the year 2021.

*	88 projects are incorporated in the relevant 319 projects which confirm the new development approach of the Government.

*	The estimated cost for the purpose is Rs.2.5 trillion and Rs.232 billion has been allocated for the said projects in this year.

*	Among the said projects, 'Water for All', 'Development of 100,000 kilometers of Roads', 'Development of 100 Townships', 'Waari Saubhagya' and 'Saubhagya Production Villages' programmes and those which have been launched by the Government to face the COVID 19 pandemic situation are also included.

*	Only 55% of the target expenditure has been utilized for the said projects within the first half of the year due to the COVID-19 pandemic situation in the country.

It was decided by the Cabinet to review the projects which have shown low progress and implement the same on the priority basis enabling to achieve the objectives and targets of these projects and implement the said projects within the close supervision of the Ministry of Develop Co¬ordination and Monitoring enabling to  finalize the activities of the said projects within the due time frame and provide its benefits to the general public.

description: Obtaining an additional Financing from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) under the 'Health System Enhancement Project' (AF-HSEP)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-23
decision_details_body: - In view of implementing the 'Health System Enhancement Project' for generating a healthy community with access to a wider Primary Health Service System, the Asian Development Bank has granted funds of US$ 50 million including  a  loan  of  US$  37.5  million  and  a  grant  of  US$ 12.5  million, to Sri Lanka. Taking into consideration the COVID 19 pandemic situation in the country, US$ 15 million has already been allocated for the COVID 19 related activities out of the said sum, at the request of the Government. In addition, the Asian Development Bank has agreed to provide an additional financing of US$ 125 million under the 'Health System Enhancement Project' to provide facilities required for the management of the increasing number of patients due to COVID 19 pandemic situation. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Health, to conduct negotiations with the Asian Development Bank to secure the said funds, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Motor Vehicle Fleet of the Government
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-23
decision_details_body:
- A Report including the following information on the Motor Vehicle Fleet of the Government was brought to the notice of the Cabinet by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Economic Policies & Plan Implementation.

*	There are 82,194 vehicles belonging to Government Institutions including Ministries, State Enterprises and the Provincial Councils and Local Government Authorities.

*	Out of them, 76,661 vehicles are in running condition while 5,533 vehicles are not.


*	Out of the vehicles in running condition, there are 33,931 vehicles belonging to Government Institutions including Ministries, 26,395 vehicles belonging to State Enterprises and 16,335 vehicles belonging to Provincial Councils and Local Government Authorities.

*	Further, approval has been granted to provide a monthly allowance to around 8,500 Senior Officials at State Institutions and use their personal vehicles for official traveling purposes.
	
	Taking into consideration the above information furnished by the Minister of Economic Policies & Plan Implementation, it was decided by the Cabinet to renovate and make use of the vehicles that may be repaired, out of those which are not in running condition at the time expeditiously and dispose of the vehicles which can not be repaired without any delay, following the formal procedure.

description: Issuance of one-time tourist visa up to 180 days for travelers arriving via Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-23
decision_details_body:
- The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2021 01 04, decided to issue a one-time tourist visa up to 180 days for travellers arriving in Sri Lanka, connecting the ''Sri Lanka Tourism Mobile App'' of the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA) to the tourist visa applying process via ''Online Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA)'' which is operated under the Department of Immigration and Emigration. As such, it was decided to grant concurrence to the proposal made by H. E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence, to issue the said tourist visa charging the following levies:

*	travellers from SAARC countries - US$ 70 
*	travellers from Non SAARC countries - US$ 85 
*	travellers from Singapore, Maldives, Seychelles - US$ 50 (according to the bilateral agreements with those countries)

description: Donation of August salary of the Cabinet Ministers to the COVID 19 Fund
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-23
decision_details_body: - In response to a proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister, it was unanimously decided by the Cabinet to donate the August salary of the Ministers of the Cabinet to the COVID 19 Fund, with a view to strengthening the said Fund to assist in the controlling of the prevailing COVID 19 pandemic situation which has been spread over the country.

description: Scarcity of Milk Powder in the Market
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-09
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet focused its attention on the prevailing scarcity of milk powder in the domestic market. Therefore, the Cabinet decided to authorize the Minister of Finance to examine the prevailing situation in this regard and take necessary action to ensure the adequate supply of milk powder to the domestic market by revising the existing import duty on milk powder or by adopting any other means, without permitting any price increase of milk powder.

description: Appointing a Cabinet Sub-Committee to study the issues relating to salary anomalies in the Teachers’ and Principals’ Services
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-09
decision_details_body:
- The Cabinet conducted lengthy discussions in relation to the current situation occurred with regard to salary anomalies in the Teachers’ and Principals’ Services. Accordingly, the Cabinet decided to appoint a Cabinet Sub-Committee comprising of the following Ministers to further examine the matter, taking into consideration all relevant factors in this regard and submit the same to the Cabinet for consideration: 

	*	Hon. Dullas Alahapperuma,
		Minister of Power 

	*	Hon. Wimal Weerawansa,
		Minister of Industries

	*	Hon. Mahinda Amaraweera,
		Minister of Environment

	*	Hon. Prasanna Ranatunga,
		Minister of Tourism.

description: Importation of organic fertilizer and natural minerals and chelated plant micro nutrients for Maha season 2021/2022
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-09
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2021 05 31 for the importation of fertilizer required for Maha Season 2021/2022 which cannot be secured from the local organic fertilizer producers, by following the open competitive bidding procedure. Accordingly, international competitive bids have been called to secure the required quantity of fertilizer for the Ceylon Fertilizer Company and Colombo Fertilizer Company Limited. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minster of Agriculture to award the relevant procurements, as recommended by the Cabinet Appointed Special Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Consumer Affairs Authority Act N0.9 of 2003
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-09
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2021 07 19 to amend the sub section 5 of section 60 of the Consumer Affairs Authority Act No.9 of 2003. It is expected through these amendments to make required legal provisions to control the sale of essential commodities at high prices by certain traders exceeding the control price in particular. The clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the draft bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman and therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade, to publish the said bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter present the same in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Making legal provisions for the recognition of foreign divorces, annulments or judicial separations within Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-09
decision_details_body: - Sri Lankans who had married in Sri Lanka and thereafter reside in overseas have faced with difficulties as decrees given by foreign courts on the matrimonial cases they have field are not recognized in Sri Lanka. Such parties have to file a fresh divorce case in Sri Lanka, if they want to get order for a divorce. As such, the Family Law Advisory Committee appointed by the Minister of Justice has recommended that it would be appropriate to impose legal provisions enabling to recognize foreign divorces, annulments or judicial separations. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice, to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft legislation to impose legal provisions for the recognition of foreign divorces, annulments or judicial separations in this country, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Tourism Act No. 38 of 2005 to upgrade Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism & Hotel Management(SLTHM) as a degree awarding institute
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-09
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism & Hotel Management (SLTHM) which was established under the Tourism Act No 38 of 2005, conducts training courses from foundation level to management level. Although several universities and private institutes conduct courses equivalent to that of the SLTHM at present, those courses are mainly based on theory and there is no possibility yo obtain a sufficient practical training for the required fields through such courses. Therefore, it has been found appropriate to conduct degree courses in the tourism sector also with a sufficient field training by the Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism & Hotel Management. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Tourism to take necessary action to amend the Tourism Act No 38 of 2005 so as to secure required legal provisions for the purpose and to upgrade the SLTHM in to a tertiary level higher education institute, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Voluntary Social Service Organizations (Registration & Supervision) Act, No. 31 of 1980
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-09
decision_details_body: - It has been observed that the provisions of the existing Voluntary Social Service Organizations (Registration & Supervision) Act, No. 31 of 1980 for the registration of voluntary services are inadequate for the present requirements. Accordingly, the Cabinet having taken into consideration the proposal made by H.E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence, decided to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a Bill to enable to introduce new Act to suit with the present day needs in place of the Voluntary Social Service Organizations (Registration & Supervision) Act, No. 31 of 1980.

description: Regularization of improvements, operation and maintenance of playgrounds and sports complexes constructed at provincial and district levels
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-09
decision_details_body: - Due to the improper maintenance of sports complexes and stadiums located countrywide, it has been observed that sportspersons using these grounds have been unable to obtain their expected training. It is essential to maintain well-equipped sports complexes and stadiums especially for talented athletes at the district and provincial levels in order to achieve the anticipated objectives in the field of sports. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Youth and Sports to introduce a proper methodology to maintain those sports complexes and stadiums with participation of the private sector, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining the service of an Expert Committee for a Sustainable Agriculture
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-09
decision_details_body: - The Ministry of Agriculture and the Institutions coming under its purview are making arrangements to overcome the challenge of directing the entire local agriculture towards the use of fully organic fertilizer to ensure the right of the people to a non-toxic diet with a view to producing a healthy and productive citizen as stated in the Government's policy statement “Vistas of Prosperity and Splendour”. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture to appoint an Expert Committee comprising of scholars in the field, chaired by the Prof. Priyantha Indralal, Professor in Environmental Agriculture of the University of Sabaragamuwa with a view to obtaining the participation of all parties concerned to conduct this programme in a more formal way, and seeking the necessary guidance for making policy decisions, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Working Capital Loan Scheme under concessionary terms for re-energizing Public Enterprises
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-09
decision_details_body: - Operations of around 282 fully or partially public owned enterprises which are now in operation, have been suffered a setback due to the improper function of the market mechanism in consequence of Covid - 19 pandemic situation. Due to that reason, it has become difficult securing working capital required to run their day-to-day business activities. With the spread of Covid - 19 pandemic across the country at the end of the year 2020, the concessionary loan scheme named “Saubhagya Covid-19 Renaissance Facility” was implemented under the supervision of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka to meet the working capital requirement of small and medium scale enterprise sector and under the said scheme, approximately Rs. 156 billion has been granted to around 53,200 entrepreneurs by now. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Finance to make arrangements to secure working capital requirement of the public enterprises through the said loan scheme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Open University of Sri Lanka and the University of Essex, the United Kingdom
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-09
decision_details_body: - It has been proposed to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding between the Open University of Sri Lanka and the University of Essex, the United Kingdom for the objectives of obtaining opportunities to enter into the University of Essex for students who have qualified after completing the relevant courses at the Open University of Sri Lanka, implementing collaborative research projects on mutual consent and organizing student, faculty and staff exchange programmes. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to sign the said MoU between two parties, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the University of Sri Jayewardenepura and the Edith Cowan University, Australia
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-09
decision_details_body: - It has been proposed to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding between the University of Sri Jayewardenepura and the Edith Cowan University, Australia for the objectives of improving research collaborations in the fields where the two parties are mutually agreed, implementing mobility programmes for students according to the requirements of both parties, implementing the Executive Education Programme on Hospitality and implementing curricula and study development programmes and joint Doctoral Degree programmes. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to sign the said MoU between two parties, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Commencing a national broadcasting channel for primary, secondary, higher education and tertiary education
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-02
decision_details_body: - The Ministry of Education together with the Ministry of Mass Media has planned to commence a broadcasting channel to address the anomalies emerged in the field of education due to the social distancing caused by the Covid - 19 pandemic situation, so as to cover the entire island. Since it takes a considerable period of time to get completed the required infrastructure facilities for the purpose, the joint proposal made by the Minister of Education and the Minister of Mass Media to utilize one of the channels of the Sri Lanka Broadcasting Corporation covering the entire country so as to commence a broadcasting channel dedicated for education, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Revising the compensation scheme for the damages caused by protected wildlife including wildlife
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-02
decision_details_body:
- The Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Wildlife and Forest Conservation to revise the scheme of compensation presently being paid for the dependants of the deceased and those who succumb to complete or partial disability and for the the houses and properties damaged due to the attacks by protected wild life such as wild elephants, leopards, bear, wild buffaloes and crocodiles as follows:

* 	to increase the the amount of compensation of Rs.500,000/- which 	was being paid for a death, up to Rs.100,0000/, irrespective of age or gender.

* 	to increase the the amount of compensation of Rs.500,000/- which 	was being paid for a person who becomes completely disable, up to Rs.100,0000/-, irrespective of age or gender.

* 	to increase the the amount of compensation of Rs.75,000/- which was being paid for a person who becomes partial impairment or physical injury, up to Rs.150,0000/-. 

* 	to increase the the amount of compensation of Rs.100,000/- which 	was being paid for the damages caused to houses and property by wild elephant attacks, up to a maximum of Rs. 200,0000/-.

description: Celebration of the National Logistics Day
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-02
decision_details_body: - Efficient and effective operation of all supplies of a country is termed logistics. If the functioning process related thereto could not be operated properly, it would resulted in causing several problems such as increase of the prices of goods thereby making it difficult to control the cost of living. Therefore, declaration of a National Logistics Day has been found appropriate in order to make the public aware on the process related to Logistics. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport to declare the 16th of August as the National Logistics Day from this year onwards and to issue a commemorative stamp to mark the said day, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Joint Agreement between the University of Ruhuna, University of Jaffna, National Aquatic Resources Research and Development Agency (NARA) and UiT the Arctic University of Norway
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-02
decision_details_body: - UiT the Arctic University of Norway implements the Project of ''Innovative Network in Fisheries, Aquaculture and Aquatic Science'' under the financial contribution of the Norwegian Partnership Programme for Global Academic Co‑operation. The University of Ruhuna, University of Jaffna and the National Aquatic Resources Research and Development Agency (NARA) have been recognized as local partners of the said project. Accordingly, it has been proposed to enter into a Joint Agreement between UiT the Arctic University of Norway and the said Institutions for implementing the said project. Under this Agreement, it is expected to implement scholarship programmes for the benefit of both parties through a collaborative partnership between UiT the Arctic University of Norway and local institutions, maintain student and staff exchange programmes and promote international understanding. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Education, to enter into the proposed Joint Agreement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into an Agreement between the University of Colombo and the University of Birmingham, United Kingdom for a Research Project to Explore the Global Spectrum on Science and Religion
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-02
decision_details_body: - In view of creating an expanded dialogue on the nexus between Science, Evolution and Religion among professional scientists and the general public and exploring the historical, cultural, social and psychological factors affecting the public opinion on the said elements, the University of Colombo has been selected as a partner of the research project on 'Science and Religion: Exploring the Spectrum of Global Perspectives' conducted under the financial provisions of the Religious Fund named 'Templeton Religious Trust'. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education, to enter into a Joint Agreement with the University of Birmingham, United Kingdom, which is its main partner, to implement the said research project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing a plot of land from Millewa, Horana to the State Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Corporation of Sri Lanka, on Lease Basis
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-02
decision_details_body: - Since the existing space in the State Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Corporation of Sri Lanka is not sufficient for increasing the capacity of the said Corporation, the State Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Corporation of Sri Lanka has made a request to the Urban Development Authority (UDA) to provide a plot of land to establish five (05) production facilities and expand its manufacturing activities. Accordingly, the Board of Management of the Urban Development Authority has given its concurrence to allocate a plot of land in extent of 65 acres 17.66 perches out of the block of land 732 acres in extent, which has been acquired from Millewa area for the Horana Industrial Township Project. As such, the proposal made by Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing, to provide the relevant plot of land to the State Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Corporation of Sri Lanka on long‑term lease basis upon the said agreement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Organisational Membership Engagement Agreement between BCS, the Chartered Institute for IT and the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University (KDU)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-08-02
decision_details_body: - It has been proposed to sign an Organisational Membership Engagement Agreement between the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University (KDU) and BCS, the Chartered Institute for IT. BCS, the Chartered Institute for IT, formerly known as the British Computer Society, registers persons qualified and experienced in Computing as its Professional Members. BCS, the Chartered Institute for IT has expressed its willingness to grant a non‑exclusive license to the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University (KDU) to engage in the activities of assessing the persons who apply for the membership of the said Institute. As such, the proposal made by H. E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence, to sign an Organisational Membership Engagement Agreement to pursue action accordingly, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Preparation of the Annual Budget for the Year 2022
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-26
decision_details_body:
- The Minister of Finance informed the Cabinet the following measures intended to be taken when preparing Annual Budget for the year 2022 within the Medium Term Budgetary Framework 2022-2024 and the Cabinet granted its concurrence for the same.

	(a)	Macroeconomic Targets expected to be achieved ( As percentage of 	GDP) -

		*	Government Revenue		-	13.0
		*	Government Expenditure		-	20.6
		*	Budget Deficit			-	-7.5
		*	Central Government Debt		-	95.0
		*	Economic Growth	Rate		-	6.0

	In order to achieve the said targets, it is expected to maintain a stable  exchange rate, to maintain the inflation at a stable figure of 5% and to bring the unemployment rate below 4%, in the year 2022.
	
	(b)	keep the country open while safeguarding public health and continuing 	precautionary measures against the Covid -19 pandemic.

	(c)	Giving top priorities for using digital technology for rendering 	public service, providing required relief and facilities  for the sectors 	affected by the Covid -19, expanding and promoting import substitutes 	encouraging private sector investments towards export-oriented sectors, 	strengthening foreign direct investments by creating friendly 	environment for the investment, expanding government revenue and 	moving towards renewable energy.
	(d)	highly discouraging the activities such as new constructions except 	ongoing projects and tasks, expanding office space, purchase of new 	furniture and equipment, 	new recruitment, purchase of new vehicles 	other than essential	vehicles, until the economy returned to the 	normalcy.

	(e)	moving every Government institution towards new avenues of revenue 	generation in their capacity during  the year 2022.

description: Obtaining the Service of 150 Teachers for the National Institute of Education
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-26
decision_details_body: - The National Institute of Education has taken steps to introduce   educational reforms  to create an education system  required to generate competent children to find solutions for the challenges to be encountered in the 21st Century. It has been scheduled to introduce specific changes for curriculum and teaching methods through such reforms. It is expected to introduce the proposed reforms for grades 1,2,6,8 and 10 in the year 2023 and for grades 3,4,5,7 and 11 in the year 2024. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to attach 150 experienced teachers in Teachers' Service in Government schools with the proficiency of the relevant subjects, since the present staff serving in the National Institute of Education is inadequate for the said purposes, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Purchase of locally produced liquid large volume parenterals for State sector
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-26
decision_details_body: - The State Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing Corporation has facilitated to the  Kelun Lifesciences (Pvt) Limited, a local company, to construct a factory with the capacity of manufacturing 43 million of liquid large volume parenterals annually including normal saline, dextrose solution, Hartmann's solution and mannitol. Approval of  the State Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing Corporation has been received to the said factory and its productions and it is scheduled to supply its productions to the market from August, 2021. The State Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing Corporation is expected to reach an agreement with the said company to secure  liquid large volume parenterals locally. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to authorize the State Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing Corporation to enter into an Agreement with M/s Kelun Lifesciences (Pvt) Limited, to secure required liquid large volume parenterals for the institutions coming under the purview of Ministry Health from that company, was approved by the Ministry.

description: Purchase of surgical gauze from local suppliers required for the Government Hospitals and other Health Institutions
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-26
decision_details_body: - Cabinet approval has been granted in the year 2012 to purchase annual surgical gauze requirement for the Medical Supply Division from local small scale manufacturers. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to purchase 30 million meters of surgical gauze for the year 2021 from 461 local suppliers at a sum of Rs. 774 million, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Investment of South Asia Logistics Center in the Port of Colombo
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-26
decision_details_body: - One of the strategic objectives of the National Ports Master Plan is to develop the Colombo Port, being the main hub port in the South Asian region, as a logistic hub. Under this, the areas of Battenberg and Bloemendhal belonging to the Colombo South Port have been identified as those which may be developed as logistic business areas under the Public Private Partnership. And, the Unity Container Terminal (UCT) has been recognized as appropriate to construct the in house Container Freight Station (CFS) of Sri Lanka Ports Authority with logistic facilities. It has been planned to commence partial operational activities of the East Container Terminal (ECT) and West Container Terminal (WCT) in 2023 and accordingly, the throughput of Colombo Port will exceed 10 million TEU per annum.  Within this situation, the necessity of constructing a logistic centre expeditiously, has arisen and the Colombo International Container Terminal (CICT) has submitted an investment proposal for the purpose. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports & Shipping, to appoint a negotiation committee to evaluate the proposal submitted by the Company for the implementation of a project for construction of a logistic centre in a block of land nearly in extent of 5.3 hectares in the area of Battenberg of Colombo South Port adjacent to the South Asia Gateway Terminal (SAGT), Colombo International Container Terminal (CICT) and the East Container Terminal (ECT) under the Public Private Partnership and pursue action  as per the recommendations of the said Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Alienating a block of land belonging to the Land Reforms Commission, on lease basis, for an educational and entertainment tourism project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-26
decision_details_body: - Fantasy Land Entertainment (Pvt) Limited has planned to implement a tourism project with educational and entertainment components, aiming at local and foreign tourists. The Board of Investment (BOI) has agreed with the said project and for this, the relevant Company has made a request to alienate a block of land in extent of 42 acres 01 rood and 1.5 perches, out of the land called Rathwaththa in the Divisional Secretariat Division of Ukuwela in Matale district, belonging to the Land Reforms Commission, on lease basis for a period of 30 years. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Lands, to alienate the relevant block of land to the said Company on long term lease basis, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Vesting the land where the old Chemical Factory in Paranthan is situated, with Paranthan Chemicals Limited on long term lease basis
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-26
decision_details_body: - Paranthan Chemicals Limited, a State owned Company which functions within the purview of the Ministry of Industries, imports liquid Chlorine necessary for the water purification process from India and Bangladesh and supplies to the National Water Supply & Drainage Board (NWS&DB) as its main business venture. The said Company has planned to start up a factory to locally produce Sodium Hydroxide and Chlorine and expects to produce Hydrochloric Acid, Poly Aluminium Chloride and Sodium Hypochlorite as by products of the said project. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries, to vest the block of land where the old chemical factory in Paranthan is located and which has been enjoyed by Paranthan Chemicals Limited since 1954, with the said Company on long term lease basis, enabling to employ the same land for the said project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Civil Procedure Code
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-19
decision_details_body: - Provisions have been made by Article 12 of the Constitution to the effect that no citizen should be discriminated on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion or place of birth or any one of such grounds. However, since the Muslim Marriage and Divorce Act which governs marriage and divorce of Muslims, includes certain provisions which are discriminatory for women, various Women's Organizations and scholars on Muslim law belonging to Muslim community have pointed out the need of removing such provisions from the law. Therefore, it has been observed that it would be appropriate to provide the Muslim community with optional opportunities to have their marriages and divorces governed under the general law which presently governs the marriages and divorces of the citizens of Sri Lanka. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to amend the Civil Procedure Code and the procedure relating to Matrimonial actions in the Civil Procedure Code, enabling persons professing Islam to be governed under the said Ordinance, if they are expected to get married under the Marriage Registration Ordinance, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the recommendations of the Notarial Advisory Committee appointed by the Minister of Justice
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-19
decision_details_body:
- The Minister of Justice has appointed Advisory Committees with the Cabinet approval to submit recommendations on the reforms to be made in the legal field. Accordingly, the proposals made by the Minister of Justice to amend the following Ordinance/Acts as recommended by the Notarial Advisory Committee so appointed, was approved by the Cabinet.	

*	The Powers of Attorney Ordinance

*	The Notaries Ordinance

*	The Registration of Documents Ordinance

*	The Revocation of Irrevocable Deeds of Gift on the Ground of Gross 	Ingratitude Act 

*	The Wills Ordinance

description: Petroleum Resource Development Bill
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-19
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2021‑01‑25 granted approval to formulate a new Act, including necessary provisions for the development of petroleum and gas exploration and production industry in Sri lanka by repealing the Petroleum Resources Act No. 26 of 2003. Accordingly, the clearance of the Attorney General has been received to the Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Energy to publish the said draft bill in the Government Gazette and present the same thereafter in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of Gazette Notifications in Parliament for approval

description: Creation of a Judicial Training Academy
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-19
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka Judges' Institute is the sole education institute in the field of Judiciary in Sri Lanka and its contribution for adequate training and capacity building of the judges is not up to the level of satisfaction. In many countries of the world, institutions have been set up and maintained with the facilities similar to the universities, with a view to educating and training judges. The Government has prioritized the promotion of the fields of infrastructure development, legislative reforms and digitization. And also, the necessity of providing required facilities to judges to improve their knowledge and skills has been identified. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to appoint a Committee comprising the experts in the field chaired by Hon. Supreme Court Judge Buwaneka Aluwihare, to obtain recommendations for the establishment of a Judicial Training Academy in Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Granting approval for Water Villas and Water Bungalows
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-19
decision_details_body: - With a view to attracting high‑end travellers in the global tourism industry, some countries engaged in the tourism industry have introduced the concept of “Water Villas”. It has appeared that the concept of Water Villas and Water Bungalows can be used for promoting tourism industry in Kalpitiya and other maritime areas. 12 islands in Kalpitiya have already been vested with the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA) to develop tourism industry in the said areas by promoting the concept of “Island Resorts”. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Tourism to implement the project for the construction of a luxury tourist resort comprising 50 Water Villas and Water Bungalows by M/s Sun Resort Investment Lanka (Pvt) Ltd, which has acquired Vellai I, Vellai II and Vellai III islands in Kalpitiya on long term lease basis, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the University of Ruhuna, Sri Lanka and the Galilee International Management Institute, Israel
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-19
decision_details_body: - In view of exchanging the scientific and managerial knowledge and skills in the field of agriculture, it has been agreed to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the University of Ruhuna, Sri Lanka and the Galilee International Management Institute, Israel. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to sign the relevant MoU between the two parties, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Vesting the Government owned lands enjoyed by the Open University of Sri Lanka, with the said University
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-19
decision_details_body: - The Open University of Sri Lanka (OUSL) established in the year 1980 in terms of the Universities Act, No.16 of 1978, is one of the sixteen (16) national universities within the purview of the University Grants Commission. This University conducts seventy five (75) academic programmes from the Foundation Stage to the Doctoral Stage and 44,600 students have been enrolled to the said University for the year 2020. This University, being the sole higher education institute established by the Government for the purpose of providing higher education through open and distance education methods, has its nine (09) Regional Centres and nineteen (19) Study Centres established island‑wide. In view of providing proper education to students, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to vest seventeen (17) Government owned land plots where Regional Centres and Study Centres are located, with the Open University of Sri Lanka as per the provisions of the State Lands Ordinance enabling to further improve the adequate physical facilities of the said Centres, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Programme to encourage farmers for production and use of fertilizer by themselves for paddy cultivation in Maha Season of 2021/2022
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-12
decision_details_body: - The Ministry of Agriculture has planned to meet the requirement of organic fertilizer for paddy cultivation of about 800,000 hectares for the Maha season 2021/2022. Accordingly, necessary steps have already been taken to direct farmers to produce quality organic fertilizer, specially under the guidance of the Department of Agrarian Development, and to increase the quantity of organic fertilizer produced by licensed manufacturers. The proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, to pay an incentive of Rs. 12,500 per hectare not exceeding 02 hectares (05 acres) to farmers who themselves produce and use organic fertilizer, in order to encourage them for the production of organic fertilizer, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Mid - Year Fiscal Position Report
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-12
decision_details_body: - The Minister of Finance is required to present the report on the Mid – Year Fiscal Position to the public by the last date of the month of June in every fiscal year as per the provisions of section 10 of the Fiscal Management (Responsibility) Act, No.3 of 2003 and subsequently the said report is required to be submitted in Parliament. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Finance to submit the Report on the Mid – Year Financial Position of 2021 which was issued on the 2021‑06‑30 in parliament, was approved by the Cabinet of Ministers.

description: Amendments to the National Water Resources Supply and Drainage Board Act in order to face the present and future challenges in the water sector
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-12
decision_details_body: - The National Water Supply and Drainage Board, established in 1975 under the provisions of the National Water Supply and Drainage Board Act, No. 2 of 1974, currently operates 331 water supply schemes and operates 2.4 million domestic connections and 207,000 commercial connections. Accordingly, the National Water Supply and Drainage Board contributes 43.8% of the 93.8% of the total safe drinking water coverage in the country. However, the National Water Supply and Drainage Board has to take the necessary steps in the future to address the challenges such as the rapid urbanization, climate change, rising consumer demands for water and the use of digital technology in the water sector.
