Although the National Water Supply and Drainage Board Act has been amended on several times to address these issues, it has been identified that the Act needs to be further amended to suit the present requirements. Accordingly, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Water Supply to appoint a committee headed by the Secretary to the Ministry of Water Supply for preparing a preliminary draft by taking suggestions and recommendations from the public and private sector stakeholders regarding the amendments to be made to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board Act.

description: Amendments the Water Resources Board Act No.29 of 1964
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-12
decision_details_body: - In terms of the provisions of the Water Resources Board Act, No. 29 of 1964, relevant orders have been published in the Gazette Notification dated 2017‑03‑16, to bring the regulations on the monitoring and supervision of activities relating to the control of the excessive use of ground water for commercial purposes and prevention of water pollution under the supervision and control of the Water Resource Board. However, it has been observed that the Water Resources Board Act does not have adequate provisions for imposing penalties for the offences related thereto. Although the Act carries provisions to control the use and possession of illegal drilling machines without being registered under the Water Resources Board, no legal provisions have been made to take legal actions in the case of breach of such orders. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Water Supply to introduce necessary legal provisions required to take action as stated above and to face the challenges encountered by the said board in discharging services, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Signing a Memorandum of Understanding between the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Russian Federation for strengthening the cooperation in Sports
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-12
decision_details_body: - It has been proposed to enter into a bilateral Memorandum of Understanding between Sri Lanka and the Russian Federation to strengthen the cooperation in the field of sports. Under the said MoU, it is expected to organize sports related games for all the sports with priority to the sports such as athletics, swimming, gymnastics, volleyball, weightlifting, wrestling, swordsmanship, football and squash and to exchange the programmes, experiences and information between sports organizations, sports federations and other recognized sports structures. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Youth and Sports to enter into the proposed Memorandum of Understanding, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Introducing a Long-Term Visa Category to promote Sri Lanka as a favorable destination for digital nomads
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-12
decision_details_body: - Digital nomads are people who use digital technologies to earn a living and spend their lives in a nomadic manner. Facilitating such nomads has become a trend in the tourism sector at present. Digital nomads provide their services through the use of internet devices staying in restaurants, public libraries and such other places or recreational vehicles. Availability of high speed internet access for communication, long term visa, cost effective accommodation, tax exemption for their earnings has been very helpful in attracting such nomads. It will be possible to earn a huge amount of foreign exchange by way of attracting digital nomads to Sri Lanka and facilitating them to stay a longer period in this country. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Tourism to implement a promotion programme by the Sri Lanka Tourism Promotion Bureau in order to attract digital nomads and to introduce a long term visa category (up to one year) for digital nomads, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of ''Nationally Determined Contributions'' to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change related to the Paris Agreement
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-12
decision_details_body:
- Sri Lanka functions as a party of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Changes from the year 1993. Accordingly, Sri Lanka signed the Paris Agreement on 2016‑04‑21 and it was ratified on the 21st September of the same year. The prime objective of the Paris Agreement is to maintain global warming under 2° C compared to the level which prevailed in the pre – industrial era, and to take all possible measures to maintain it at 1.5° C level. The activities carried out by the stakeholders to achieve said objectives are called as “Nationally Determined Contributions”.

Accordingly, the first “Nationally Determined Contributions” recognized to implement by Sri Lanka during the period 2020 – 2030 has been submitted to United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Changes in the year 2016 with the Cabinet approval. Those contributions, submitting under 14 major sectors should be updated once in every 05 years and re–submitted by preparing same in a more targeted manner. However, those updated contributions were scheduled to be submitted to the 26th session of stakeholders to be held in the month of December 2020, yet the session has been postponed up to the month of November 2021 due to the COVID pandemic situation. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to submit the “Nationally Determined Contributions” that has been re–updated with the participation of stakeholder institutions of the relevant sectors by adapting to the current Government policy to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Changes and to appoint a National Steering Committee to monitor the effective implementation of the said contributions, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Promoting the use of Electric Vehicles in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-12
decision_details_body: - According to the data of the Department of Motor Traffic, the number of registered motor vehicles in Sri Lanka by the end of the year 2020 has exceeded 8 million. A considerable portion of vehicles out of which are older than 10 years and it has been identified that improper maintenance of such old vehicles resulted in toxic gas emissions. The University of Moratuwa and few other Institutions have confirmed through their researches that 60% of air pollution in Sri Lanka is caused by motor vehicles. Attention has also been drawn to the use of renewable energy for running vehicles since the expeditious implementation of renewable energy projects is one of the first priorities of the Government. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to prepare a strategic plan to promote the use of electrical vehicles in Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the University of Peradeniya, Sri Lanka and the Meijo University, Japan
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-12
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by the Minister of Education to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding for developing higher education collaboration between the University of Peradeniya and the Meijo University, Japan with the objectives of organizing student and staff exchange programmes, exchanging academic publications and study materials in areas of common interest and organizing lectures, seminars and conferences under joint studies and scientific activities, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the University of Sri Jayawardenepura and Chengdu Agricultural College, China
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-12
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by the Minister of Education to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding on developing collaborations between the University of Sri Jayawardenepura and Chengdu Agricultural College, China with the objectives such as exchanging data and information on the educational and scientific researches between the two parties, exchanging staff and students, developing and disseminating integrated curricula, conducting combined researches and production of tea and herbal crops, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishing nine (9) Video Evidence Recording Units of children exposed to abuses, at provincial level
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-12
decision_details_body: - The evidence given by children who become victims of various forms of abuses, pertaining to that incident is more vital in the judicial process. However, Since, such victimized children are faced with various problems in presenting evidence before the court publicly, provisions have been introduced to the judicial system of Sri Lanka by the Evidence (Special Provisions ) Act No. 32 of 1999 to obtain and present such evidence as video recordings. Accordingly, a Video Evidence Recording Unit was set up at the National Child Protection Authority in 2001 and the process of obtaining such evidence is carried out only in Colombo at present. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to establish 09 Video Evidence Recording Units in Hospitals covering the nine (09) provinces in the country, enabling to establish the said facility at provincial level, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment of Committees to make recommendations on disburse claims for the damages caused by the fire of the MV X-Press Pearl Maritime Disaster
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body: - An amount of Rs. 720 million has been approved as the first interim claim to be paid to the parties affected by maritime damage caused by MV X-Press Pearl fire. Accordingly the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Hon. Minister of Justice to appoint a committee chaired by the Secretary to the Ministry of Fisheries and comprising of officials from other relevant institutions to make recommendations on the payment of compensation to the fishing community and to appoint a committee under the chairmanship of the secretary to the Ministry Finance and comprising of secretaries to the other relevant Ministries to pay compensation to the affected parties other than the fisheries sector.

description: Implementation of Paddy Purchasing Programme in Yala Season 2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body:
- A paddy harvest of 1,500,000 is expected to be received during this yala season. Out of this harvest, the Paddy Marketing Board has planned to purchase a considerable quantity of paddy. Therefore, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture to implement the paddy purchasing programme for yala season 2021 as follows:

* 	To purchase paddy from farmers under guaranteed prices of Rs.50/- for one kilo of Nadu, Rs.52/- for one kilo of Samba and Rs.55/- for one kilo of Kiri Samba.

* 	To pay Rs. 1.50 per 1kg of paddy for farmers for processing and transportation when purchasing quality paddy directly from farmers in addition to the guaranteed price.

* 	To pay Rs. 1.50 per 1kg of paddy to the farmer organizations for processing and transportation when purchasing quality paddy from farmers in difficult areas through farmer organizations in addition to the guaranteed price.

* 	to pay farmers having deducted the guaranteed price by Rs. 8 per kilo of paddy with 14% - 22% moisture, when purchasing paddy through Paddy Mill owners and farmer organizations that have drying facilities, and to pay Rs 4/- per kilo of paddy to dry and prepare such stocks and to pay Rs. 2/- for transportation to such mill owners and farmer organizations.

* 	Making provisions for the purchase of harvest in 2021 Yala season to the Paddy Marketing Board with the intervention of the General Treasury and the District Secretaries/ Government Agents.

description: Submission of Regulations issued under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, No.1 of 1969 for approval in Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body:
- Action has been taken since April 2020 to limit the importation of goods in order to ease the pressure on external reserves and the financial market which caused by unexpected economic crisis resultant by the Covid-19 pandemic. However, the Tariff Determination Committee appointed by H.E the President has taken following steps to safeguard local industries and to continuously facilitate for the importation of essential commodities:

* 	Granting permission to import goods which were permitted to import on suppliers' credit facility as general importation of goods.

* 	Further continue the importation restrictions on selected Agro products, plastic goods,ceramic products,vehicles and wooden products. 

* 	Granting permission to import oxygen and respiratory apparatus only on the recommendation of the National Medicinal Regulator Authority.

* 	Listing out the importation of gold and face masks under the Import Control License System.

	Therefore, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to submit 03 regulations issued under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, No.1 of 1969 and published in the Government Gazette dated 2021‑06‑11, for approval in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Universities Act, No 16 of 1978 for inclusion of the provision required for the establishment of Universities with specific purposes
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted previously to amend the Universities Act, No 16 of 1978 incorporating the provisions required to establish universities for specific purposes. Accordingly, clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the draft bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Education, to publish the said draft bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter present the same in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of New Tax Proposals
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body: - Budget 2021 has proposed to impose legal provisions for the investors to pay only a “Tax on Voluntary Disclosure” at the rate of 1%, exempting them from a paying a tax, penalty or interest or from any investigation or prosecution in order to encourage such investors to disclose and invest undisclosed income and assets. Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2021‑02‑22 to draft the Finance Bill - 2021 in order to make provisions required for the purpose. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, to publish the draft bill so prepared in the Government Gazette and thereafter present the same in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Gazette Notification published under the Value Added Tax Act, No14 of 2002 for approval in Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body: - The Gazette Notification No.2228/33 dated 2021‑05‑20 has been issued under the Value Added Tax Act, No. 14 of 2002 enacting a regulation by the Minister of Finance making it compulsory the completion of schedules 6 and 7 that can be obtained from the web portal of the Department of Inland Revenue, enabling to streamline the values of exports declared by exporters with export data submitted to the Sri Lanka Customs. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to submit the said regulation in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Aranya Senasana Conservation Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body: - It has been identified the necessity of making a formal arrangement to conserve and maintain Aranya Senasana while protecting the identity of the Bikkhus living in Aranyas. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs ,to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft legislation for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding of the contract for the phase II of Multi-Storied Car Park & Mixed Development Project at Colombo Fort
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body: - Bids have been invited for the Design & Construction of Super Structure of Multi‑Storied Car Park & Mixed Development Project at Colombo Fort ‑ Phase II, following the National Competitive Bidding Procedure. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing to award the relevant contract to M/s. Tudawe Brothers (Pvt.) Ltd., the lowest bidder, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Joint re-establishment of Kondachchi Estate of Sri Lanka Cashew Corporation in amalgamation with the Sri Lanka Cashew Corporation and Civil Security Department
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body: - A Cashew cultivation had been commenced and maintained in a land of 6,000 acres in extent acquired by the Sri Lanka Cashew Corporation from the Government in 1979, situated in the village of Kondachchi of the Musali Divisional Secretariat Division in Mannar district and the said cultivation has been defunct due to the civil conflict prevailed. By now, the Sri Lanka Cashew Corporation and the Civil Security Department have taken action to cultivate Cashew in an area of 935 acres of the said extent of land. The Budget ‑ 2021 has allocated a provision of Rs.125 million for the re‑establishment of Cashew cultivation in the Kondachchi estate. Having utilized the said provisions, the Sri Lanka Cashew Corporation has planned to implement a Cashew Cultivation project in an area of 1,500 acres and to cultivate Cashew in another area of 500 acres in addition to the extent of 935 acres already cultivated by the Civil Security Department. Both parties have agreed to provide saplings, technical assistance, training and supervision required for the cultivation activities of the Civil Security Department by the Sri Lanka Cashew Corporation and to conduct maintenance activities of the cultivation by the said Department. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Plantation to take action accordingly, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Accelerating land acquisition for identified Irrigation Development Projects
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet was granted at its meeting held on 2021‑02‑01 to adopt the 'LARC' and 'SUPER LARC' system to pay compensation for the lands acquired for Government purposes, until appropriate amendments are to be introduced to the Land Acquisition Act. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Irrigation to calculate and pay compensation adopting the 'LARC' and 'SUPERLARC' system to the relevant owners for the lands to be acquired for the implementation of the drinking and irrigated water supply projects in the Northern, North Central, Central, North Western and Eastern provinces identified as prioritized projects, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Provision of essential goods on the intervention of Lanka Sathosa and Co-operative Sector for price stabilization in Local Market
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body: - In the wake of COVID‑19 pandemic situation, the necessity of continuing the supply of essential food items in the local market without shortage has been identified. It has been observed that specially Red Dhal and White Sugar are sold at higher prices by now in the local market. As a remedy, it has appeared that it is possible to directly import Sugar and Dhal from India and Australia on the intervention of Co‑operative sector and sell the same through Lanka Sathosa and Co‑operative sales network. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade to take necessary action, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Keeping Children Learning Through Home-based Activities' during the COVID-19 closure of schools
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body:
- Action has been taken to offer education to students through alternative ways such as 'e-thaksalawa', 'Guru Gedara' TV and radio programmes, NIE YouTube Channel and Provincial level and School level on‑line lessons during the school closure due to the COVID‑19 pandemic situation. However, practical issues have arisen in respect of optimal utilization of schools, principals, teachers, in‑service advisors and other senior officials, maintenance of common standards in teaching methods, accounting of student engagement and assessment of learner achievement. Accordingly, as a remedial measure against the said issues, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to implement a programme titled 'Keeping Children Learning Through Home‑based Activities' designed as follows, from 2021‑08‑01, by utilizing all institutions and human resources belonging to the Education sector optimally, following the health rules and guidelines, was approved by the Cabinet. 

* 	standardization and integration of activities with the expected learning outcomes for each grade level.

* 	supervision and monitoring of activities by teachers.

* 	Weekly assessment of student performance and maintenance of student performance reports by teachers.

* 	Implementation of Home‑based Learning activities by the school principal and teachers with the involvement of parents and students.

*	Supervision and monitoring of teacher performance by the in‑service advisors.

* 	Appointment of Committees comprising Senior Officials to implement and monitor the proposed programme at national, provincial and zonal levels.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the National Korea Maritime & Ocean University and the Ocean University of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body: - The National Korea Maritime & Ocean University and the Ocean University of Sri Lanka have agreed to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between each other encouraging the collaborative activities such as the exchange of faculty, researches and administrative staff, exchange of students, academic co‑operation on collaborative research, lectures and conferences and exchange of academic information and materials. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to sign the relevant Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Agreement on Co-operation and Mutual Administrative Assistance in Customs Matters between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka and Bangladesh have agreed to enter into an agreement on co‑operation and mutual administrative assistance in Customs matters with the objectives of accurate assessment of Customs Duty and other taxes, ensuring the proper enforcement of prohibitions, restrictions and measures of control by the Customs administration in respect of specific goods and effective enforcement of Customs Laws against Customs offences. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to sign the proposed agreement between the two countries, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Granting tax exemptions as per the provisions of the Strategic Development Projects (SDP) Act, No.14 of 2008, for the projects to be set up in the Dedicated Textile Manufacturing Zone at Punnaikudah, Eravur Pattu, Batticaloa
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-07-05
decision_details_body:
- Approval of the Cabinet was granted at its meeting held on 2020‑10‑26 to set up a Dedicated Textile Manufacturing Zone at Punnaikudah, Eravur Pattu, Batticaloa and to treat it as a strategic development project as proposed by the Minister of Industries. Accordingly, the tax and other exemptions to be granted for the projects to be set up in the proposed zone, under section 3 (2) of the said Act has been published in the Extraordinary Gazette Notification dated 2021‑04‑20. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to take action as follows, was approved by the Cabinet:

* 	to identify and recognize the proposed Textile Manufacturing Zone as a Strategic Development Project under section 3 (3) of the Strategic Development Projects Act.

* 	to adopt the relevant tax and other exemptions for the projects to be set up in the said zone as per the provisions of the Act.

*	to publish a Gazette Notification in terms of section 3 (4) of the Strategic Development Projects Act, specifying the tax and other exemptions to be so granted.

*	to submit the said Gazette Notification, which include the tax and other exemptions to be so declared, in Parliament for approval as per section 3 (5) of the Act.

description: Facilitating the raising of foreign funds to local Companies
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-28
decision_details_body: - In view of providing the opportunity to raise foreign funds to local Companies onshore, the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) has submitted a proposal to list foreign currency denominated shares issued by the Companies registered in Sri Lanka, in the Colombo Stock Exchange. In terms of the Foreign Exchange Regulation No.02 of 2021, it is not permitted to credit the proceeds arising from debt securities listed in foreign currency or an Initial Public Offering of foreign currency denominated shares or payment of dividends or any other distribution in foreign currency, to a Business Foreign Currency Account. Having considered the matters such as boosting the interest of foreign investors in Sri Lankan listed Companies, attracting foreign currency inflows and increasing the number of participants, limiting pressure on the Sri Lankan Rupee and creating an alternative for reaching foreign share markets by the Sri Lankan Companies to raise foreign funds, the Monetary Board of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka has recommended the implementation of the proposal made by the Colombo Stock Exchange. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to issue an Order under section 7 (1) of Foreign Exchange Act, No.12 of 2017 amending the Regulation No.02 of 2021 currently issued to provide for the necessary provisions to implement the said proposal and to submit the same in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining Financial Assistance from the Asian Development Bank for 'Responsive COVID-19 Vaccines for Recovery Project' (RECOVER)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-28
decision_details_body: - The Government of Sri Lanka has planned to obtain a loan of US$ 150 million from the Asian Development Bank to implement the 'Responsive COVID-19 Vaccines for Recovery' (RECOVER) Project. Of the said sum, it is expected to obtain US$ 84 million under the Asia Pacific Vaccine Access Facility (APVAX) and the balance of US$ 66 million under the regular country allocation of the Ordinary Capital Resources of the Asian Development Bank. The total cost of the project is US$ 161.85 million and US$ 11.85 million will be incurred by the Government of Sri Lanka. It has been planned to use the said loan for some other associated activities including meeting the cost of vaccines, establishing vaccine related monitoring systems, providing cold chain related transport facilities and strengthening the medical waste management. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to pursue future action to obtain the said loan, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendments to the Immigrants and Emigrants Act for revision of the existing visa period with regard to the process of issuing visas of the Department of Immigration and Emigration
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-28
decision_details_body: - In view of amending the Immigrants and Emigrants Act to revise the existing visa period with regard to the process of issuing visas of the Department of Immigration and Emigration, H. E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence submitted a proposal previously to the Cabinet to publish the draft Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman in the Government Gazette and submit the same in Parliament for approval. The Minister of Justice was requested at the Cabinet meeting held on 2021 04 05 to study the matters pertaining to the said Bill and submit further amendments, if any, to the Cabinet. As such, the Minister of Justice has conducted discussions with the relevant stakeholders and it has been recommended to the Cabinet that it would be appropriate to pass the relevant Bill in Parliament as it is. Having considered the said recommendation, the proposal made by H. E. the President through the Cabinet Memorandum dated 2021 02 23 to publish the draft Bill prepared for amending the Immigrants and Emigrants Act in the Government Gazette and submit the same in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendments to the Dangerous Animals Ordinance
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-28
decision_details_body: - The Sub Committee for Criminal Law Reforms of the Special Unit of the Ministry of Justice has recommended that the Dangerous Animals Ordinance should be amended to suit the present needs. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to take necessary action to amend the Dangerous Animals Ordinance, No.38 of 1921, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of the National Aquaculture Development Authority of Sri Lanka Act, No.53 of 1998
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-28
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2017 08 15 to amend the National Aquaculture Development Authority of Sri Lanka Act, No.53 of 1998 to grant wide powers of regulation, promotion and management of the aquaculture, to the Director of the National Aquaculture Development Authority of Sri Lanka. Accordingly, the Minister in charge of the subject has appointed a Committee to study the matters pertaining to the amendments to be made and submit recommendations. The said Committee has submitted proposals relating to amending the said Act and pursuant to the said proposals, it has been recommended to amend the National Aquaculture Development Authority of Sri Lanka Act, No.53 of 1998 and also concurrently, the Fisheries & Aquatic Resources Act, No.2 of 1996 amended by the Act, No.22 of 2006. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Fisheries to amend the National Aquaculture Development Authority of Sri Lanka Act, No.53 of 1998 and the Fisheries & Aquatic Resources Act, No.2 of 1996 concurrently, based on the draft prepared by the Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Accommodating Companies incorporated in Sri Lanka to invest in the Sri Lanka International Sovereign Bonds
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-28
decision_details_body: - Several Licensed Commercial Banks and few Companies registered in Sri Lanka have expressed their willingness to borrow from outside Sri Lanka in order to invest in the Sri Lanka International Sovereign Bonds. Having considered the overall benefit to the country, the Monetary Board of Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) has agreed to permit Licensed Commercial Banks, the National Savings Bank and non financial corporates registered under the Companies Act, No.7 of 2007 from time to time, to purchase Sri Lanka International Sovereign Bonds/Sri Lanka Development Bonds subject to certain conditions. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to promulgate regulations under section 7 (1) of the Foreign Exchange Act, No.12 of 2017 for facilitating the non financial corporates registered under the Companies Act, No.7 of 2007 to pursue action accordingly and to submit the said regulations in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Further extension of the Order issued under Section 22 of the Foreign Exchange Act, No.12 of 2017 for controlling the foreign exchange outflows
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-28
decision_details_body: - Having considered the potential negative impact on the foreign currency reserves and foreign exchange market in the country due to the COVID 19 pandemic, Orders have been made under section 22 of the Foreign Exchange Act, No.12 of 2017 in view of suspending outward remittances related to certain transactions. The period of validity of the said Orders is due to be expired on 2021 07 01 and it is the view of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka that the said Orders should further continue in order to minimize the potential risk in the foreign exchange market and to maintain the stability of the financial system. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to further extend the Orders made under section 22 of the Foreign Exchange Act, No.12 of 2017 imposing certain limitations/restrictions on foreign exchange outward remittances, for a period of six (06) months from 2021 07 02, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Making provisions for granting an additional interest for Special Deposit Accounts
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-28
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted previously to open Special Deposit Accounts with effect from 2020 04 07 to encourage inflow of foreign exchange to Sri Lanka and to pay an additional interest to further detain the deposits of such accounts. Accordingly, relevant regulations have been issued under the provisions of the Foreign Exchange Act No.12 of 2017, and under the existing provisions it is also possible to rollover the special deposit accounts operated with a tenure of 06 months or 12 months and to grant an additional interest for such Special Deposit Accounts. However no provisions are available to pay an additional interest for the Special Deposit Accounts which have been rolledover exceeding the period of 12 months and therefore, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, to impose regulations incorporating provisions required for the purpose in terms of the section 7(1) of the Foreign Exchange Act No.12 of 2017 and thereafter present the said regulations for approval in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Provision of requisites for the religious places which are facing difficulties in obtaining them
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-28
decision_details_body: - The Ministry Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs has designed a programme to provide dry rations to the religious places that have been found difficult to secure requisites from their lay devotees due to the Covid - 19 pandemic and the constant travel restrictions imposed as a result. Therefore, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs to distribute the parcels of dry rations worth of Rs.5000/- purchased from Lanka Sathosa Limited to selected temples and religious places through the delivery unit of the said institution, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Facilitation for the legal procedure regarding the maritime disaster caused by the fire at MV X-press Pearl
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-28
decision_details_body:
- In order to facilitate for the legal procedure regarding the maritime disaster caused by the fire at MV X-press Pearl, a consultation programme has been initiated by the Minister of Justice under the guidance of H.E the President and with the participation of other relevant ministers. Accordingly, following measures have been taken under the said programme:

* 	Five Sub-Committees have been appointed to asses the damage caused by the fire in order to obtain insurance claims.

* 	Newspaper advertisements have been published in all the three languages regarding insurance claims and information.

* 	The Attorney General has taken legal action against the Ship Owner, Captain and the Board of Directors of the Local Agent at the Colombo High Court.

* 	A committee has been appointed to investigate on the deaths of marine animals under the chairmanship of the Secretary, State Ministry of Wildlife Protection, Adoption of Safety Measures including the Construction of Electrical Fences and Trenches and Reforestation and Forest Resources Development.

* 	Expression of Interests have been called to select a suitable legal firm since the service of law experts in the relevant field is essential for the future legal proceedings and accordingly 08 international legal firms have expressed their interest.

* 	The London P & I Club has agreed to pay Rs.720 million as an interim compensation at a discussion conducted with insurer of the said vessel by the Attorney General.

	Accordingly, the Cabinet decided to grant its concurrence for the above measures taken by the consultation process which is functioning under the chairmanship of the Minister of Justice and to appoint a Committee comprising of senior officials for selecting the most suitable law firm from among the firms who have expressed their interests for providing consultation.

description: National Level media programme to make aware of the importance of production and use of organic and natural fertilizer
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-28
decision_details_body: - The Government has taken a policy decision to utilize organic and natural fertilizer for agricultural purposes instead of using chemical fertilizer. Therefore, it has been found necessary to launch an accelerated awareness programme to make understand the actual situation to the farmers and other parties who believe in chemical fertilizer as the only alternative to increase crop production, to widen the knowledge of the farmers on the use of organic fertilizer and to inspire the promotion of organic and natural fertilizer as well as environmental friendly programmes. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture to implement awareness programmes through the use of audio, video, printed and digital media to make aware the youths including the farmer community and other relevant stakeholders, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Re-acquisition of the land belonging to the BCC Lanka Company Limited allocated for the re-establishment of Welikada Prison
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-28
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2016 06 27 to remove the Welikada prison from the said land premise and relocate it in a land in extent of 06 acres 03 roods and 8.77 perches belonging to the BCC Lanka Company Limited. However, at present the Government has taken a policy decision to re-establish the Welikada prison in a building complex constructed in a land located at Horana which belongs to the Urban Development Authority. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries with the consent of the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing to utilize the land by the BCC Lanka Company Limited to carry out its further development activities, adhering to the development plan made by the Urban Development Authority, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing relief to the entities in the tourism sector affected by the Covid-19 pandemic
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-28
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted previously to the proposals made by the task force comprising of employers, representatives of workers' trade unions, officials of the Ministry of Labour and the Department of Labour with the objective of providing relief for the continuation of entities affected by the Covid - 19 pandemic and keeping the jobs of workers intact. Accordingly, granting proportionate opportunities so as to ensure that each employee receive opportunity to work, payment of 50% of the basic salary of the month in which the employee last received his full salary or Rs.14,500/-, whichever is more favorable to the employee, in case the employees are asked to stay at home and payment of contributions to the Employees' Provident Fund and the Employees Trust Fund from the salary so paid will be implemented until the end of June 2021. With the impose of international aviation restrictions around the world, it has not been able to keep the tourism sector into normalcy, in particular, and therefore the Cabinet decided to grant its concurrence to the measures taken by the Minister of Labour to further implement the relief measures already granted to the entities in the tourism sector until the end of December 2021 from July 2021.

description: Japanese Grant Aid for Human Resources Development Scholarship Programme - 2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-28
decision_details_body: - The Government of Japan launches the “Japanese Grant Aid for Human Resources Development Scholarship Programme” since 2010 in order to provide opportunities to the executive level public sector officials to undergo Master Degree Programmes in prominent universities in Japan. Under this programme, 180 opportunities for Master Degree Programmes and 08 opportunities for PhD programmes have been provided to Sri Lanka. The Government of Japan has agreed to provide a grant of Japanese Yen 271 million (approximately Rs.488 million) for the group of executive officers scheduled to be commenced their studies in September 2021. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, to sign Exchange of Notes to obtain that grant aid and to enter into an Agreement with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) to implement the said programme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Restructuring of the Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) Industry in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-21
decision_details_body:
- The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2021‑06‑07 decided to appoint a Cabinet Sub-Committee chaired by the Minister of Trade to obtain recommendations pertaining to restructuring of the Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) Industry in Sri Lanka. Accordingly, the Cabinet granted approval to implement the following recommendations submitted by the Cabinet Sub-Committee based on the outcome of the discussions heldwith the representatives from the Gas companies in Sri Lanka, relevant Government Institutions and Banks and the experts in the field.

    • Continue selling a 12.5kg domestic gas cylinder at a price of Rs 1,493/- by the Litro Gas Limitedand LAUGFS Gas PLC as currently determined by the Consumer Affairs Authority. 
      
    • Purchasing, transporting and storing of gas by both companies jointly and using the Hambanthota Gas Terminal for that.
      
    • Appointing a Committee comprising of officials with expertise knowledge in the field including representatives from the Litro Gas Ltd and LAUGFS Gas PLC for maintaining the procurement process of purchasing gas required to the country and transporting and storing same in a proper manner.

    • Implementing themethodology recommended by the Sub-Committee within next 06 months and take future action upon outcome of the same.

description: Declaration of the “National Energy Day”
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-21
decision_details_body: - A national programme including various activities to enhance the knowledge, attitudes and creativity of school children on sustainable energy has been planned by the Ministry of Power, Ministry of Energy, Ministry of Education together with the State Ministry of Solar Power,Wind and Hydro Power Generation Projects Development. Simultaneously, it has been proposed to declare 26th of June as the “National Energy Day” annually, taking into account the 26th of June, 1882, the date on whichSri Lankans first saw the light emanating from an electric lamp at the time that the German vessel SS Helios arrived at the Colombo Harbour. Accordingly, the joint proposal made by the Minister of Power and the Minister of Energy to declare 26th of June at each year as the “National Energy Day” and to implement the proposed programme to make school children aware from 26th June to 26th Junein the following year and to culminate in an award ceremony, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No. 15 of 1979 (Pre trial Procedure)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-21
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2018‑02‑14 granted approval to introduce amendments to the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No. 15 of 1979 with a view to introducing new provisions pertaining to the conduct of Pre-trial conferences in the High Courts. Accordingly, the clearance of the Attorney General has been received to the draft Bill so prepared by the Legal Draftsman as per the said Cabinet approval. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to publish the said draft Bill in the Government Gazette and to submit the same thereafter in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Timely strengthening of existing Legal Framework for streamlining the fertilizer management and regulation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-21
decision_details_body: - The Regulation of Fertilizer Act No.68 of 1988 has been introduced to regulate the manufacture, preparation, import and distribution of fertilizer and to make provisions for the matters related thereto. Issues have been arisen as certain provisions of the said Act are not adequate and do not meet the present day requirements. Especially, since the necessary action has been taken to implement the use of organic fertilizer throughout the country as per the Government's Policy Statement “Vistas of Prosperity and Splendour”, it has been found necessary to include provisions related to that in the said Act. Accordingly,the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture to take necessary action to introduce a new Act in place of the the Regulation of Fertilizer Act No.68 of 1988, incorporating provisions to suit the present day needs , was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendments to the Consumer Affairs Authority Act No.9 of 2003
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-21
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2018‑09‑03 granted approval to draft a Bill to amend the Consumer Affairs Authority Act. Accordingly, the Attorney General has pointed out the need to formalize the draft Bill so prepared. Moreover, the Ministry of Trade has identified the provisions required to be incorporated further to thesaid Bill as per the present day needs. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade to take necessary action to get prepared the said draft Bill by the Legal Draftsman, incorporating the identified provisions, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendments to the Sri Lanka Telecommunications Act, No.25 of 1991
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-21
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Telecommunications Act, No.25 of 1991 and the relevant amendments operative at present have provided the Telecommunication Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka (TRCSL) with the powers only for the regulation of telecommunication. Even though the Legal Draftsman's Department has drafted a basic draft for amending the said Act, the necessity of further amending the said draft to suit the present needs has been recognized. Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Technology to draft a Bill to amend the Sri Lanka Telecommunications (Amendment) Act, No. 25 of 1991 incorporating the necessary provisions, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the Advisory Councils for Strengthening and Promoting Local Industries
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-21
decision_details_body: - The absence of proper coordination among Line Ministries, other relevant institutions and the representatives of the Industry Sector has caused issues and unnecessary delays in the process of formulation and implementation of policies. Even though there is a possibility of setting up of an Advisory Council on Industries in terms of the provisions of the Industrial Promotion Act, No. 46 of 1990 in view of establishing coordination among the relevant stakeholders, necessary action has not yet been taken for the purpose accordingly. Necessary Action is being taken to amend the Industrial Promotion Act, No. 46 of 1990 incorporating the appropriate provisions to suit the present needs of the Industry Sector. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries to appoint Advisory Councils for 20 major industrial sectors comprising the Specialists representing Chambers/Federations in the said sector, Universities and Research Institutions and the Specialists in the relevant Industrial Sector until the said amendments are to be introduced, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Transferring the title of the Kurunduwatte land located in Ekala, Ja-Ela, enjoyed by the Sri Lanka Transport Board as a Free Grant
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-21
decision_details_body: - Even though the possession of the Ekala Estate in the Kurunduwatte land 23 acres 01 rood 16.5 perches in extent, located in Ekala, Ja-Ela in the Ja-Ela Divisional Secretariat Division has been given away to the Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB) in the year 2017 in terms of the provisions of Section 44 of the Land Acquisition Act, it has not yet been transferred to the said Board by way of a Free Grant. The warehouses of the Ja-Ela Depot are being maintained in one part of this land which has been enjoyed by the Sri Lanka Transport Board for a period of nearly 50 years and manufacturing of bus bodies and some other projects of Lakdiva Engineering Company (Pvt) Limited take place in another block of land in extent of 17 acres, of this land. Lakdiva Engineering Company (Pvt) Limited has planned to establish and maintain a Repair and Service Centre for dilapidated vehicles of the Ministries and Departments. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport to transfer the above land to the Sri Lanka Transport Board as a free grant to enable the said land to be utilized for investment purposes of the Sri Lanka Transport Board and Lakdiva Engineering Company (Pvt) Limited including the said proposed project and to implement the same through a Public‑Private Partnership, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the University of Ruhuna and the Vellore Institute of Technology, India
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-21
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by the Minister of Education to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the University of Ruhuna and the Vellore Institute of Technology, India for higher education co‑operation by organizing student exchange programmes for undergraduate and postgraduate degree programmes, organizing academic staff exchange programmes for sharing mutual experience on teaching, research and practical training and implementing integrated research and development programmes inclusive of exchanging publications and reports etc:, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Annual Report – 2020 of the Ministry of Finance (Final Budget Position Report)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-14
decision_details_body: - The Annual Report (Final Budget Position Report) should be presented to Parliament and to the general public by the Minister of Finance prior to the lapse of 05 months after the end of financial year as indicated in Section 13 of the Fiscal Management (Responsibility) Act, No. 03 of 2003. Accordingly, the Annual Report - 2020 has been published on 2021‑05‑31.The Report provides an analysis of macroeconomic and socio-economic indicators, covering the areas such as fiscal policy, economic developments in 2020, global economic developments and monetary sectors, domestic demand and supply, investment and savings, developments in foreign and monetary sector and inflation including the measures taken to mitigate the impact of COVID-19 pandemic and its ramification effect on the economic variables. Further, it also includes a detailed analysis on final budget position including government revenue and expenditure, cash flow management, budget deficit financing and debt structure. As such the proposal made by Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to table the said Annual Report in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing a MRI (I.5T) Scanner to Apeksha Hospital, Maharagama
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-14
decision_details_body: - National Competitive Bids have been called for the procurement of Supply, Delivery, Installation, Commissioning and Maintenance of a MRI (I.5T) Scanner for Maharagama Apeksha Hospital. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to award the procurment of providing a MRI (I.5T) Scanner to M/s Technomedics International (Pvt) Ltd as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee and the recommendation made by the Procurement Appeal Board in that regard, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the term contract for the import of Murban Crude Oil
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-14
decision_details_body: - Bids have been invited from the registered suppliers of Ceylon Petroleum Corporation for the term contract for importing Murban Crude Oil for a period of 09 months from 2021‑06‑01 to 2022‑01‑31. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Energy to award the relevant contract to M/s Conscio Ltd, Nigeria as recommended by the Special Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the contract for the import of Gas Oil for a period of 08 months from 2021-06-01 to 2021-01-31
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-14
decision_details_body: - Bids have been invited from the registered suppliers of Ceylon Petroleum Corporation for the term contract for importing 1,137,500 Bbls of Gas Oil (0.05% maximum sulfur ) and 262,500 Bbls of Gas Oil (0.001% maximum sulfur) for a period of 08 months from 2021‑06‑01 to 2022‑01‑31. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Energy to award the relevant contract to M/s Petrochina International (Singapore) Pte. Ltd as recommended by the Special Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Purchasing textile necessary for the Government Institutions from the local manufactures at provincial level
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-14
decision_details_body: - Invading the domestic market by sub-standard imports which are not subject to a standard quality and increase of the production cost due to importing 70% of raw materials of apparels have been identified as the problems faced by the local manufactures engaged in the textile and local apparel industry. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries as per the recommendation of the State Minister of Batik, Handloom Fabric and Local Apparel Products to make provisions for the purchase of batik, handloom and local apparel required for the government institutions located in each provinces from local manufactures in the same area and for purchasing from the manufacturers in any other province, in case the required quantity cannot be met by the said manufacturers, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of Mannar Wind Power Plant
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-14
decision_details_body: - 	The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2019‑01‑29 granted approval to add wind power capacity of 60 MW for five substations located in Trincomalee, Mannar, Madampe, Bolawatta and Kappalthurai. Accordingly, International Competitive Bids have been invited for the construction of Wind Power Plant for Mannar Grid Substation and for connecting the same to the transmission network, under that project. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Power to award the contract for the construction of the relevant Wind Power Plant and connecting the same to the transmission network of Mannar Grid Substation to M/s Hiruras Power (Pvt) Ltd on Built-Own-Operate basis for an operational period of 20 years as recommended by the Cabinet Appointed Negotiating Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of Small Claims Courts
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-14
decision_details_body:
- Since the delay in functioning of law has reached a breaking point in Sri Lanka, a complete and widespread reform with planned and a focused approach is found to be required to focus on the issues causing delay of law and to revitalize and strengthen the process of the administration of justice. Accordingly, the Minister of Justice has appointed a committee under the chairmanship of Hon. Justice Dr. Ruwan Fernando, Judge of the Court of Appeal for studying in regard to the establishment of Pre-trial and Small Claims Court. Considering the recommendations submitted by the said Committee, the Cabinet approved the proposals made by the Minister of Justice to pursue action as follows.

*	Amendment to the Judicature Act No. 2 of 1978 securing provisions required to Small Claims Courts.

* 	Formulation of a draft bill enabling to introduce of new laws to make  provisions for special procedure of Small Claims Courts.

description: Amendment to the Civil Procedure Code
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-14
decision_details_body: - It has been identified the necessity of amending the provisions in Chapter XVI of the Civil Procedure Code for formalizing the appointment and monitoring of sworn translators and also to clear the ambiguity in the existing provisions. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to amend the sections 118, 119 and 120 of Chapter XVI of the Civil Procedure Code and to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft legislation for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Commencing negotiations between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh for entering into a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-14
decision_details_body: - Both Sri Lanka and Bangladesh function as the stakeholder member countries of the SAARC Preferential Trade Agreement (SAPTA), the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA), the Global System of Trade Preferences (GSTP), and the Asia Pacific Trade Agreement (APTA) and the proposed Agreement on Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC). Although there are special provisions provided under the said agreements, the trade between two countries remains to be minimal. During the official visit made by the Hon. Prime Minister to Bangladesh during last March, leaders of the both countries acknowledged the necessity of entering into a Free Trade Agreement between the Countries immediately. Further, both countries agreed upon to explore the possibility of entering into a Preferential Trade Agreement with a short list of products. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade for conducting negotiations with the relevant authorities with regard to entering into a preferential trade agreement with Bangladesh, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Upgrading selected District General Hospitals administered by Provincial Councils under the administration of the Ministry of Health
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-14
decision_details_body: - The Government has planned to upgrade one selected hospital in each district providing facilities such as medical treatment, surgical theatres and laboratories similar to that of the National Hospital of Sri Lanka at present. Accordingly, the district general hospitals Matale, Nawalapitiya, Embilipitiya, Awissawelle, Gampaha, Mannar, Vavuniya, Killinochchi and Mullaitivu administered by Provincial Councils at present and coming under the category of tertiary care hospitals have been identified to be taken under the purview of the Ministry of Health for enhancing their quality, equality, and efficiency of service delivery as well as for the smooth administration thereof. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health for taking over those district general hospitals under the purview of the Ministry of Health in order to accomplish those objectives, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Hosting of the 16th Session of the UNESCO Intergovernmental Committee Meeting for Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) from 13th to 18th December 2021 in Colombo, Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-14
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka is a state party of the UNESCO Convention for Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage and at present, it is a member of its Intergovernmental Committee. Sri Lanka has been privileged to host the 16th session of that Intergovernmental Committee scheduled to be held in Colombo from 13th to 18th December 2021. It is expected that approximately1000 foreign representatives including a delegation of 30 members from the UNESCO Secretariat with the Director General of UNESCO and representatives and delegation from 195 Member States will be present here for the relevant session. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to carry out future activities as per the Work Plan prepared for hosting this session, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Progress of Mega Scale Development Projects by the end of the First Quarter - 2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-14
decision_details_body: - 284 Mega Scale Development Projects exceeding Rupees one billion of estimated cost are being implemented under 41 ministries at present whereas Rupees 692.5 billion has been allocated for the year 2021, to carry out those projects. 53 projects from among them are related to the priority development targets of the Government such as “drinking water for all” and “development of 100,000 km road network”. The Cabinet noted the report regarding the progress of these projects at the end of first quarter of 2021 submitted by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance informing the necessity of integrating all the relevant institutions in order to achieve specific investment targets of those projects and resolving procedural and legal issues relating to the land acquisition which directly affects on the performance of certain projects.

description: Purchasing and distribution of surplus stocks of vegetables and fruits by the Government that the farmers are unable to sell during the period of prevailing COVID-19 travel restrictions
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-07
decision_details_body: - It has been clear that the small and medium scale farmers as well as large scale farmers face a major economic crisis due to the destruction of their products especially, vegetables and fruits for not being able to be transported and traded in a normal way because of the travel restrictions imposed by the Government island‑wide. Further, consumers also have faced a scarcity of proper vegetables and fruits at a fair price. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture to implement a Programme to purchase the stocks of vegetables and fruits that could not be sold during the period of travel restrictions, by the District Secretaries/Government Agents at the prices of the District Price Committee and provide the stocks of vegetables and fruits so purchased free of charge, to COVID Treatment Centres, all Government Hospitals, Tri‑Forces, Displaced Camps and families who have lost their livelihoods, as found necessary, until the travel restrictions will be lifted, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Sale of essential food items which are not released from the Port and confiscated by the Sri Lanka Customs, to the general public at a concessionary price by Lanka Sathosa Ltd.
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-07
decision_details_body: - A system to provide essential food items to the general public at an affordable price without any shortage under the prevailing COVID‑19 pandemic situation is already implemented by Lanka Sathosa Ltd. As such, the joint proposal made by the Minster of Trade and the Minister of Ports & Shipping to take necessary action to provide the essential food items confiscated by the Sri Lanka Ports Authority and the Sri Lanka Customs to Lanka Sathosa Ltd., enabling to further maintain the said System effectively, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing houses to the families to be affected by the Four Lane Elevated Highway Construction Project from the New Kelani Bridge to Athurugiriya
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-07
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted to implement the Four Lane Elevated Highway Construction Project from the New Kelani Bridge to Athurugiriya. The need for providing alternative housing facilities to 1,100 families including the families and sub‑families of unauthorized occupants living in those lands so acquired for the project and the families living in lands less than the extent of 06 perches and those families who are unauthorized occupants of the land where the Dematagoda sports ground is to be constructed, as well has been identified. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Highways to provide houses to the said 1,100 families from the housing schemes in Kolonnawa, Henamulla and Maligawatta implemented by the Urban Development Authority, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Orders issued under the Sri Lanka Export Development Act, No.40 of 1979
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-07
decision_details_body: - An Order has been issued under the Sri Lanka Export Development Act, No.40 of 1979 to amend the CESS duty on importation of tiles and ceramic sanitary fittings. The said Order has been published in the Extraordinary Gazette Notification No.2219/15 dated 2021‑03‑15 and the proposal made by the Minister of Trade to submit the said Order in Parliament for approval as per the provisions of this Act, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Securities and Exchange Commission of Sri Lanka Bill
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-07
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2020‑10‑26 to draft the Securities and Exchange Commission of Sri Lanka Bill. As such, the Bill drafted by the Legal Draftsman has also received the clearance of the Attorney General. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to publish the said Bill in the Government Gazette and submit the same thereafter in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the Export Agro Value Chain Development Industrial Zone at Mahaheentenna area in Elpitiya
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-07
decision_details_body: - It has been identified that there is a potential of gaining market opportunities and entering into high standard markets by enhancing value added products in the field of export agriculture thereby fetching a higher amount of foreign exchange to this country. In view of facilitating such projects, it has been planned to establish an Export Agro Value Chain Development Industrial Zone in a land of 64 acres in extent belonging to the Land Reforms Commission, at the area of Mahaheentenna in Elpitiya. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Plantation to evaluate the business viability under the Agriculture Sector Modernization Project which operates at present, as the first phase of this project and give away blocks of land to 14 recognized agricultural entrepreneurs to commence projects and to appoint a Committee headed by the Secretary to the State Ministry in‑charge of the subject for selecting agricultural entrepreneurs under the second phase of the project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of a pilot project to manufacture organic fertilizer at Divisional Secretariat Division level in the North Central Province
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-07
decision_details_body: - Since the Government has already taken measures to ban the use of chemical fertilizer for Agriculture, it is essential to prepare an appropriate programme for ensuring a sufficient supply of organic fertilizer by increasing the production of the same by the start of the comming Maha season in the month of September. Therefore, a project has been planned to implement an organic fertilizer production project having secured essential fundamental capital from the fund of the Land Reform Commission, so that manufactured organic fertilizer can be purchased by the Ministry of Agriculture and then distribute among the farmers. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Lands to implement the proposed pilot project by establishing at least one organic fertilizer centre at each Divisional Secretariat division covering 29 Divisional Secretariat divisions in the districts of Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa where agriculture is done in abundance by obtaining the required raw materials from the said areas, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Special Programme to provide investment opportunities for business development and set up industries at Divisional Secretariat level in island wide
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-07
decision_details_body: - The Ministry of Industries together with the Ministry of Youth & Sports have planned to implement an industry and enterprise development programme at divisional secretariat division level with the objective of minimizing the regional imbalance of development, maximizing the use of rural resources as well as encouraging entrepreneurs in the industrial sector who expect to generate employment opportunities in rural areas. Under this, it has been planned to implement at least one project at each Divisional Secretariat division with the intention of promoting especially the small and medium scale enterprises thereby increasing the employment generation having created a network of strong entrepreneurship at rural level, promoting value - added productions utilizing resources/raw-materials dispersed at divisional level, while promoting exports and encouraging import substitutes. Accordingly, the Cabinet approved the joint proposal made by the Minister of Industries and the Minister of  Youth & Sports to encourage and provide facilities to the entrepreneurs/investors who are investing at least Rs.100 million and  promoting the inauguration of industries/ enterprises that generate at least 50 employment opportunities in the field and encouraging the existing industries/ enterprises.

description: Entering into Memoranda of Understanding between Sri Lankan Universities and Foreign Universities aiming at Educational Collaboration
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-07
decision_details_body:
- The Cabinet approved the proposals made by the Minister of Education, to enter into following Memoranda of Understanding, with the objective of improving the educational collaboration with foreign universities for elevating the universities of this country to a higher level in the world university rankings in accordance with the Government Policy Framework.

	* The Memorandum of Understanding between the University of Sri Jayewardenepura and the Manipal School of Life Sciences, Manipal Academy of  Higher Education, India for Joint Collaborative Activities.

* The Memorandum of Understanding between the University of Peradeniya and the SAARC Agriculture Centre for Joint Collaborative Technological Collaborative Activities.

* The Memorandum of Understanding between the University of Colombo and the University of Malaya,Malayasia.

* The Memorandum of Understanding between the University Grants Commission (UGC) of Sri Lanka and the Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency of Australia for Information Exchange, cooperation in Quality Assurance and Networking of Institutes.

* The Memorandum of Understanding between the Agricultural Extension, Faculty of Agriculture of the University of Peradeniya and the Faculty of Extension, University of Alberta, Canada.

description: Hundred Cities Beautification Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-07
decision_details_body: - Certain second and third order towns located all over the country keep to be unpleasant and disorderly towns that are oppressive for the public due to the haphazard development and those towns can be converted into people friendly and pleasant towns by taking action in keeping with an organized plan and a programme. Therefore, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development and Housing for the implementation of a programme called “Siyak Nagara” with the assistance of all the Government sector institutions and all other parties entrusted with the supply of infrastructure facilities for the purpose of orderly beautification of 100 such recognized cities located all over the island by enhancing their initial facilities, through the Urban Development Authority, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Drafting a National Cultural Policy
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-06-07
decision_details_body: - In the year 2007, a National Cultural Policy has been formulated and Gazetted for the first time. Although approval of the Cabinet was granted in the year 2017 to prepare a National Arts and Cultural Policy by further amending the said National Cultural Policy, actions have not been taken in pursuant with the said decision. Therefore, the need has arisen for a National Cultural Policy as applicable to the present context. Accordingly, the Proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of  Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs, to prepare a new National Cultural Policy having further amended the existing policy, and to appoint a committee comprising of expertise of relevant field representing all the cultures, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Importation of natural organic fertilizer and chelated mineral micro 	nutrient for Maha Season 2021/2022
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-31
decision_details_body:
- The Government has taken steps to ban the use and import of chemical fertilizers, pesticides and herbicides to promote the use of organic fertilizers in the country. Accordingly, the Ministry of Agriculture has identified the need to take immediate action to supply the required organic fertilizer for the 2021/2022 Maha Season. At present there are 27 domestic organic fertilizer manufacturers licensed by the National Fertilizer Secretariat and considering the production capacity of ten of them, it is possible to supply organic fertilizer locally for 224,000 hectares for the 2021/2022 Maha Season and to manufacture the required organic fertilizer for another 100,000 hectares subsequently to make available of the required facilities for the identified farmers. Therefore, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture for taking action as follows.

*  Appointing a Special Procurement Committee relating to the procurement of  organic fertilizer, natural minerals and chelated mineral micro nutrient and a Technical Committee comprising of the expertise on the relevant field to assist the Procurement Committee.
* Import required organic fertilizer and natural mineral through Government Owned Fertilizer Companies for 500,000 hectares of paddy cultivation for Maha Season 2021/2022 following the international competitive bidding procedure and distributing them through the Department of Agrarian Development.
*  Import the organic fertilizer required to cultivate  600,000 hectares of the other crops through the licensed companies that have permission to import fertilizer adhering to the recommendations of the relevant research institutions and distributing them to the relevant farmers.
* Import identified specific fertilizers for ornamental plants, cut flower and foliage cultivations through the Import License Method adhering to the recommendations of the research institutes of the relevant crops and distributing them to the relevant farmers.

description: Granting “Guru Abhimani” allowance for pre-school teachers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-31
decision_details_body: - The Government National Policy Framework “Vistas of Prosperity and Splendor” has identified pre-school teachers as significant stakeholders of human resources development and has paid special attention on giving them a certain training and providing a permanent allowance.
