Accordingly, it has been identified that it is appropriate to increase the allowance of Rs.250/= presently being paid to pre-school teachers up to Rs.2500/=. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to increase the present allowance of Rs.250/= to Rs.2500/= for eligible pre-school teachers under identified criteria to be effective 2021‑06‑01 and provide the said allowance to 25,000 pre-school teachers as its first phase, was approved by the Cabinet of Ministers.

description: Construction of  a new Police Headquarters Complex
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-31
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Police Headquarters which is presently maintained in 03 buildings of more than 100 years old has been constructed in a land located in between the York Street and the Chethiya road. Since the building premises is not spacious enough, civil administration office and several other divisions of the Police Headquarters are maintained at rented out buildings. Although, the approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2011‑07‑11 to construct the Police Headquarters Complex at Mirihana, necessary measures have not been taken accordingly. Under these circumstances, the land in extent of 14 acres 02 roods and 38.50 belonging to the Sri Lanka Police at No 142, Bellantota Junction, Attidiya Road has been found suitable to construct the Police Headquarters Complex. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Public Security to construct the Police Headquarters Complex in the said land belonging to the Sri Lanka Police instead of constructing in Mirihana  and to identify the required buildings as separate projects according to the requirements and carry out relevant procurement procedures, was approved in principle by the Cabinet.

description: Selection of Ground Handling Agents for SriLankan Airlines Limited
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-31
decision_details_body:
- Limited international bids have been called for the selection of ground handling service providers for the SriLankan Airlines Ltd. (SLA) at the Bangkok International Airport and  at the London Heathrow International Airport. Accordingly, the proposal made by the  Minister of Tourism to award the following contracts for a period of 03 years as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet. 

		* Awarding the contract for the ground handling services supply of the  	 	   Bangkok International Airport to Bangkok Flight Services.

		* Awarding the contract for the passenger and ramp handling services of the  	   London Heathrow International Airport to Dnata Limited.

		* Awarding the contract for the cargo handling services of the London 	 	   Heathrow International Airport to Worldwide Flight Services (WFS)Ltd.

description: Awarding term contracts for fuel purchasing
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-31
decision_details_body:
- The Cabinet approved the  proposals made by the Minister of Energy to award the following term contracts relating to the purchase of fuel for the period of eight months from 2021‑06‑01 to 2022‑01‑31 as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee. 

		*Awarding the term contract for the import of 2,700,000+10/-5% of 		  Gasoline (92 Unl) to M/s Swiss Singapore Overseas Enterprises Pte. 		  Ltd., 	Singapore.

		*Awarding the term contract for the Single Berth Delivery of 			1,120,000+10/-5% Bbls of Gas oil (0.05% of maximum sulphur) at 			SPM Muthurajawela to M/s Petrochina International (Singapore) Pte. 		Ltd., Singapore.


		*Awarding the term contract for the import of 1,341,000+10/-5% of 		  Gasoline (92 Unl) and 459,000+10/-5% of Gasoline (95 Unl) to M/s 		Petrochina International (Singapore) Pte. Ltd., Singapore.

		*Awarding the term contract for the for 	Duel Berth Discharge of		1,120,000+10/-5% Bbls of Gas oil (0.05% of maximum sulphur) at 	Dolphin Tanker Berth (DTB) and SPM 	Muthurajawela, to 	M/s 	Petrochina International (Singapore) Pte. Ltd., Singapore.

description: Procurement of 32,000 vials of Bevacizumab Injection 100mg/4ml
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-31
decision_details_body: - International Competitive Bids have been invited for purchasing this medicine which is used for the treatment of certain types of cancers. 04 bids have been submitted in this regard and the proposal made by the Minister of Health to award the procurement of 32,000 vials of Bevacizumab Injection 100mg/4ml, at a sum of LKR 220.8 million, to M/s Medmart Pharma (Pvt) Ltd., as per the recommendation of the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of OPD, Administration Block and Ward Complex at the Lady Ridgeway Hospital for Children, Colombo
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-31
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by the Minister of Health to implement the project for construction of the OPD, Administration Block and Ward Complex at the Lady Ridgeway Hospital for Children, Colombo within the Medium Term Budgetary Framework 2022‑2024 and to obtain the labour contribution of the Sri Lanka Navy for the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Housing Project of Maliboda Estate - Deraniyagala
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-31
decision_details_body: - In response to a request made at the 'Gama Samaga Pilisandarak' program conducted by H. E. the President at Deraniyagala area, it has been proposed to implement a housing project for the estate workers in Maliboda area. It has been planned to construct 171 houses for the estate workers under the said project. The Government of India has also agreed to provide a grant of Rs.500 million for construction of 480 estate houses including the proposed houses in response to the request made by H. E. the President. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing to implement the project for constructing 171 housing units at Maliboda Estate under the proposed Indian Grant Scheme and to award the contract for constructing 60 houses as its first phase, to the State Engineering Corporation (SEC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of a Vessel Monitoring System (VMS) to comply with the local and international legal requirements
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-31
decision_details_body: - In accordance with the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission (IOTC) Resolution 15/03, it is essential to set up a Vessel Monitoring System (VMS) to identify the location of multi‑day fishing vessels at sea, to launch Search and Rescue (SAR) Operations at disaster situations and to control illegal and unofficial fisheries activities carried out via maritime passages by using multi‑day fishing vessels. In 2015, a VMS using satellite technology was installed in 1,250 multi‑day fishing vessels registered under the Department of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (DFAR). In addition to the said fisheries vessels, 4,200 other such multi‑day fishing vessels are required to be fitted with the relevant devices. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Fisheries to take necessary action to install the said VMS through a procurement process conducted by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) by using a grant of Australian Dollar 5.38 million provided by the Department of Home Affairs (DOH) of Australia, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Payment of compensation to the people affected by the establishment of the Anuradhapura South and Anuradhapura North Multi-Transport Centres
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-31
decision_details_body: - The Anuradhapura Joint Urban Development project is carried out by the Ministry of Urban Development & Housing on the funds provided by the French Development Agency (AFD). The prime objective of this project is to improve urban services and public places in the city of Anuradhapura while preserving its cultural heritage. It has been planned under this project to develop the Anuradhapura new bus stand as the Anuradhapura South Multi‑Transport Centre and to remove the Anuradhapura old bus stand and the long distance service bus stand from those places and to develop the same as the Anuradhapura North Multi‑Transport Centre in close proximity to the Anuradhapura main Railway Station. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing to pay compensation to 302 families to be affected by the said projects subject to the relevant criteria, taking into consideration the nature of the impact, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of Regulations issued under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, No.1 of 1969, for approval in Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-31
decision_details_body: - In view of promoting the use of organic fertilizers for agricultural products, the Cabinet decided on 2021‑04‑27 to ban the importation of chemical fertilizers, pesticides and herbicides. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to submit the Imports and Exports (Control) Regulations promulgated under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, No.1 of 1969 pertaining to the implementation of the said Cabinet decision, for approval in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Purchase of Sinopharm and Oxford-AstraZeneca (OAZ) Vaccines
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-24
decision_details_body: - The required quantity of vaccines has to be obtained at the earliest in the circumstances where there is no other remedy to combat the COVID - 19 pandemic other than vaccination. The Government has planned to vaccinate 60 % - 70% of the overall population by the end of this year. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to take necessary action to purchase 14 million doses of Sinopharm Vaccine from the relevant manufacturer of China and 1 million doses of Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine expeditiously, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Accelerating treatments for COVID-19 patients
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-24
decision_details_body:
- The critically ill patients among the most of patients diagnosed under the third wave of COVID – 19 are required to be treated under oxygen concentrators. Accordingly, proposals made by the Minister of Health to take expeditious action as follows to ensure the medical oxygen supply for the critically ill patients, were approved by the Cabinet.  
	
    • Establishment of High Dependency Units with Wall Oxygen Outlets enabling to treat the critically ill patients in 25 Hospitals identified Provincial level covering the whole Island.
      
    • Installation of 15 Oxygen Concentrators in 15 identified hospitals located in remote areas to secure medical oxygen supply required for hospitals.
      
    • Providing 2500 Portable Oxygen Concentrators by 100 machines per each district thereby reducing the requirement of Cylinder-based oxygen supply. 
    • maintenance of adequate stock of Oxygen in the country having imported 120,000 litres of Liquefied Oxygen monthly in order to meet the increasing demand for medical Oxygen.

description: Construction of the Elevated Expressway connecting Athurugiriya Interchange and New Kelani Bridge
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-24
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2020‑04‑08 has granted approval to implement the Elevated Expressway connecting Athurugiriya Interchange and New Kelani Bridge on Built, Operate and Transfer (BOT) basis. Accordingly, Bids including technical and financial proposals have been invited from the relevant investors for the proposed project. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport to assign the task of implementing the said project to M/s China Harbor Engineering Corporation (CHEC) as recommended by the Cabinet Appointed Negotiating Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of Regulations issued under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, No.1 of 1969 in Parliament for approval
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-24
decision_details_body: - It has been observed that certain vehicle importers get a special advantage by registering the imported mobile workshops as dual purpose vehicles. Taking into account the recommendations made by the Committee on Public Accounts to that effect, Regulations to introduce a new Harmonized System Code (HS Code) to levy equal duty on mobile workshops and dual purpose vehicles and to allow to import them based on equal lifetime, have been published in the Gazette Notification dated 2020‑04‑23 as per the provisions of the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, No. 1 of 1969. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to submit the Regulations so published in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation Act No. 28 of 1961
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-24
decision_details_body: - Since some of the provisions of the the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation Act No. 28 of 1961 which are currently in force, are inadequate for the present-day requirements, the proposal made by the Minister of Energy to amend the said Act, incorporating the amendments identified for the same and to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a draft Bill for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of a fully equipped Haemodialysis Unit and Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) Clinic with NCD Screening facility at Colombo East Base Hospital, Mulleriyawa
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-24
decision_details_body: - Colombo East Base Hospital located at Mulleriyawa provides secondary healthcare facilities to a large number of people in Colombo district and the Hospital, at present, offers all major specialist consultation services in the fields of medicine, surgery, gynecology and obstetrics and pediatrics. Further, under the ongoing projects, it has been planned to establish new units of National Stroke Centre, Level 2 Accident and Emergency Unit, Intensive Care Unit (ICU), Neo-natal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) and Simulation Centre for this Hospital. In addition, it has been proposed to establish a dialysis unit with 12 dialysis machines and a fully equipped Haemodialysis Unit with necessary surgical equipment which can cater to 20 patients per day and a CKD clinic with Non Communicable Disease (NCD) screening facility, using a grant provided by the District 306 C1 of International Lions Clubs. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Health and the District 306 C1 of International Lions Club for the implementation of the said project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Open University of Sri Lanka and the Korea National Open University, South Korea
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-24
decision_details_body: - An agreement has been reached between the Open University of Sri Lanka and the Korea National Open University, South Korea to develop collaboration in the fields of open and distance education, capacity building, ICT applications, use of laboratory services, research and publications and staff exchange programmes. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to sign an MoU to that effect, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Introducing Guidelines for COVID-19 Emergency Procurement Procedure (CEPP)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-17
decision_details_body: - Due to the prevailing COVID‑19 situation, it has been recognized the need for simplifying the existing procurement procedure to procure the essential items required for the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Defence and the State Ministries within the purview of the said Ministries related to the health sector, without delay. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to amend the existing operational procurement procedure and issue new guidelines enabling to purchase vaccines, medical equipment, other medical requirements and essential items expeditiously, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of Land Acquisition (Payment of Compensation) Regulations - 2013
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-17
decision_details_body:
- Approval of the Cabinet has been granted to pay compensation for 20 identified projects under Land Acquisition and Resettlement Committee (LARC) and Land Acquisition and Resettlement Special Committee (SUPER LARC) systems and relevant regulations have been enacted for the purpose as per the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act. The Cabinet has granted approval to adopt the same system to pay compensation for the lands so acquired under the following projects:

i. 	Metro Colombo Urban Development project.
ii. 	Railway Track project from Kurunegala to Habarana via Dambulla.
iii. 	Strategic City Development Programmes.
iv. 	Grid Sub‑Stations and Transmission Lines project under the funds of the Asian Development Bank.

	As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Lands to submit the amended Land Acquisition (Payment of Compensation) Regulations‑ 2013 published in the Gazette dated 2021‑03‑18 for approval in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Conservation of the environment through promotion of Green Entrepreneurship
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-17
decision_details_body: - 	The Government Policy 'Vistas of Prosperity and Spelndour' has proposed to increase the total forest layer of the country up to 30%. Accordingly, 'Surakimu Ganga' National Environment Conservation Programme and 'Husma Dena Thuru' Tree Planting Programme are being implemented under the Ministry of Environment, through a number of stakeholders including Government Institutions, Private Sector, Non-Government Organizations (NGOs') and Voluntary Organizations islandwide. In view of meeting the sapling need of the said programmes and creating green entrepreneurs while encouraging the rural community, it has been planned to generate 650 new plant nursery operators all over Sri Lanka. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to provide a formal training to 650 low‑income families to be selected under the said programme as nursery plant operators and grant opportunity to function as green entrepreneurs, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Vesting a land belonging to the Department of Irrigation to the Institute of 	Indigenous Medicine, University of Colombo
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-17
decision_details_body: - The Department of Irrigation has extended its concurrence to transfer a land in extent of 0.1765 hectares located at No.330 of Dr.N.M Perera Road, Colombo 08, to the Institute of Indigenous Medicine. The Board of Management of the said Institute has decided to construct a multi-purpose building complex with 08 stories comprised of a clinical skills development laboratory and study hall, an indigenous food processing training centre with a restaurant and concurrence of the Urban Development Authority has been given for the purpose. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to transfer the said land to the  Institute of Indigenous Medicine, University of Colombo, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Granting insurance entitlements for Sri Lankan migrant workers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-17
decision_details_body: - A migrant worker insurance coverage had been made by the Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment for Sri Lankan migrant workers and compensations will paid through this cover subject to a maximum of Rs.600,000/-and Rs.400,000/- respectively in the event of death or permanent disability of a migrant worker. However, it does not provide any insurance coverage for industrial or domestic accidents caused, diseases and also for taking medical treatments for mental and health issues caused due to harassment or abuses by employers and for the loss of jobs due to the Covid-19 pandemic. Therefore,  the proposal made by the Minister of labour to introduce a suitable insurance coverage for Sri Lankan migrant workers taking into consideration the above facts, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of Welikada Prison Complex at Millewe, Horana and utilization of the premises of Welikada Prison for a Mixed Urban Development Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-17
decision_details_body: - The Welikada Prison Complex, located on a 42-acre land, is planned to be relocated on a land called Millewa Watta, Horana in extent of 200 acres. Taking into consideration the future needs, it has also been planned to construct a new prison complex on the said land and transfer the land on which the Welikada prison is located at present to the Urban Development Authority to grant the same to the formally selected local and foreign investors on long term lease basis to carry out development projects. Accordingly, proposals of the Memorandum submitted jointly by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development and Housing and the Minister of Justice to implement the proposed project, were approved by the Cabinet.

description: Investment Strategy and Policy Framework - Selendiva Investment (Pvt.) Ltd.
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-17
decision_details_body: - In accordance with the Cabinet approval granted on 2020‑03‑04 to form a state-owned Property Development Company with the objective of transforming the State-Owned Hospitality Portfolios to optimum performance level through appropriate restructuring, action was taken to establish the  Selendiva Investment (Pvt.) Ltd. with 100% ownership of the Treasury. State-owned Canwill Holdings (Pvt) Ltd., Hotel Developers (Lanka) PLC and Hotels Colombo Ltd have been vested in Selendiva Investment (Pvt.) Ltd at present. An Investment Facilitation Model based on Public Private Partnership has been planned by  Selendiva Investment (Pvt.) Ltd. with a view to facilitating the identified state-owned institutes and investments and under this, it has been identified to implement three (03) investment portfolios as 'Heritage Square in Colombo Fort', 'Real Estate Development' and 'State-Owned Hospitality Sector'. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development and Housing to take necessary action for the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Gazette Notification published under Sri Lanka Export 	Development Act No. 40 of 1979 to Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-10
decision_details_body: - Any good imported for any project with an investment of 50US$ million or more which implemented on 2019‑03‑06 or later has been exempted from CESS prior to the commencement of the commercial operations of that project. However, since some large scale projects commence its commercial operations in stages before the completion of the entire project, the relevant provisions for CESS exemption have not been made available for such projects. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade to submit the Gazette Notification No.2219/36 dated 2021‑03‑17 published under Sri Lanka Export Development Act No. 40 of 1979 imposing the provisions for CESS exemption of such projects as well, in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Project of Silting of Reservoirs controlled by the Sri Lanka Mahaweli 	Authority
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-10
decision_details_body: - Among the primary objectives of the construction of the Mahaweli Reservoirs, priority has been given to the supply of drinking water, providing water for agriculture and the generation of renewable energy. Nevertheless, the capacity of many of such reservoirs has been significantly reduced due to siltation, making it difficult to achieve the desired objectives of such reservoirs. It has been planned to implement a programme to remove silt and classify such silt in order to use them. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Irrigation to obtain a local or international Consultancy Service to prepare a basic feasibility report obtaining required data for surveying including all details pertaining to Polgolla, Victoria, Randenigala, Rantambe, Kalawewa and Bowathanna Reservoirs and to call for competitive bids nationally or internationally to select a suitable entity to remove silt in such reservoirs based on the above feasibility report, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing relief for continuing inter - provincial bus operations in the face of the COVID-19 pandemic
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-10
decision_details_body:
- Approval of the Cabinet of Ministers had been granted previously to grant relief identified for the continuation of inter-provincial bus operations in the face of the COVID-19 pandemic, up to 2021‑03‑31. Taking into consideration the fact that bus operations do not function properly as the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic still remains, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport to grant the following relief to the bus operators from 2021‑04‑01 to 2021‑09‑31, was approved by the Cabinet. 

    • Charging only 50% of annual tender fees.
    • Charging only 50% of the Expressway temporary permit fee.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Faculty of Technology, University of Jayewardenepura and the Tropical Biosphere Research Centre of University of Ryukyus, Japan
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-10
decision_details_body: - It has been agreed to enter into an MoU between the Faculty of Technology, University of Jayewardenepura and the Tropical Biosphere Research Centre of University of Ryukyus, Japan on collaboration in the field of inter-institutional research, development of innovation programmes, providing facilities to the staff and student exchange programmes and sharing experiences. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to enter into the said MoU, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into an Agreement with the University of Colombo and Taylor's University, Malaysia to implement a Research Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-10
decision_details_body: - The University of Colombo and Taylor's University, Malaysia have entered into an agreement to implement a Research Project on the extent and nature of unhealthy food and drink TV marketing using girls and boys across 09 countries in Asia. The International Development Research Center of Canada provides financial assistance to Taylor's University, Malaysia for the purpose. Accordingly, Taylor's University will arrange the financial provisions required for the functions discharged by the University of Colombo. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the implementation of the proposed project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Conservation and Sustainable use of the Muthurajawela Wetland Zone
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-10
decision_details_body:
- The Wetland eco-system associated with Muthurajawela, which is spread around an area of 6,232 hectares, consisting of the Negombo Lagoon and a Wetland area, supports immensely in preserving the environmental stability of the area and maintaining the socio‑economic well being of the urban population. The Master Plan jointly prepared by the Central Environmental Authority (CEA) and the the Greater Colombo Economic Commission in 1991 in view of protecting this Wetland Zone, has introduced 03 major land use patterns namely, Conservation Zone, Induction Zone and Mixed Urban Zone. Further, an area of 1,285.45 hectares of the zone has been designated by the Department of Wildlife Conservation as the Muthurajawela Sanctuary and another area of 162.1 hectares has been designated by the Central Environmental Authority as an Environmental Protection Area. However, the said eco‑system is now under a threat of extinction due to reasons such as irregular landfills that are still underway, creation of various infrastructure facilities in Wetlands, land acquisition for different purposes, unauthorized occupation of lands and dumping of garbage. Therefore, the joint proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing; the Minister of Wildlife & Forest Conservation and the Minister of Environment to take the following measures to ensure the long term sustainability of the said Wetland and the sustainable use of the said land, was approved by the Cabinet. 

* 	Preparation of a Master Plan expeditiously in line with present needs for the conservation and sustainable use of the Muthurajawela Wetland Zone.

* 	Appointment of a Steering Committee and a Working Committee comprising the Heads/agents of the relevant stakeholder institutions for the purpose.

* 	Acquisition of government/private lands as per the provisions of the Urban Development Authority Act, required for the implementation of an appropriate conservation mechanism as recommended by the Steering Committee.

* 	Assigning the responsibility of carrying out the activities pertaining to the sustainable use of the said eco‑system as a low lying area, to the Sri Lanka Land Development Corporation.

* 	Declaring the land areas that should be conserved as a National Reserve identified under the Master Plan, as a National Reserve under the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance.

* 	Taking necessary action to continue the Master Plan prepared by the Steering Committee and declare the Muthurajawela Wetland Zone as a Ramsar Wetland.

description: Implementation of Third Tranche of the Second Integrated Road Investment Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-10
decision_details_body: - The Government of Sri Lanka and the Asian Development Bank have entered into an agreement to obtain US$ 900 million from the said Bank to implement the Second Integrated Road Investment Programme. Under the said programme, it has been planned to upgrade and maintain about 3,400km of rural access roads in Eastern, Northern, Uva and Western Provinces and to rehabilitate 340km of national roads between the rural community and social economic centres in the said provinces. It is expected to complete the overall programme by 31st March, 2027. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to obtain a sum of US$ 200 million from the Asian Development Bank as the third installment of US$ 900 million which has been agreed to finance the Second Integrated Road Investment Programme and to enter into the agreement for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Increasing the PCR capacity during the third wave of COVID-19 Pandemic
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-03
decision_details_body: - With the detection of the new COVID variant, the demand for the COVID PCR tests in the government laboratories has been increased up to 20000 per day at present and there is a trend of increasing the demand. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to take action to purchase the test kits and other consumables required for PCR tests, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Annual Report of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka for the year 2020 to Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-03
decision_details_body: - The Monetary Board of the  Central Bank of Sri Lanka should submit a report containing the condition of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka, the policies and measures adopted by the Monetary Board during the year, to the Minister of Finance within 04 months from the commencement of the following year. Accordingly, the Annual Report of the  Central Bank of Sri Lanka for the year 2020 has been submitted to the Minister of Finance  on 2021‑04‑30 and it should be submitted to Parliament by the Minister of Finance within 14 days from the receipt in terms of Monetary Law Act. Accordingly, proposal made by the Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to table the Annual Report of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka for the year 2020 in Parliament , was approved by the Cabinet.

description: National Regulatory Framework for the vessels engaged in coastal trading activities
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-03
decision_details_body: - It has been identified the necessity of having a National Regulatory Framework for commercial coastal vessels  due to the increase of passenger and cargo transportation by ships with the development of tourism related activities.  Accordingly, the Export Development Board and the then Ministry of Development Strategies and International Trade in collaboration with he Ministry of Port and Shipping have initiated a project for developing such regulatory framework  and  the assistance of the Lloyd's Register Asia has been obtained for the same. As such, 04 regulations have been drafted in consultation with  all related parties. In terms of the provisions of the Merchant Shipping Act No.52 of 1972, authority of promulgating said regulations have been entrusted with Minister in charge of subject of shipping.  Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports and Shipping to publish draft regulations in the Government Gazette upon the receipt of the concurrence of the Legal Draftsman and to present the same thereafter in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement for Supply of 840,000 Prefilled Syringe of Enoxaparian Sodium Injection, 4000IU, 0.4ml
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-03
decision_details_body: - International Competitive Bids  have been called for the procurement of this drug which is used for the treatment of patients with heart diseases.  Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to award the above procurement to  M/s Slim Pharmaceuticals (Pvt.) Ltd of Sri Lanka at a sum of Rs.541.80 million as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement for supply of 112,500 Vials of Human Immunoglobulin for Intravenous use BP, 5g -6g Vial
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-03
decision_details_body: - International Competitive Bids  have been called for the procurement of this drug which is used for the treatment of patients with  immune deficiencies.  Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to award the above procurement to  M/s Reliance Life Science (Pvt.) Ltd of India at a sum of Rs. 13.10 million as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of 500 Container Based Cross - Fit Gyms at selected locations throughout the Country
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-03
decision_details_body: - It has been scheduled to establish 500 Container Based Cross - Fit Gyms   countrywide under the theme of 'lets win' in view of directing the youths towards active lifestyle and giving some motivation for the progress of the field of sports. The estimated cost for this is Rs. 625 million  and approximately 100,000 general public and 5000 athletes would be able to accrue benefits by implementation of the project. It is expected to delegate the responsibility of running these Gyms to the Youth Societies and Sports Clubs at the regional level and to assign at least one trainer to each Centre. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Youth and Sports to implement the proposed project in the years 2021-2022 and to build said Container Based Cross - Fit Gyms,  covering 250 selected areas countrywide in the year 2021, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Assignment of the activities of Smart Sri Lanka Programme to the Department of Manpower and Employment
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-03
decision_details_body: - The Smart Sri Lanka Institute has then been established under the Presidential  Secretariat on the Cabinet approval with a view to coordinating and supervising career guidance from national level to regional level and implementing the same as a national programme under a new approach utilizing the modern technology. The said Institute has now been included in the purview of the Ministry of Youth and Sports. Accordingly, the Cabinet granted its concurrence to the action taken by the Minister of  Youth and Sports to assign the Smart Sri Lanka Institute to the Department of Manpower and Employment and continue its functions.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism & Hotel Management (SLITHM) and EHL Advisory Services LLP, New Delhi, India
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-03
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism & Hotel Management (SLITHM) has been established in 1966 to train the youth in the field of hospitality and tourism industry. In view of providing educational facilities in the field of hospitality to students isalndwide, its provincial schools have been established in the towns of Anuradhapura, Bandarawela, Pallekele, Koggala, Rathnapura, Kurunegala, Jaffna and Pasikudah. Even though the training schools of Private sector in the said sector have achieved a rapid progress, the image of Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism & Hotel Management has been tarnished gradually. It has been planned to seek the assistance of  EHL Advisory Services LLP, New Delhi, India with the intervention of the Embassy of Switzerland in Sri Lanka, to conduct an Analytical Study on the quality of the education programmes of the said Institute, enabling to rebuild the Institute and uplift its image. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Tourism to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between EHL Advisory Services LLP and the Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism & Hotel Management to obtain the services of EHL Advisory Services LLP, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Government of Sri Lanka and the Great Britain and Northern Ireland of the United Kingdom on Microplastics related Researches
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-03
decision_details_body: - Since the adverse effects of the use of microplastics extend to a number of fields including Health, Agriculture and Tourism, Sri Lanka has initiated many programmes on management of the said waste. Great Britain and Northern Ireland of the United Kingdom have expressed their willingness to cooperate in the related research activities and thus assistance will be provided to increase the local research capacity on microplastics. It has been proposed to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the purpose to be effective for two years and the concurrence of the relevant Ministries and the Attorney General's Department has been received for the draft MoU. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to enter into the said MoU and to appoint an Inter-Institutional Committee comprising the representatives of the Ministries relating to the subject and the institutes falling under the purview of the said Ministries, aiming at management of plastics including the increasing of research capacity of Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Declaring a Road Safety Week to draw special attention of the society for minimizing road traffic accidents
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-03
decision_details_body: - At present, between 8-10 people lose their lives daily because of road traffic accidents and the majority of them are males. Their dependents become extremely helpless due to this reason and it shows an increasing trend in that number year by year. In the last year, there had been 2,023 fatal road accidents and out of them, 2,114 people have succumbed to death. 963 of them are motorcycle related accidents which have caused 987 deaths. It has been reported that around 500 deaths occur annually due to road accidents caused by three wheelers and lorries as well. Taking into consideration these matters, the National Council for Road Safety has drawn its attention to implement a National Road Safety Week from 21st November, which is the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims, and to take necessary measures to raise awareness among the Public and Private Institutes, students, drivers and the General Public on reducing the occurrence of road traffic accidents. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport to declare a National Road Safety Week to be effective from Sunday 21st November 2021 and to continue such a week annually in every November in future, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Open University of Sri Lanka and the Graduate School of Environmental and Life Science, Okayama University, Japan
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-03
decision_details_body: - In view of promoting the activities of organizing student, faculty and staff exchange programmes, collaborative research, instructional and cultural programmes and exchanging research information, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Open University of Sri Lanka and the Graduate School of Environmental and Life Science, Okayama University, Japan, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Enabling students to obtain first degree qualifications within a minimum period by amending the time schedules of holding the G.C.E. (Ordinary Level) and G.C.E. (Advanced Level) examinations and minimizing the time taken for selecting students to State Universities
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-03
decision_details_body:
- Since there is a lapse between the releasing of the G.C.E. (O/L) Examination results and the commencement of G.C.E. (A/L) classes and the time taken for selecting students to the State Universities, it has been observed that, at the time of completing school education and university education, students normally reach the age of 19-20 years and 25-26 years, respectively. Due to structural mismatches of these examination systems and the administrative delays associated with the existing technical procedures, the youth have been obliged to spend their time unnecessarily, to complete higher education expeditiously and enter the job market. It has been observed that this situation adversely affect them personally as well as the economic growth of the country as a whole. 

	Therefore, with a view to avoiding this situation in future, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to take action as follows, was approved by the Cabinet. 

* 	Restructuring of the curriculum of Grades 10 and 11, so as to limit for a study period of 01 year and 09 months.

* 	Conducting the G.C.E. (O/L) Examination in August and the G.C.E. (A/L) Examination in December and reducing the current time of  45 months to 32 months spent for the entire process by releasing the results of each examination within 03 months and providing technical arrangements required for the purpose.

* 	Implementing the selection process of students to universities on z‑Score without waiting for the finalization of the re-scrutinization process of G.C.E. (A/L) Examination results.

*	Providing opportunity to those students, if any, who have achieved higher results through the re-scrutinization process, to follow the relevant degree programmes by providing them with new z-Scores and implementing the said methodology from the G.C.E. (A/L) 2020 onwards.

description: Construction of a Buddhist Temple of Sri Lankan tradition at the premises of White Horse Temple in the People's Republic of China
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-05-03
decision_details_body: - In view of enhancing the long standing diplomatic relations between the People's Republic of China and Sri Lanka, it has been proposed to construct a Buddhist temple of Sri Lankan tradition which the world Buddhist Community pays homage to, in the premises of White Horse temple in the People's Republic of China. All expenses incurred for the proposed construction activities will be met by the White Horse temple and the said construction activities will be carried out under the supervision of the Ministry in-charge of the subject of Buddhasasana in Sri Lanka. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious & Cultural Affairs to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the White Horse temple of the People's Republic of China and the Ministry of Buddhasasana, Religious & Cultural Affairs for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Enactment of laws required for Protection from false and misleading statements made through Internet
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-19
decision_details_body: - Online falsehoods create a severe threat and it has been observed that this situation is being used to divide the society, spread hate and weaken the democratic institutions. In view of resolving this issue, various countries have already taken action to enact laws. Actions have to be taken to provide an opportunity to the citizens and civil society for access to accurate information by introducing a new law for protection of the society from harms caused due to online falsehoods. As such, the joint proposal made by the Minister of Justice and the Minister of Mass Media to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft a Bill for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the functions of the Department of Manpower and Employment on legal basis
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-19
decision_details_body: - In terms of a Cabinet decision, the Department of Manpower and Employment was established in the year 2010 by an Extraordinary Gazette Notification. The said Department is vested with preparation and implementation of a National Policy on Manpower and Employment, creation and promotion of employment, career guidance related activities, collection, analysis and distribution of labour market details and the services rendered by the Job Portal. Through this, it is expected to achieve the objectives of reducing the rate of unemployment and underemployment in the country and, shaping and managing the manpower in line with the future trends. The necessity of legitimacy of this Department in discharging the said functions has been recognized and the appropriateness of establishing the same through a Parliamentary Act has been observed. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Youth & Sports to establish the functions of the Department of Manpower and Employment on legal basis and to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft a Bill incorporating the provisions for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Drafting an Act for the Registration of Dairy Entrepreneurs Societies
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-19
decision_details_body: - Even though Dairy Entrepreneurs Societies registered at district and provincial levels operate in view of encouraging the entrepreneurs engaged in dairy farming, there does not exist a common organization consisting of all dairy entrepreneurs societies that operates under the Government sponsorship. Therefore, in taking action for the upliftment of dairy industry, the necessity has arisen to register the Dairy Entrepreneurs Societies within single legal framework at regional, district, provincial and all island levels under such common structure. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft a Bill for registration of Dairy Entrepreneurs Societies for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Fiscal Management (Responsibility) Act, No.3 of 2003
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-19
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted on 2020‑12‑21 to draft a Bill for amending the Debt and Guarantee Rules specified in the Fiscal Management (Responsibility) Act, No.3 of 2003. The Legal Draftsman has drafted the relevant draft accordingly and clearance of the Attorney General has been obtained for the same. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to publish the said Bill in the Government Gazette and submit the same thereafter in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Enactment of an Act for the Regulation of Publishing Buddhist Publications
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-19
decision_details_body: - In terms of Article 9 in Chapter II of the Constitution, one of the main responsibilities of the Government shall be the protection and fostering Buddhasasana while giving the foremost place to Buddhism. It has been apparent that  various books, publications, Compact Discs (CDs) and other productions emerge distorting the pure Buddhism and Buddhist traditions. Therefore, it has been observed that it would be appropriate to enact an Act incorporating the provisions for regulation of such productions. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious & Cultural Affairs to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft a Bill for regulating the publication of Buddhist publications, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Purchasing of School uniform materials - 2022
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-19
decision_details_body: - It has been planned to provide school uniform materials to school children for the year 2022, before the end of final school term in year 2021. Approval of the Cabinet has previously been granted to the effect that school uniform materials be procured from local textile manufacturers so as to encourage them and as such, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to take action accordingly to call for bids from the local textile manufacturers who have registered under the Ministry of Industries and select appropriate suppliers, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: 'Youth Hub' - The Project for the establishment of the  High Impact Youth Community Centres
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-19
decision_details_body: - To lead an efficient social life by sharing ideas, existing facilities for Sri Lankan youth community to find solutions through negotiations for their educational, health, civil and political issues are inadequate. Specially, the opportunities and the locations available at divisional level for organizing and engaging voluntarily in such activities are very limited. As a remedy to this situation, it has been identified that it would be appropriate to create suitable locations for youths to gather at a familiar environment and to engage in productive activities by sharing experiences. For this purpose, it has been planned to identify the underutilized government schools and other buildings with sufficient spaces at divisional and district level and launch a programme to establish High Impact Youth Community Centres creating multiple opportunities and activities. It is also expected to construct Youth Community Centres in each Divisional Secretariat Divisions of the country within five years implementing as public private joined project and facilitating for various activities within 04 zones such as Youth Development Zone, Youth Entertainment Zone, Economic Zone, and Green Zone in the same centre. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Youth and Sports to implement the said programme at phase out level and to establish 25 centres covering all districts as the first phase of the project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Digitization of Terrestrial Television Broadcasting Project in Sri Lanka under the Japanese Loan
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-19
decision_details_body: - The Terrestrial Television Broadcasting is evolving from Analog to Digital and it has been found necessary to adapt this system according to the world trend. Accordingly, required decisions had been made at several occasions to move to Analog to Digital Terrestrial Television Broadcasting system, but those decisions have not been implemented so far. It has been decided to introduce ISDB-T Technology to suit Sri Lanka, subsequent to a feasibility study conducted by the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA). Adaption to the Digital Technology will enable to use a part of Frequency Spectrum utilized at present for wireless broadband services thus increasing  internet access in rural areas. Accordingly,  the joint proposal made by H.E the President in his capacity as the Minister of Technology and the Minister of Mass Media to implement  Digitization of Terrestrial Television Broadcasting Project utilizing modern technology, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of Hardy Institute of Technology
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-19
decision_details_body: - In line with the development needs in 1960s, the Hardy Institute of Technology has been set up as a Technical Training Institute to provide systematic engineering knowledge to the Technical Officers aiming the Galoya Development Project, the first multipurpose reservoir project of Sri Lanka. Subsequently, the scope and the structure of the said Institute has been changed at many occasions and at present, it functions as two separate institutes such as Hardy Technical College, offering National Diploma (NVQ - 5 Level) and Higher National Diploma (NVQ - 6 Level) to provide those who have missed the mainstream higher education with alternative higher education opportunities and as Hardy Advanced Technological Institute established under  Sri Lanka Institute of  Advanced Technological Education  conducting NDT Agricultural Programme which was conducted by the said Hardy Technical College earlier. Since it has been identified that the structure and the course content are required to be changed in order to create entrepreneurs enriched with high technical knowledge assisting to expedite the economic development  and expand the economy according to the economic programmes of the present Government, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to establish an independent institution named “Hardy Institute of Technology” combining the said two institutions and to amend the relevant Acts for the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the University of Sri Jayewardenepura and the University of Sungkyunkwan in Republic of Korea
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-19
decision_details_body: - It has been proposed to enter into an MoU between the University of Sri Jayewardenepura and the University of Sungkyunkwan in Republic of Korea for academic and cultural exchange in the areas  of Immunology and Molecular Medicine through enhancing the collaboration in undergraduate curriculum development in Immunology and Molecular Medicine, assisting in commencing the study programme and development and operation of innovative research programmes for secondary and junior college students in the community. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to sign the relevant MoU, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of City Universities
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-19
decision_details_body: - Creation of globally competitive professionals equipped with competencies has been identified as a timely requirement in order to enhance the quality of highly demanding professions in the job market. Only about 20% out of the students who passed G.C.E. (A/L) and qualified for universities, get opportunities to enter into the state universities for studies and inclination of the rest of students towards the vocational education is not at a considerable level. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to establish City Universities as universities awarding degrees to suit with employment opportunities developing skills required for the production sectors in the relevant Districts and to get provided necessary legal provisions for the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Purchasing another 6 million doses of ‘Sputnik V’ Vaccine to prevent the spread of Covid – 19
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-05
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2021‑03‑23 to purchase 7 million doses of ‘Sputnik V’ Vaccine at a cost of US$ 9.95 each to a sum of 69.65 US$ million upon the recommendation of the Cabinet Appointed Negotiating Committee. The Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Health to purchase another 6 million doses of ‘Sputnik V’ Vaccine at the same price in addition to the aforesaid doses of vaccines.

description: Further extension of the validity period granted to open 'Special Deposit Accounts' under the Foreign Exchange Act No.12 of 2017
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-05
decision_details_body: - Relevant regulations have been issued under the Foreign Exchange Act No.12 of 2017, making provisions to open Special Deposit Accounts to be effective from April, 2020 with a view to encouraging the foreign exchange inflows into the country. Moreover, Cabinet approval has been granted to pay an additional interest with a view to further retaining the available deposits of the said accounts. Accordingly, as at March, 2021, total deposits in the said accounts amounted to US$ 360.3 million. Since the validity period granted for opening the said Special Deposit Accounts is due to be ended on 2021‑04‑07, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to further extend the validity period to encourage those are interested in making deposits in such accounts further and to issue regulations for the purpose in accordance with the provisions of the Foreign Exchange Act , was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Repealing the Tourism Act No 38 of 2005 and enacting a New Tourism Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-05
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority, the Sri Lanka Tourism Promotion Bureau, Sri Lanka Convention Bureau and the Sri Lanka Institution of Tourism and Hotel Management were established, having divided the entire tourism sector into four major entities in terms of the provisions of the Tourism Act No 38 of 2005. However, due to the tourism sector being separated into 4 entitiess, it is observed that there have been negative impacts such as delays in coordinating relevant entities and wastage of resources etc. Therefore, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Tourism to repeal the Tourism Act No 38 of 2005 and to draft a bill to enact a New Tourism Act in order to ensure the sustainable development of the Tourism industry thereby taking necessary action to establish a new authority by the name of “Sri Lanka Tourism Authority” having confederated the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority, Sri Lanka Tourism Promotion Bureau, Sri Lanka Convention Bureau.

description: Award of contracts to the suppliers for the supply of food items to the Department of Prisons for the year 2021/2022
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-05
decision_details_body: - National competitive bids have been called to select contractors for the supply of food items for the Department of Prisons for the year 2021/2022. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to award the relevant contracts for the selected suppliers for the supply of food items to the Department of Prisons for the period of 2021‑04‑16 to 2022‑04‑15, as recommended by the Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of an Accelerated Procurement Process for implementing the Projects of Corporate Plan 2020-2025 of the National Water Supply and Drainage Board
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-05
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2021‑01‑11 granted approval to implement water and sewerage projects which included in the Corporate Plan 2020-2025. It has been planned to meet 78.8% of drinking water requirement of the households in the country by 2025 through the implementation of the proposed projects. In order to achieve this target, It has been scheduled to increase the present production capacity by 2.35 million cubic metres per day and supply and laying of around 40,000km of transmission and distribution pipe lines. Further, it has been found that the National Water Supply and Drainage Board takes more time for the procurement process than the time taken by the other institutions due to the complex nature of the water sector projects. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Water Supply to procure pipes and fittings under a centralized procurement system and to introduce a unit price system for the same and to introduce a Unit Rate procedure when awarding pipe laying contracts as well, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Revision of Tea Planting Subsidies currently paid to encourage the Tea Cultivation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-05
decision_details_body: - The total tea production in the year 2019 was 300 million kg and approximately 75% out of which amounting to 225 million kg were manufactured by tea smallholdings sector. It has been identified the necessity of enhancing the productivity of tea smallholdings lands in order to maintain the tea production at the optimum level. It is required to encourage farmers to obtain the production target of 360 million kg of tea by the year 2025, since the attention of farmers for tea cultivation and replanting is insufficient due to the fact that it takes nearly 04 years to generate income by the replantation of tea and it will cost a lot of money. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Plantation to increase the Tea Replanting Subsidy and the Tea New Planting Subsidy of Rs. 400,000/- per hectare to Rs.500,000/- per hectare, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Opening of Batticaloa, Vauniya and Jaffna Dedicated Economic Centres
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-05
decision_details_body: - The Dedicated Economic Centre Programme has been initiated so as to sell the agricultural products of the farmers directly and to implement the price mechanism more efficiently through competition and 15 such Economic Centres are functioning countrywide at present. Accordingly, construction work of Batticaloa and Vauniya Dedicated Economic Centres have been completed and the construction work of the phase I of the Special Economic Centre in Jaffna has been completed by now. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture to establish the Management Committee for the administration of the said Special Economic Center and to allocate business premises of such Economic Centres following a formal methodology, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of Trusted Digital Repository at the National Archives
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-04-05
decision_details_body: - The Department of National Archives holds valuable archives from the Dutch and British administration since the year 1640 and those created after independence and the legal deposits of all publications including newspapers published from the the 19th Century. This Department receives a large number of documents daily including digital publications and documents, radio and television broadcasting, websites and emails etc. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs to establish a trusted digital repository, following the international standards on digital preservation in order to ensure the reliability and authenticity of the said digital records, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Civil Procedure Code
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-03-29
decision_details_body: Recently, motor traffic accidents have alarmingly increased. In order to seek reliefs against such an accident, a case has to be filed in a Civil Court. Here, the victim or his heir has to produce Medico Legal Report and other medical reports and those reports will then be inevitably marked as 'subject to proof'. The victim or his heir is responsible to ensure that the Medical Officer will appear in Courts to testify to prove the contents in the said reports. Since such a motor traffic accident case takes 10 or 12 years of prolonged period for its conclusion, the Government has to incur an unnecessary expenditure burden to summon the relevant Medical Officer to the Court if he serves at a distant location and at the same time, he loses the opportunity to engage his precious time in professional activities. Taking into consideration these matters, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft legislation to amend the Civil Procedure Code, to provide for considering the Medico-Legal Report, Post Mortem Report and the Bed Head Ticket as prima facie evidence and to enable to provide for shifting the burden of rebutting the Medico-Legal evidence when the defendant contests such evidence, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Preparation of the National Drinking Community Water Development Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-03-29
decision_details_body: Subsequent to the establishment of the Department of National Community Water Supply, the said Department regulates and empowers the Community Based Organizations managed by the Community. Yet, the said Department has faced with a number of issues for not possessing the legal power required for the purpose. Taking into consideration these matters, the proposal made by the Minister of Water Supply to draft the National Drinking Community Water Development Act to enable formal and effective functioning of the Department of National Community Water Supply, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Firearms Ordinance, No.33 of 1916 (Chapter 182) amended by the Act, No.22 of 1996
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-03-29
decision_details_body: Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2007 06 13 to draft a Bill for further amending the Firearms Ordinance, No.33 of 1916 (Chapter 182) as last amended by the Act, No.22 of 1996. However, drafting of the said Bill has been delayed due to amendments proposed from time to time. As such, the proposal made by H.E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft a Bill incorporating all the relevant amendments to meet the present requirements, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding four civil works contract packages on rehabilitation, improvement and maintenance of the Colombo - Kandy Road (A001) (44+300 km to 100+000km)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-03-29
decision_details_body: National Competitive Bids have been called for 04 civil works contract packages for rehabilitation, improvement and maintenance of the Colombo - Kandy Road (from 44km to 100 km) under the Asian Development Bank funded Integrated Road Investment Programme. Accordingly, 15 bidders have submitted 47 bids. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Highways to award the said relevant contract packages to the substantially responsive bidders selected as per the recommendation of the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement of Design, Manufacture, Supply, Installation, Commissioning and handing over of a Single Sleeper Multiple Tie Tamping Machine for the Department of Sri Lanka Railways
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-03-29
decision_details_body: With a view to enhancing the maintenance capacity of the Department of Sri Lanka Railways and reducing the maintenance cost, International Competitive Bids have been called for manufacturing and handing over of a Single Sleeper Multiple Tie Tamping Machine. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport to award the relevant procurement to M/s Matisa Matériel Industriel S.A. - Switzerland, for a sum of US$ 4.96 million, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee (SCAPC), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Introduction of a mechanism for the protection of consumers of petroleum
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-03-29
decision_details_body: At the initial stage, the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) was responsible for all petroleum industry related activities. However, a number of parties are currently involved in these activities. Even though the Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) has been appointed as the regulatory body of the petroleum industry, the functions of the said Commission has been limited to providing advice to and assisting the Ministry regarding policy and regulation of the lubricant industry. Under this condition, a practical mechanism has not been established for the protection of rights of the consumers of petroleum. Therefore, it has been proposed to establish an independent and transparent mechanism for handling and resolving consumer complaints under the supervision of the Ministry of Energy and the Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL). In the implementation of the said mechanism, the Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL), Consumer Affairs Authority, Sri Lanka Customs, Sri Lanka Police, Sri Lanka Standards Institute, Industrial Technology Institute and other relevant Government Institutes will join. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Energy to implement the drafted 'Statement of Rights and Obligations of Consumers' and the 'Procedure for Handling Compliants and Resolution of Disputes' and to sign a Memorandum of Understanding with the relevant Government Institutes for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Allocation of land blocks from Regional Industrial Estates to set up industries
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-03-29
decision_details_body: The Regional Industrial Services Committee and the Project Evaluation Committee of the Ministry of Industries have recommended the allocation of 16 land blocks in the 09 Industrial Estates of Nalanda (Matale), Bataatha, Karandeniya, Udukawa, Embilipitiya, Kalutara, Batticaloa and Nawagampura, for investors to start up new industries. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries to allocate the said land blocks on 35 year lease basis and subject to the condition of 'not transferable to other parties' and other relevant conditions, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of Cyclotron Based Radio - Pharmaceutical Production Centre in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-03-29
decision_details_body: Fluoro Deoxy Glucose (18F-FDG) which is a radioactive drug, is used for PET and CT tests to diagnose cancers. A special device called Cyclotron is used to produce this drug and this radioactive drug is imported from India since the required facilities are not available in Sri Lanka. Due to its radioactive decaying nature, about 97% of the strength of the drug losses when it is imported from India. Only 10 patients can be treated from the remaining capacity. Although, about 30,000 patients are required to undergo the relevant test annually,  only 1600 patients can be tested due to the above reason. It costs Rs. 54,000 to the government to test one patient using the imported drug and If the drug is manufactured locally, the cost can be reduced to Rs. 14,000. Taking into consideration this situation, the Government has planned to set up a Cyclotron based Radio-pharmaceutical Production Centre in Sri Lanka in the premises of Kotelawala Defence University Hospital, Werahera in collaboration with the Atomic Energy Board of Sri Lanka and Sir Jhon Kotelawala Defence University. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Power to implement the said project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining service facilities from Sri Lanka Telecom to promote the services of the Department of Motor Traffic
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-03-29
decision_details_body: A large number of clients arrive in the Head Office of the Department of Motor Traffic, Werahera office and district level offices in order to obtain services rendered by the said Department. Since both clients and the staff of the Department are faced with difficulties in certain occasions due to the above reason, it has been planned to redress this matter by utilizing modern information and communication technology for reserving a time for the duties in advance, obtaining a number for the same, guiding to reach the relevant divisions for services according to service requirement of clients and notifying the relevant information to the client by SMS etc. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport to implement the proposed project in association with Sri Lanka Telecom and to implement the same in the offices of Narahenpita and Werahara and 05 Districts offices where online facilities are available as the first phase and  thereafter implement in the rest of 19 District Offices as the second phase of the proposed project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Ruhuna and the Graduate School of Environmental and life Sciences, Okayama University, Japan
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-03-29
decision_details_body: It has been proposed to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding between the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Ruhuna and the Graduate School of Environmental and Life Science, Okayama University, Japan with a view to enhancing higher education cooperation and international relations. It has been planned to launch programmes for exchange of students, exchange of faculty and staff and to conduct collaborative research and to exchange research  information. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to enter into the said MoU for a period of five years initially, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Cooperation Agreement between the University of Peradeniya and the International Development Research Center (IDRC), Canada
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-03-29
decision_details_body: Various strategic methods have been  adopted by countries to control the spread of Covid - 19 pandemic and to minimize its damage. In this instance, it has been planned to implement a research project on the impact caused to women, children and less privileged social groups  due to the various strategies used by certain countries for the said purpose. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to enter into a Cooperative Agreement between  the University of Peradeniya and the International Development Research Center (IDRC), Canada to implement the said project based on Sri Lanka and Malaysia, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of a Research Project on the use of Nitrogen based Chemical Fertilizer
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-03-29
decision_details_body: Taking into consideration the environmental pollution caused due to the mismanagement of chemical fertilizer (Nitrogen in particular) in the South Asian region, it has been planned to implement a multitask research proposal based on South Asian region on the use of nitrogen based fertilizers in different farming systems led by the United Nation Environmental Programme (UNEP) in association with the International Nitrogen Management Systems (INMS). Under this project, it has been scheduled to carry out the activities such as collecting data on nitrogen losses and greenhouse gas emission from selected farming systems (vegetables-Nuwara-eliya and Kalpitiya), (Rice - Anuradhapura) making the farmers aware on such  things, identifying atmospheric pollution on lower plant diversity of montane forests and educating farming communities and stakeholders for creating best nitrogen management systems to minimize Nitrogen losses, within a period of 05 years. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to enter into a Collaboration Agreement among the University of Peradeniya, Sri Lanka and United Kingdom Research and Innovation (UKRI), Global Challenge Research Fund  (GCRF) and South Asian Nitrogen Hub (SANH), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Flood Mitigation Projects in the year 2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-03-29
