decision_details_body: - Public Transport Service of Sri Lanka relies on fares and with a view to avoiding the hardships resulting in, approval has been granted at the Cabinet Meeting held on 02nd October 2018, to appoint a Steering Committee comprising of representatives from all the relevant institutions, to implement a project for introducing a Transit Card for the use in Buses and Trains belonging to public transport. As such, a local Company, Lanka Clear (Pvt) Ltd. which is 100% affiliated to the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) with its approval, has submitted a proposal for the proposed Transit Card Project and based on such project proposal, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport to take necessary action for the use of Transit Card in the island, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the University of Colombo and the Lahore School of Economics in Pakistan
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-15
decision_details_body: - With a view to exchanging research materials, publications and information mutually benefiting each party, encouraging the joint and individual research projects of the two institutions and providing opportunities to have experiences through the Programme of exchanging students with skills and abilities, it has been proposed to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the University of Colombo and the Lahore School of Economics in Pakistan. An Expert Committee has studied the proposed MoU and submitted its recommendations and, concurrence of the Foreign Ministry and the Attorney General's Department has been granted for the same. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to sign the said MoU, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of Summit Flats Premises for the promotion of construction of Multi-storied Housing Units
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-15
decision_details_body: - In order to meet the increasing demand on houses due to the dearth of lands available in the City of Colombo, the Government has paid its attention to identify suitable land blocks and construct multi-storied housing units. The Summit Flats, having established in the year 1976, comprising 176 housing units and 15 bungalows constructed in a land block of 12 acres in extent and located in Keppetipola Road, Colombo 05, under the governance of the Ministry of Public Services, Provincial Councils and Local Government, are being used for official residential requirements of the Public Officers. Most of these housing units are in dilapidated condition at present and the National Building Research Organization (NBRO) has recommended that the said housing units should be fully repaired. Further, around 700 Public Officers are in the waiting list in anticipation of official residences. Taking these matters into consideration, the Ministry of Urban Development & Housing and the Ministry of Public Services, Provincial Councils & Local Government have entered into an Agreement to implement a project for constructing 400 official residences for Public Officers, in a block of land of 02 acres of the said 12 acres in extent, as its first stage. 100 housing units from the Middle Income Housing Schemes currently underway by the Urban Development Authority within the purview of the said project, will also be transferred to the Ministry of Public Services, Provincial Councils & Local Government. Accordingly, the remaining land in extent of 10 acres will be transferred to the Urban Development Authority for development. As such, the Joint Proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing and the Minister of Public Services, Provincial Councils & Local Government to implement the proposed project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Presenting the promulgated Regulations on 'Special Deposit Accounts' under the Foreign Exchange Act, No.12 of 2017, to Parliament for its approval
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-15
decision_details_body: - With a view to encouraging the remittance of foreign currency into the country, approval has been granted to open 'Special Deposit Accounts' and approval of the Cabinet was also granted previously to pay an additional interest for further retaining the deposits in the said accounts. Accordingly, Regulations have been promulgated through the Extraordinary Gazette Notification No.2202/07 dated 2020-11-17 under the Foreign Exchange Act, No.12 of 2017, to extend the validity period to open the said Special Deposit Accounts for a further period of six (06) months with effect from 08th October 2020. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to present the said Regulations for approval in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement of Chemical Fertilizer - 2021 Yala Season - (Early April Delivery)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-08
decision_details_body:
- International competitive bids have been called to procure chemical fertilizer for Ceylon Fertilizer Company Ltd. (Lak Pohora) and Colombo Commercial Fertilizers Ltd. (Commercial Fertilizer) for early April delivery of 2021 Yala Season. Accordingly, the proposals made by the Minister of Agriculture to award the following procurement for the supply fertilizer as per the recommendation made by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee with regard to the said quotations, was approved by the Cabinet. 

* 	To procure 40,500+5% MTs of Urea (Granular) under 270 days credit period from M/s Swiss Singapore Overseas Pte. Ltd. at US$343.10 per 1 MT. 

* 	To procure 8,500+5% MTs of Urea (Prilled) under 180 days credit period from M/s Valency International Pte. Ltd. at US$ 364.74 per 1 MT.

* 	To procure 13,900+5% MTs of Muriate of Potash under 180 days credit period from M/s Agricultural Resources and Investments Pte. Ltd. at US$ 258.74 per 1 MT.

description: Projects proposed to be implemented by the State Ministry of Livestock, Farm Promotion and Dairy & Egg related Industries for the upcoming 5 years from the year 2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-08
decision_details_body:
- The Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture to update the activities of the following projects presently being implemented for the increase of production capacity of the other industries related to local dairy production and livestock development and implement the same during the next 05 years. 

* Project for the popularization of liquid milk consumption.
* Project for the establishment of breeder farms.
* Swine industry development project.
* Small and medium scale poultry farms development project.
* Enhancement of productivity through promotion of small and medium scale diary farms.
* Medium term livestock development project.

description: Construction of Rural Roads and Bridges
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-08
decision_details_body: - The State Ministry of Rural Roads and other Infrastructure which is coming under the purview of the Ministry of Highways has planned to construct 5000 rural bridges such as pedestrian bridges and vehicular bridges all over the Island. It has been proposed to implement the said construction of bridges process under the project of the rehabilitation of 100,000km rural road network of the Government. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Highways to implement the said project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Project to provide financial facilities for the sectors mostly affected by the COVID -19 pandemic
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-08
decision_details_body: - A project has been designed to implement with the participation of the Bank of Ceylon and the Peoples' Bank under the COVID-19 Emergency and Crisis Response Facility of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank with the objective of providing required funds for the mostly affected sectors by the COVID - 19 pandemic such as tourism, textile, construction, trade, manufacturing, agricultural exports and health care. The proposed project will assist to increase the liquidity support for the small and medium scale enterprises of those sectors. Under the said project, two credit facilities of US$ 90 million each will be granted for the Bank of Ceylon and the Peoples' Bank and the said two banks will grant sub-loans to their clients. Therefore, the proposal made by the Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to take necessary action to implement the said project including the entering into relevant agreements, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Removal of scrap metals in the Kankesanthurai Cement Factory Premises
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-08
decision_details_body: - Preliminary plans have been made by the Ministry of Industries to launch a Cement Manufacturing Project at the Kankesanthurai Cement Factory premises. Accordingly, a Five -Member Committee has been appointed to conduct a site inspection and make recommendations relating to the removal of scrap metals and cleaning of the said factory premises. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries as recommended by the said Committee to remove the unusable buildings, structures, machinery, scrap metals and steel at the Kankesanthurai Cement Factory Premises, by following the Government Procurement Procedure, based on the valuation made by the Chief Government Valuer, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement of 150MW of Solar Power Capacities
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-08
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted to implement the procurement process on the establishment of 150MW Solar Power Plants in different locations across the country. Accordingly, approval has been granted at the Cabinet Meeting held on 14th December 2020, to award the procurements in respect of which appeals had not been made against the recommendations of the Cabinet Appointed Negotiation Committee (CANC) and for which International Bids were called under 05 Packages. The Procurement Appeal Board has rejected the appeals made in respect of the rest of the procurements. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Power, to award the procurements to the selected bidders for the Anuradhapura, Habarana, Matara, Galle, Deniyaya, Kosgama, Mathugama, Pannala, Mahawa and Kurunegala Grid Sub‑Stations for a period of 20 years, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Granting Long term lease of a land to the Sri Lanka Cashew Corporation for the Cashew Seed Garden
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-08
decision_details_body: - A land block in extent of 86.093 hectares (212 acres 02 roods 23.95 perches) located in the Ralmaduwa Grama Niladhari Division, Wanathavilluwa where the Agricultural Research Unit‑ Eluwankulama was maintained, has been transferred to the Sri Lanka Cashew Corporation in July 1998 for development and use. Accordingly, the Sri Lanka Cashew Corporation is using the said land for Cashew cultivation. The Sri Lanka Cashew Corporation has planned to maintain a collection of Cashew varieties available in different areas of Sri Lanka through the Plant Breeding Centre located in the said land, in association with the Faculty of Agriculture of Wayamba University. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Lands, to transfer the said land to the Sri Lanka Cashew Corporation on long term lease basis for a period of 50 years, to implement the said project which is of tremendous economic and social significance, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Allocation of land blocks from the Regional Industrial Estates to set up Industries
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-08
decision_details_body: - The Regional Industrial Services Committee and the Project Evaluation Committee of the Ministry of Industries have recommended the allocation of land blocks from 08 Industrial Estates for 22 investors, subject to a lease period of 35 years, under the Regional Industrial Estates Development Programme implemented by the Ministry of Industries. Those investors are to invest Rs.24,047.85 million and US$ 3 million for the said projects and it has been estimated that 3,326 direct employment opportunities will be generated from these projects. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries, to allocate the said land blocks for the investors subject to the relevant conditions, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Sri Lanka's Regional Trade Agreements (RTAs) and Free Trade Agreements (FTAs)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-08
decision_details_body: - Regional Trade Agreements and Free Trade Agreements are a key feature in the International Trade and those Agreements have increased in number as well as in complexity over the past few years. Sri Lanka has also entered into such several Trade Agreements and it has been observed that the country could not achieve the expected outcome under some Agreements. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade, to review such Agreements currently under negotiations in order to comply with the National Policy Framework of the 'Vistas of Prosperity and Splendour' and resume negotiations accordingly and, to take necessary action to explore the feasibility of entering into new Regional Trade Agreements and Free Trade Agreements, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Maintaining the 'Ape Gama' Folk Heritage Exhibition Centre situated in Pelawatta, Battaramulla in Colombo District productively
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-08
decision_details_body: - The 'Ape Gama' Folk Heritage Exhibition Centre has been administrated as a project of the Central Cultural Fund from the beginning up to now and the State Ministry of National Heritage, Performing Arts and Rural Arts Promotion conducts its administration under the guidance of the Ministry of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs. Since neither a specific staff nor a Vote of Expenditure for the maintenance and administration has been allocated for the Centre, which is 13 acres 03 roods 25.1 perches in extent, it has been observed that it is being inactive. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs, to appoint a definite staff for maintaining the 'Ape Gama' Folk Heritage Exhibition Centre and to take necessary action to maintain the Centre in a formal manner, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development and operation of East Container Terminal and West Container Terminal of the Colombo South Port
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body:
- A Memorandum of Cooperation has been entered into between Sri Lanka, India and Japan for the development of the East Container Terminal of the Colombo South Port. The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2020-10-26 granted approval to appoint a Negotiating Committee to evaluate an investment proposal submitted by an Indian investor in accordance with the provisions of the said Agreement. Accordingly, the following proposals made by the Minister of Ports and Shipping based on the recommendations submitted by the aforesaid Negotiating Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

    • to operate the East Container Terminal as a fully owned container terminal of the Sri Lanka Ports Authority.
      
    • to take necessary action to develop the West Container Terminal of Colombo South Port as a Public Private Partnership by the parties nominated by India and Japan in association with the Sri Lanka Ports Authority on the basis of returning the same within 35 years, with a view to developing Colombo Port as a competitive port in this region and to adopt the International Agreements signed by the Government of Sri Lanka.

description: Production of railway passenger coaches domestically
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - The requirement of Railway passenger coaches, as at today is approximately 700 and it has been estimated that this could be increased up to 800 over the next 05 years. The available Railway passenger coaches are of various ages, 30% out of which are over 30 years old, 60% are over 25 to 30 years old and 10% have been in service for 12 years or less. 42% of the total Railway passenger coach requirement could be fulfilled by 160 coaches to be received from India and 140 coaches expected to be received from coach repairing project. Therefore, further 50% of total fleet need replacement or rehabilitation early. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport to select an investor adopting the Government Procurement Guidelines to produce 100 Railway passenger coaches with the participation of private sector as a remedy to prevailing situation, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendments to the Civil Procedure Code
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - The Civil Procedure Code makes provisions to set aside the judgment given by a court of law upon a request made by a defendant to the court of law with notice to the plaintiff stating that he has reasonable grounds for such default, within 14 days of the decree entered against him for default. It has been observed that by taking advantage of these provisions, it has enabled the defendant to employ delaying tactics and to resist a just claim of the plaintiff. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to amend the section 88(2) of the Civil Procedure Code, enabling to prevent such adverse conditions, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Industrial Disputes Act, No.43 of 1950 enabling to expedite the measures to be taken in respect of private sector employees subject to disciplinary inquiries or interdiction
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - The Labour Laws do not specify the period of time during which a final ruling should be given having conducted a formal disciplinary inquiry on such allegations in the event of an interdiction upon anti-disciplinary acts or acts of misconduct by Private Sector Employees. As a result, it has been found that in some cases, interdicted employees face various economic and social difficulties. Therefore, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Labour to amend the Industrial Disputes Act No.43 of 1950 incorporating provisions for the issuance of a final disciplinary order within 6 months from the date of interdiction of an employee and to pay half of the wage provided that the misconduct is not a financial fraud.

description: Restructuring of the Prisons Intelligence Unit
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - The need to restructure the existing prison intelligence unit so as to perform security duties, protection of special prisoners/suspects, riot control and security duties, without being limited to the functions of the said unit has been identified. Accordingly the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to restructure the existing Prison Intelligence Unit as the "Sri Lanka Prison Emergency Action Tactical Force" (SPEAT FORCE) enabling to assign identified specific duties in addition to the duties performed by ordinary prison officers, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Recommencement of the Bunkering Business by the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - The monopoly of the supply of bunkering oil was upheld by the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation under the "Lanka Maritime Services Limited" affiliated to Ceylon Petroleum Corporation and that business was opened to the Private Sector in 2004. Accordingly, the bonding storage facility which is maintained at the Sri Lanka Ports Authority has been sold to the Private Sector by the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation and as such, the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation has ceased to function from such bunkering business. Therefore, few suppliers are dealing in the process of importing bunkering oil in small scale, store that oil stocks at the Jaya Container Terminal (bonding storage) and then they are re-exported to ships sailing across the territorial sea of Sri Lanka. The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation possesses the capacity of importing fuel oil in bulk at favourable prices and supplying the same to licensed suppliers at competitive prices. Therefore, with the possibility of supplying of bunkering oil at competitive prices, it will be possible to increase the number of naval vessels sailing across the territorial waters of Sri Lanka. Under such circumstances, the Cabinet decided to grant its concurrence for the programme presented by Minister of Energy with regard to the recommencement of the import of bunkering oil business by the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation.

description: Amending Fertilizer Subsidy Scheme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body:
- Approximately 382,000 metric tons of fertilizer for paddy cultivation is provided free of charge to 1.45 million beneficiaries annually. Further, the opportunities have been provided to obtain subsidized fertilizers in the market for other non-paddy crops without any restrictions. It has been found that, under the existing methodology, the fertilizer subsidy for non-paddy crops is being utilized by other parties outside the target farmers, making it difficult for farmers to meet their fertilizer requirements when required. Due to this, it has also been found that, the Government has to incur more than the estimated cost for the fertilizer subsidy program annually. Taking these matters into consideration, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture to implement the fertilizer subsidy program in future as follows:

*	Implementing the fertilizer subsidy scheme for paddy in the same manner as at present for 2 seasons per year, subject to a maximum of 02 hectares per one cultivation season.
*	Providing opportunity to purchase fertilizer under the fertilizer subsidy programme up to a maximum of 05 hectares per year, subject to the quantities determined by the relevant research institutes for each non-paddy crops.

description: Streamlining Government Intervention in the Organic Fertilizer Production and Distribution Sectors
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - The need of directing Sri Lanka's agriculture to use organic fertilizer has been emphasized by the Government Policy Statement ''Vistas of Prosperity and Splendour''. In order to monitor the strategic plan of implementing this policy, it has been identified the need of having a Government institute with modern technology and research facilities, capable of carrying out production, marketing, research and development of organic fertilizers in line with international standards for direction of strategical arrangements to implement the said policy. Accordingly the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture for the conversion of Colombo Commercial Fertilizer Company Ltd. into an institution for production, formulation and distribution of organic fertilizer and chemical fertilizer of higher generations and undertaking research and development in the relevant field, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Project on Integrated Management of Forestry, Agriculture and Tourism sectors through Community based Ecosystem-approaches
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - Non-eco friendly land use plans have resulted in the breakdown of ecological balance thereby causing a number of social, environmental, economic and health problems at present. In order to control this situation, the Government has initiated various programmes and the need of having a programme with long term plans which is jointly implemented in the sectors of Agriculture, Tourism and Forestry has been identified. Accordingly, the “Project on Integrated Management of Forestry, Agriculture and Tourism sectors through Community based ecosystem approaches” has been designed to be implemented in the Malwathu Oya basin in Anuradhapura, Mannar, Vavuniya and Puttlam districts as a pilot project. It has been agreed to grant a credit facility of US$ 3.34 million under the Global Environment Facility of the United Nations Development Programme for this project. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to implement the said project during the period from 2021-2024, utilizing the said grant, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing lands in the Mahaveli regions on lease basis for commercial agriculture
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - The Government has taken measures to restrict the importation of identified food crops that could be cultivated within the country with a view to controlling unnecessary foreign exchange outflow. Accordingly, the importation of maize has been suspended and approximately 250,000 metric tons of maize required for the production of Thriposha and other animal food has to be produced domestically. In this context, it has been planned to provide underutilized 2,750 acres of Rambukkanoya area managed by the Sri Lanka Mahaweli Authority not belonging to the identified reservations, to the local agricultural investors on lease basis in view of encouraging them to produce maize in large scale domestically. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Irrigation to allocate the relevant blocks of land to the recognized local investors on lease basis for a period of one (01) year and to grant the relevant land blocks to the same investors on long - term lease basis as per the provisions of the State Land Ordinance upon the success of the cultivation in future, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Gazette Notification No.2160/33 dated 2020.01.30 issued, publishing the Motor Traffic (Restrictions) Regulations to Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - It has been reported that some container vehicles running under the Sedawatte railway bridge of the road section from Thotalanga junction to Kohilawatte junction of Colombo – Hanwella (AB 010) highway cause damages to the railway bridge due to the negligence of container drivers. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport to present the Gazette Notification No. 2160/33 dated 2020.01.30 issued in terms of the provisions of the Motor Traffic Act in Parliament in order to ban the travelling of all the vehicles which transport containers, other vehicles with more than 3.2m in total height above ground level and vehicles with a load height of more than 3.2m above ground level through the said road section, with a view to avoiding dangerous accidents caused by the same and to introduce alternative routes for those restricted vehicles, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Revising the Temporary Permit (MTA 37) issued by a Policeman
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - When conducting an investigation pertaining to an offence under section 135 (4) of the Motor Traffic Act, a Police officer would take charge the relevant driving license and issue a temporary permit. The specimen form relating to that has been published in the Extraordinary Gazette Notification dated 1951‑08‑25. Since, the contents in that temporary permit are inadequate at present, the then Minister in charge of the subject of transport issued the Gazette Notification No 2144/19 dated 2019‑10‑09 revising the said format to suit with the present requirements. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport to submit the said Gazette Notification to Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Mutual Cooperation between Diplomatic Academies / Training Institutions of BIMSTEC Member States
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) has been established in the year 1997 as a forum to further enhance the cooperation within the region of the Bay of Bengal. At present, seven (07) countries including Sri Lanka are members of this organisation. It has been proposed to enter into an MoU on Mutual Corporation between Diplomatic Academies / Training Institutions by the member countries. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Foreign Minister to adopt the proposed MoU at the 05th BIMSTEC Summit scheduled to be held in Sri Lanka in early of this year, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Resettlement of internally displaced landless families in the welfare centres in Jaffna District
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet of Ministers was granted previously for taking necessary measures for granting a block of land in extent of 20 perches at a cost of Rs. 700,000 per each for 381 landless families living in the welfare centres in Jaffna District, subject to the valuation of the Chief Valuer. 233 families have been identified as landless families out of 409 families currently in welfare centres in Jaffna District and they have made requests to obtain alternative lands in close proximity to their birth places. However, obtaining a 20 perch block of land at a sum of Rs. 700,000/- has been found to be difficult as per the current prices of lands in those areas. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development and Housing, to purchase blocks of land in extent of 10 - 20 perches from private owners subject to the valuation of Chief Valuer without exceeding aforesaid amount of money and provide them to the said families and to take necessary action to settle those families in the said lands expeditiously by preparing a mechanism to construct houses on those lands parallel to aforesaid task, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Hosting 55th Asian Development Bank (ADB) Annual Meeting in Sri Lanka in 2022
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - 	Approval of the Board of Governors of the Asian Development Bank has been received to hold its 55th Annual Meeting in Colombo. This meeting would be attended by approximately 3000-4000 participants including more than 30 Ministers of Finance, Governors of Central Banks from member countries, Chief Executives of major global banks and companies and other local and international dignitaries and media personnel. The proposed meeting is scheduled to be held for 04 days from 2022‑05‑02 to 2022‑05‑05 and a number of other meetings and functions related to this are to be held parallel to the said meeting. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, to make necessary arrangements to host the Annual Meeting of the Asian Development Bank in May, 2022 in Sri Lanka and to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) relevant to this with the Asian Development Bank, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Continues implementation of the Micro-finance Credit Facility Programme for the debt-ridden people of the Northern and North Central Provinces
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - The credit scheme with low interest rate introduced through Co-operative Rural Banks and Thrift & Credit Co-operative Societies, with the intention of getting the rural low income people who have become debt-ridden after obtaining loans from various micro finance credit schemes, out of the debt trap, is presently being implemented by 06 District Secretariats in the Northern and North Central Provinces. Under the said scheme, Rs. 542 million, as Rs. 292 million for Northern Province and Rs. 250 million for North Central Province, has been granted to the beneficiaries to the date and this money is maintained as a revolving fund of the said loan scheme. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance for continuous implementation of the relevant credit scheme by using the money of the said revolving fund, for the increase of the maximum credit limit granted under the same up to Rs. 100,000/- and for the reduction of the annual interest rate pertaining to the said loans from 9% to 6% in order to provide the debt-ridden people with a relief, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointing new members to the National Border Management Committee
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-02-01
decision_details_body: - ''The National Border Management Committee'' has been established to function as the focal point within the Government responsible for assessing high level risks and setting priorities and goals on all aspects of border management in Sri Lanka. Heads of the other institutions involved in the border management have been appointed as the ex-officio members of this Committee under the chairmanship of the Secretary, Ministry of Defence. The proposal made by H.E the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence to appoint the Chairman of the Sri Lanka Ports Authority, one of the important entity in the boarder management, the Chief of Defence Staff who have been entrusted the coordination activities among Tri Forces and the Ministry of Defence, and the Secretary to the Ministry in-charge of the subject of Fisheries as members of the said Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing 500,000 doses of AstraZeneca's COVISHIELD Vaccine by the Government of India to Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body: - The Hon. Prime Minister informed the Cabinet that the Indian High Commissioner has conveyed that the Government of India has decided to provide 500,000 doses of AstraZeneca's COVISHIELD vaccine to Sri Lanka taking into account the longstanding relationship between Sri Lanka and India and the cooperation experienced between the two countries during the last year in facing the COVID‑19 pandemic situation and that the stock of vaccine is scheduled to arrive in the country on the 28th of this month. The Cabinet of Ministers decided to convey the appreciation and gratitude of the Government of Sri Lanka  to the Government of India for  timely cooperation extended in the hour of need.

description: Amendments to the Regulations and Orders made under the Foreign Exchange Act No.12 of 2017
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body:
In terms of the provisions of the Foreign Exchange Act No.12 of 2017, the Minister in charge of the subject of Finance is entrusted the power of promulgating Regulations in order to implement the said Act subject to the Cabinet approval in consultation with the Monetary Board of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka. Accordingly, Regulations No.01 of 2017, Regulations No.02 of 2017 and Regulations No.03 of 2017 have been promulgated and Orders made under Section 8 and Section 31 of the Act have been issued. It has been found necessary to amend the said Regulations and Orders to suit with the present requirements. As such, the proposal made by  Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to take the following measures in accordance with the provisions of  the Foreign Exchange Act No.12 of 2017, was approved by the Cabinet. 
 
    • to promulgate the following Regulations and submit the same to Parliament for approval.
i.	Foreign Exchange  (Classes of Capital Transactions Undertaken Outside Sri Lanka by a Person Resident in Sri Lanka) Regulations 	No.01 of 2021 
ii.	Foreign Exchange  (Classes of Capital Transactions Undertaken in Sri 	Lanka by a Person Resident in Sri Lanka) Regulations No.02 of 2021 
iii.	Foreign Exchange  (Remittance of Funds by Emigrants) 	Regulation No.3 of 2021		
 vi.	Foreign Exchange (Classes of Miscellaneous Capital Transactions) Regulations No.4 of 2021
v.	Foreign Exchange  (Opening and Maintenance of Accounts for the purpose of engaging in Foreign Exchange Transactions) Regulations 	No.5 of 2021

    • to make Orders in accordance with  Section 8 and Section 31 of the 	said Act.

description: Submission of the Regulations issued under the Import and Export (Control) Act No.1 of 1969 in Parliament for approval
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body: - Necessary measures have been taken to restrict and regulate certain imported goods which may cause pressure on the foreign exchange rate. Accordingly, the proposal made by Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to submit the Gazette Extraordinary Notification dated 2021‑01‑05 issued imposing regulations under the Import and Export (Control) Act No.1 of 1969, in  Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of Katunayaka Industrial Zone
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body: - Nearly 150 investors have made requests to the Ministry of Industries to provide them with opportunities to initiate industries in the Western Province and it has been found that  approximately 11,500 job opportunities could be generated under  an investment of around Rs. 30,000 million by providing necessary facilities for the same. At present there are 08 industrial zones located in the Western Province and they are operating with their full capacity. Therefore, it has been found necessary to establish an industrial zone in the Western Province.  Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries to establish the Katunayaka Industrial Zone at a land block of 100 acres of State owned land called  Kaludiyawala Watta, belonging to Katana Divisional Secretariat Division to provide necessary facilities to commence industries such as rubber, plastics, medicines and allied products, electrical and electronic appliances, packaging, value added agricultural products and recycling industries by giving priority to garments and associated products, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement for supply of 14,000,000 bottles of 500ml Sodium Chloride Intravenous Infusion BP 0.9% w/v or Sodium Chloride Injection USP, 0.9% w/v
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body: - International Competitive Bidds have been invited for the procurement of the above drug which is used for volume replacement of the patients with Hypovolemia. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to award the said procurement to M/s. Sichuan Kelum Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd., China at a total C&F price of US$ 2.79 million as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Kuruwita-Erathna Sripada Road Development
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body: - Kuruwita-Erathna road, one of the three main routes used by Sripada pilgrims to worship Sripada, is used by more than one hundred thousand of pilgrims during a season. Due to the non repairing of naturally formed stairs situated in this lane for a long time, Sripada pilgrims are faced with difficulties.  Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Irrigation and State Minister of National Security, Home Affairs and Disaster Management to take necessary action to repair identified areas of the Kuruwita-Erathna road using the sleepers removed from railway rehabilitation activities, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Proposed Port related logistics sector development in Bloemandhal Area
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka Ports Authority has identified the urgent necessity of developing the   logistics facilities of Colombo Port to meet the growing demand with efficiency to enhance the competitiveness of the Port. Accordingly, Sri Lanka Ports Authority intends to establish a  state of art Port related logistics sector  in  Bloemandhal Area. As the first stage of the said programme, it is scheduled to  establish a large warehouse complex for  Less than Container Load (LCL), Full Container Load (FCL), Multi Country Consolidation (MCC), cold storage facility, entrepot cargo handling and other port related logistics activities. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports and Shipping to take necessary action to call for Request for Proposals to identify a suitable investor/ investors to implement the proposed project on Build, Operate, Transfer basis as a Public Private Partnership Project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of Elevated Expressway connecting Outer Circular Highway at Athurugiriyta to Kelaniya New Bridge via Rajagiriya
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body: - The Road Development Authority has conducted a feasibility study to construct an Elevated Expressway  from the new Kelani Bridge to the Athurugiriya Interchange on the Outer Circular Highway via Rajagiriya along the Port Access Elevated Expressway which is being constructed under the funds of Asian Development Bank. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of  Highways to take necessary action to call for Request for Proposals (RFP) to  implement the above project with 100% foreign financing on Build, Operate, Transfer (BOT) basis, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Conducting the Feasibility Study to implement the first Pumped Storage Hydro Power Plant in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body: - The intermittent nature and non-firmness of generation of power through certain renewable energy resources make it technically challenging to add more such energy plants into the main electricity grid. In order to face this situation and store excess generated capacity, it has been identified the necessity of establishing the “Pumped Storage Hydropower Plant”. Under the Long Term Generation Plan for the period of 2018 – 2037, it has been identified to operate a Pumped Storage Hydropower Plant in 03 phases from the year 2025 onwards. According to a study conducted in association with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), the Aranayake area  in the Ma oya Valley and Wewathenna area in Kandy, have been recognized as suitable for the construction of the proposed power plant. The Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) intends to identify the most suitable place out of those two locations and conduct a comprehensive feasibility study  in this regard.  There is a potential of securing the funds required for the purpose, out of the balance funds of the “Green Power Development and Energy Efficiency Improvement Investment Project” under the Asian Development Bank. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Power, to conduct a comprehensive feasibility study on the said project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Coconut Development Act to amalgamate all the Regulating State Institutions of the Coconut Sector
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body: - The Coconut Cultivation Board, Coconut Development Authority and the Coconut Research Institute have been established under the Coconut Development Act, No.46 of 1971 for the Coconut cultivation, industry and research areas. And, the Kapruka Fund Management Board has been established under the Kapruka Fund Act, No.31 of 2005. Even though the said institutions have been set up for coordinating all functions related to Coconut cultivation regulation, those institutions have failed to provide services to clients at the anticipated level due to inefficient coordination between the said institutions. Taking into consideration the duplication of certain functions discharged by the said institutions and clients having to liaise with several institutions to meet their requirements and incurring of a considerable cost for its maintenance,  it has been decided to amalgamate these 4 institutions into one establishment. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Plantation, to amend the Coconut Development Act, No.46 of 1971, facilitating the amalgamation of the said institutions and setting up of a new institution namely, ''Coconut Cultivation and Allied Industries Development Authority'', was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Enacting a new Petroleum Resources Development Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body: - Even though the Petroleum Resources Development Act, No.26 of 2003 has widely identified the requirement of local Petroleum and gas exploration and developing production industry, it has been observed that those sectors have not been interpreted properly for its management. Accordingly, during the deliberations held with the relevant parties, it was identified the necessity of revoking the said Act and formulating a new Act to differentiate the required interpretations, regulations, policy and national operator. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Energy, to revoke the Petroleum Resources Development Act, No.26 of 2003 and to draft a new Act, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining consultancy services for planning of construction of Courts
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body: - In the light of administration of justice, a large number of cases are pending before the courts in Sri Lanka and as a relief for the said issue, action is being taken to increase the number of Judges. The other facilities of courts are to be met concurrently and it has been planned to construct 100 new court houses island‑wide within the next 3 years. Under this plan, it has also been planned to construct multi‑storey court buildings and to improve the existing buildings. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice, to obtain the required consultancy services from the Central Engineering Consultancy Bureau (CECB)   which is fully fledged with experience in constructing court buildings, for the implementation of the said project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of Diplomatic Relations with Liechtenstein
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body: - Liechtenstein, a small land locked country situated between Switzerland and Austria is a country with Parliamentary Democracy and a Constitutional Monarch as its Head of State. It is a highly industrialized country which manufactures mainly pharmaceuticals, precision instruments and electronics and is considered as one of the world's richest countries. Last year, its Gross Domestic Product (GDP) was US$ 5.8 billion and the per capita income was around US$ 143,700.   Liechtenstein, being a member of the United Nations' Organization, is also a member state of the European Economic Area with low income tax regime that has attracted investments through developed banking system, and maintains diplomatic relations with many countries including India and Pakistan. With a view to improving the friendship and cooperation between the two countries at the bilateral and multilateral levels, the Government of Liechtenstein has expressed its interest to establish diplomatic relations with the Government of Sri Lanka. It will enable Sri Lanka to attract investments and high spending tourists by establishing diplomatic relations between the two countries. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Foreign Minister, to establish diplomatic relations with Liechtenstein, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Increasing the Daily Wage of Plantation Sector Workers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body:
- In accordance with the provisions in the ''Plantation Workers' Wages Collective Agreement 2019 – 2021'', the Plantation sector employees are entitled for a daily wage of Rs.750/- including a Fixed Price Allowance of Rs.50/- and for an another allowance called ''Over kilo rate'' when exceeding the amount of kilos related to the productivity.

It was proposed to provide a daily wage of Rs.1,000/- to the Plantation sector through the budget proposals presented in Parliament in November, 2020. Even though several deliberations have been conducted with the signatories  to the ''Plantation Workers' Wages Collective Agreement 2019 – 2021'' for the implementation of the said proposal, the Employers' Federation of Ceylon representing the Planters' Association which is one party to the said Collective Agreement, has proposed to increase the daily wage up to Rs.920/-. Taking these matters into consideration, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour, to take necessary steps enabling the increase of the daily wage of the Plantation sector workers up to Rs.1,000/- through the Wages Board, for the implementation of the said budget proposal, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Revising the existing Estate Housing Scheme to provide safer habitats targeting the entire Plantation Community
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body:
- From the year 2000 up to now, the ''Estate Housing Scheme'' for the construction of new houses to replace Line Rooms for the Estate community has been implemented in different ways. At present, 02 projects are being carried out namely, the project of providing a single house in extent of 550 square feet with 07 perches free hold land ownership under the Government sponsorship and the project for providing a single house in extent of 550 square feet, in collaboration with the Governments of India and Sri Lanka. Since it creates a discrepancy due to the dissimilarity of the criterion applied for providing houses under these schemes, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development and Housing, to follow a single common procedure for providing houses to the Estate community and to pursue action as follows under the said procedure, was approved by the Cabinet.

*  removal of the existing Line Rooms and construction of new houses on the same location.

*	implementing housing schemes in other locations in case there is a risk of disasters such as floods/landslides and there is insufficient space at the locations of the Line Rooms.

*	construction of the first phase of the house with 550 square feet at a cost of Rs.1.3 million, enabling to convert the same into 02 floors later.

*	allocation of 03 perches in addition, to each housing beneficiary for  animal husbandry and home gardening purposes.

*	recovery of only 50% of the value of constructing houses from the beneficiaries and granting of a period of 20 years for the purpose.
*	Providing facilities for tentative accommodation at another place in close proximity of those Line Rooms until new houses will be constructed at the same location.

description: Report of the Auditor General on the President's Fund - 2018
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-25
decision_details_body: - In terms of Section 9(2) of the President's Fund Act, No.7 of 1978 to be read with the provisions of Article 154(3) of the Constitution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, the Auditor General has audited the President's Fund pertaining to the financial year ended on 31st December, 2018. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, to table the said Report of the Auditor General pertaining to the financial year 2018 in accordance with the provisions of Section 10 of the said Fund Act, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on the Return and Readmission of Persons between the Commonwealth of Australia and the Government of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-18
decision_details_body: - A proposal has been made to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding between Australia and Sri Lanka incorporating the provisions for the exchange of persons staying in violation of the immigration laws between two countries. The said Memorandum of Understanding ensures a safe and orderly return to their country of residence. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Irrigation and State Minister of National Security, Home affairs and Disaster Management to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding between the Commonwealth of Australia and the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka on the Return and Readmission of Persons, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Decisions and Recommendations of the Presidential Commission of Inquiry to Investigate and Inquire into and Obtain Information
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-18
decision_details_body: - H.E the President has appointed a Presidential Commission of Inquiry to investigate and inquire into and obtain information in relation to alleged victimizations of Public Officers, Employees of Public Corporations, Members of Armed Forces and Police Service, who were holding posts during the period commencing from 08th January 2015 and ending on 16th November 2019. The Report of the said Commission has been submitted by H.E the President. Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E the President to submit the said report in Parliament and to take necessary action to implement the decisions and recommendations of the said Report, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Installation of Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems in Small Island
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-18
decision_details_body: - The Ceylon Electricity Board with the financing of the Asian Development Bank implements the 'Supporting Electricity Supply Reliability Improvement Project (SESRIP)'. Under the said project, international competitive bids have been called to install Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems in Nagadeepa, Delft and Analitive islands utilizing the widely accessible energy resources to improve the efficiency of the prevailing electricity network. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minster of Power to award the relevant contract to the M/s Sinosoar – Etechwin Joint Venture in China, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendments to the Penal Code (Statutory Rape)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-18
decision_details_body:
- Section 363 of the Penal Code defines Rape as a serious crime and the Penal Code also includes facts relating to the specific offences which fall within the ambit of that crime. However, there seems to be an inconsistency in the law regarding the Statutory Rape. Further, a study conducted by the Medico Legal Society of Sri Lanka has pointed out the need to amend the provisions of the Penal Code relating to the statutory rape.
	
	Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft amending legislation to the Penal Code as suit to the present day requirements, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendments to the Civil Procedure Code Matrimonial Actions -
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-18
decision_details_body: - Amendments to the Civil Procedure Code Matrimonial Actions -

description: Sign Language Draft Bill
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-18
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2010‑09‑08 to accept the Sign Language as a recognized language. As a considerable number of hearing impaired people reside in Sri Lanka, making provisions to accept sign language as a recognized mode of communication would empower the hearing impaired people, in accessing their educational requirements, legal affairs, health facilities, public and personal services. Accordingly, the need to establish the sign language as a recognized language in Sri Lanka has been identified. Therefore, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to make necessary provisions enabling to accept the sign language as a formal mode of communication by an act of Parliament and to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft legislation for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendments to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, No.6 of 2006, Prevention of Money Laundering Act, No.5 of 2006 and the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, No.25 of 2005
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-18
decision_details_body:
- Approval of the Cabinet was granted at its meeting held on 05th May 2010 to make amendments to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, to address the deficiencies recognized by the Legal Review Committee and Asia Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) as approved by the National Coordinating Committee (NCC) on Anti Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism and in compliance with the recommendations of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF).

Accordingly, the task of formulating draft amending legislation has been initiated and subsequently, the Asia Pacific Group on Money Laundering has identified several further amendments to be made in addition to those which have already been recognized during its mutual assessment. The draft prepared by a Committee comprising the representatives of the relevant agencies such as the Attorney General's Department, Legal Draftsman's Department and the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) was also revisited by the International Monetary Fund Technical Assistance Mission in March, 2017. As such, with a view to addressing the issues so identified, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance to amend the following Acts and to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft legislation for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

* 	Financial Transactions Reporting Act, No.6 of 2006
* 	Prevention of Money Laundering Act, No.5 of 2006. 
* 	Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, No.25 of 2005-

description: Recommendations of the Cabinet Sub Committee on Legislation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-18
decision_details_body:
- The proposals submitted to the Cabinet regarding the amendment of the following Acts, have been referred to the Cabinet Sub‑Committee on Legislation for its recommendations. As such, taking into consideration the recommendations made by the said Sub‑Committee, Cabinet decided to instruct the Legal Draftsman to formulate the amending legislation for the purpose.

* 	Immigrants and Emigrants Act (repealing the existing Immigrants and Emigrants Act, No.20 of 1948 and the relevant amendments and replacement of a new Act)

* 	Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act, No.12 of 2006 and Provincial Councils (Transfer of Stamp Duty) Act, No.13 of 2011

* 	National Minimum Wage of Workers Act, No.3 of 2016

* 	Community Based Corrections Act, No.46 of 1999

* 	Section 53 of the Penal Code (provisions relating to death sentence on minors)

description: Collaboration between M/s CINEC Campus (Pvt.) Limited., Mahapola Ports & Maritime Academy of Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) and Sri Lanka Port Management and Consultancy Services Limited (SLPMCS) for design and delivery of Maritime Training Programmes
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-18
decision_details_body:
- It is essential to have a highly skilled and disciplined labour force which may be utilized for the ports and maritime industry for the growth and rapid expansion of the ports and maritime sector. The Mahapola Ports & Maritime Academy within the purview of the Sri Lanka Ports Authority is discharging the said functions. With a view to securing the related port services and other services, the Sri Lanka Port Management and Consultancy Services Private Limited (SLPMCS) was established with the contribution of the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA), Ceylon Shipping Corporation, Colombo Dock Yard PLC, Ceylon Association of Shipping Agents (CASA) and the Ceylon Shipping Lines Ltd.. 
	
And, M/s CINEC Campus (Pvt.) Ltd. is another approved maritime training institute in Sri Lanka.

It has been proposed to share knowledge and resources between the Sri Lanka Ports Authority, Mahapola Ports & Maritime Academy, Sri Lanka Port Management and Consultancy Services Private Limited and M/s CINEC Campus (Pvt.) Ltd. for achieving the purposes of promoting the seafaring career within the country, providing financial facilities to the trainees enrolled to the courses and promoting the Sri Lankan seafarers in foreign countries. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports and Shipping to authorize the Sri Lanka Ports Authority to enter into a collaboration with M/s CINEC Campus Pvt. Ltd. for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Granting relief to electricity consumers affected from COVID-19 Outbreak
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-18
decision_details_body:
- Taking into consideration the proposals submitted by the Minister of Power pertaining to provision of reliefs to electricity consumers affected by COVID-19 pandemic situation and those submitted by the Minister of Tourism regarding provision of reliefs to the tourism related institutions on payment of electricity and water bills, approval of the Cabinet was granted to pursue action as follows:

* 	to provide a grace period of 06 months from the date of electricity bill to the domestic, commercial and industrial electricity consumers in the areas which were under the continuous lockdown for more than 14 days, to pay the electricity bills for the relevant period and not to disconnect the electricity supply until such time.
* 	to allow the Cinema Halls registered at the National Film Corporation to settle the electricity bills from March to December, 2020 in 12 equal installments from the date of electricity bill and not to disconnect the electricity supply until such time.

* 	to allow the registered accommodation providers of the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA) to settle the cumulative electricity and water bills from 01st March 2020 to 28th February 2021 in 12 equal installments and not to disconnect the relevant supplies until such time.

description: Providing Tariff Concession to Mongolia under the Asia Pacific Trade Agreement (APTA)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-18
decision_details_body: - Mongolia has officially become a party to the Asia Pacific Trade Agreement (APTA) on 29th September 2020 to which Sri Lanka has also been a Participating State. Accordingly, Sri Lanka as a Participating State, is supposed to reciprocally exchange tariff concessions with Mongolia. Mongolia, as similar to Bangladesh and Laos who are parties to the said trade agreement, is also entitled to acquire the same tariff concessions provided under the relevant agreement. As such, the proposal made by the Foreign Minister to provide the said tariff concessions and to conduct negotiations with Mongolia to identify the reciprocal tariff concessions to be further agreed on between parties, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of a dedicated unit for International Cooperation under the purview of the Foreign Ministry
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-18
decision_details_body: - With a view to achieving a robust economic diplomacy approach in the context of changing global economic and political environment along with the emerging Asia-centric economic landscape, it has been identified the essentiality of establishing a dedicated unit for formulating policies relating to economic diplomacy within the purview of the Foreign Ministry for the purpose of coordinating the functions of all key economic institutions. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Foreign Minister to establish a special unit for International Cooperation comprising the experts in the relevant fields, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of a bridge across Benthara river along the Ittepana Horawala Thotupola road in Ittepana
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - The Road Development Authority (RDA) has planned to construct a new bridge and its approaches across Benthara River along the Ittepana‑Horawala‑Thotupola road in Ittepana. The proposed bridge is about 160m in length and the total carriageway width is 10.4 m. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Highways, to construct the said bridge under the “100,000 km of Roads Improvement Project”, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Project for the establishment of a Trade Centre on the State land adjoining the Rajarata University, Mihinthale
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - Through the “Vistas of Prosperity and Splendour”, the Policy Statement of the Government, medium term plans are being formulated for increasing the number of students who have sat the G.C.E. (Advanced Level) Examination and gained entrance to universities and in this backdrop, the number of students gaining admission to the universities will increase. This will consequently escalate the expenditure incurred on the financial facilities provided by the Mahapola Higher Education Scholarship Trust Fund. Attention has been paid to invest funds of the said Scholarship Fund in other investment avenues with the objective of developing the Fund, generating income through long term stable stream of revenue and achieving direct development through investments. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade, to appoint a Committee representing the other relevant Ministries and institutions to implement a project for the establishment of a Trade Center on a plot of State land of 300 acres adjoining the Rajarata University, Mihinthale in the Anuradhapura District and to formulate an integrated plan on the implementation of the said project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on the implementation of the Project regarding ‘Connecting the Sri Lankan Villages to the International Market’
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - The objective of the project on “Connecting the Sri Lankan Villages to the International Market” is to develop a network between the local industrialists and the international market aiming at People Centric Economic Development in the country. The State Ministry of Samurdhi, Household Economy, Micro Finance, Self‑Employment and Business Development has implemented the “Economic Empowerment and Rural Development Programme – 2020” under the Department of Samurdhi Development and, the “Model Village on Samurdhi Products” is one of its major sub programmes. Through this sub programme also, it is expected to recognize the local industrialists intending to move quality products of the rural community to the international market. As such, the Cabinet decided to grant its concurrence to the proposal made by the Foreign Minister, to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) by the State Ministry of Samurdhi, Household Economy, Micro Finance, Self‑Employment and Business Development with the State Ministry of Regional Cooperation, for the implementation of the “Connecting the Sri Lankan Villages to the International Market” project through an institutional network which has the potential of building a mechanism for covering all districts in the country.

description: Procurement for the supply of 17,000 Vials of Tenecteplase Injection 40mg Vial
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - International Competitive Bids have been called for the procurement of this injection that has been used for treatment of patients who have suffered from heart attacks. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health, to award this procurement, to Ms. Boehringer Ingelheim India (Pvt.) Ltd. of India, at a total cost of USD 7.82 million, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement for the supply of 300,000 bottles of Human Albumin Solution BP/Ph Eur, 20% in 50ml bottles
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - International Competitive Bids have been called for the procurement of this drug that has been used for treatment of patients with kidney diseases. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health, to award the procurement for the supply of 300,000 bottles of Human Albumin Solution BP/Ph Eur, 20% in 50ml bottles, to Ms. Reliance Life Science Pvt. Ltd. India, at a total cost of USD 6.27 million, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement for the supply of 1,000,000 Pre-filled Syringe of Enoxaparin Sodium Injection, 6000IU in 0.6ml
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - International Competitive Bids have been called for the procurement of Enoxaparin Sodium that has been used for treatment of patients with heart diseases. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health, to award the procurement for the supply of 1,000,000 Pre‑filled Syringe of Enoxaparin Sodium Injection, 6,000IU in 0.6ml, to Ms. Slim Pharmaceuticals (Pvt) Ltd., at a total delivered price to Medical Supply Division (MSD) of Sri Lanka Rupees 695 million, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into an Agreement for a research project to eliminate toxic chemicals in drinking water
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - It has been proposed to enter into an Agreement between the University of Peradeniya and the University of Sri Jayawardenapura in collaboration with the Robert Gordon University, United Kingdom, pertaining to the research project funded by the Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC). Through the proposed project, it is expected to invent an inexpensive and hygienic biological solution that can be produced using natural organisms to eliminate the highly toxic Cyanotoxin released from the Blue-Green Algae that has grown due to contamination of drinking water sources which is considered to be the cause for spreading of kidney disease in Sri Lanka. It is proposed to provide Sterling Pounds 0.3 million by the Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council for the said project. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Education, to enter into the relevant Agreement between the University of Peradeniya and the University of Sri Jayawardenapura in collaboration with the Robert Gordon University, United Kingdom, for the implementation of the said project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the Pirivena Development Fund Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - The Government makes an allocation of Rs.4,500 million per year, in respect of the Piriven education. At present, the Pirivenas have been classified and registered as Maha Pirivenas, Mulika Pirivenas, Vidyayathana Pirivenas, Bilingual Pirivenas, Special Pirivenas and Buddhist Seela Matha Education Institutes and, currently 62,240 students are studying at those institutes. With a view to conducting Piriven education in a more formalized manner, the proposal made by the Minister of Education, to take necessary action to establish a Piriven Development Fund, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Design, Purchasing, Testing, Supervision of Installation and Commissioning of two (02) Nos. of Generator Stators in Unit 01 and Unit 02 machines at the Victoria Power Station - (Agenda Item No.25)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - The Victoria Power Station was commissioned in 1984, with an installed capacity of 210MW comprising three (03) 70MW units. A Technical Committee has been appointed to study the refurbishment to be made for the smooth functioning of the said Power Station in the next 30 years. The above Committee has recommended the installation of two (02) Generator Stators in Units 01 and 02 at the Power Station. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Power to adopt the procurement process and select a suitable institution for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement of 200 Nos. New Low Floor Buses for the Sri Lanka Transport Board
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - The State Ministry of Vehicle Regulation, Bus Transport Services and Train Compartments and Motor Car Industry has planed to launch a public transport service with modern facilities in Colombo and suburbs with park and ride facility. For this purpose, it has been identified the need to purchase 200 buses suitable for short distance travel with more passenger comfort than the existing buses. Accordingly the proposal made by the Minister of Transport to purchase 200 high quality low floor buses following the limited competitive bidding procedure from reputable local companies and to secure necessary funds for this purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Assistance to and Protection of Victims of Crimes and Witnesses Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - The Protection of Victims of Crime and Witnesses Act, No.4 of 2015 provides a host of benefits to victims and witnesses. However, in accordance with the provisions of Section 10 of the Act, a request should be made to the Court of Appeal for bail causing severe inconveniences to the suspects and the accused. In particular, since the Court of Appeal is located in Colombo, the suspects residing in remote areas have had difficulty in filing the bail application, it has been found appropriate to amend the Act by substituting the High Court for the Court of Appeal for the purpose of granting bail to such persons. Further, it has also been identified that it is appropriate to amend the provision that "A suspect shall be placed on remand till the end of the trial in respect of the offence which he had been enlarged on bail" by substituting the phrase "A suspect placed on remand for such period as may be considered reasonable by the court". Accordingly the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to initiate necessary measures to amend the Protection of Victims of Crime and Witnesses Act, No.04 of 2015, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Family Law Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - The law relating to marriage, divorce, separation and the procedure thereto is laid down in the Marriage Registration Ordinance No.19 of 1907 and in the Civil Procedure Code. The need to amend the provisions of the Ordinance to suit to the present has been identified. Accordingly, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of justice to study the legal situation prevailing in other countries on family law by an of experts committee and take necessary action to draft a detailed Family Law bill covering all areas such as divorce, nullity, separation, alimony, custody of children and division of property.

description: Amendments to the Tea Control Act, No.51 of 1957
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body:
- Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2016‑05‑10 to amend the Tea Control Act, No.51 of 1957. Accordingly, the Legal Draftsman has prepared a draft bill and the proposal made by the Minister of Plantation to further amend the said bill incorporating the following provisions, was approved by the Cabinet.

*	To incorporate an interpretation as “Reclaimable Tea” for tea that is separated after grading in the manufacturing process of Tea Factories.

*	To designate the remnant after further reclaiming made tea from reclaimable tea as “Refuse Tea”.

*	To incorporate legal provisions affected to tea processors including registration of them, issuance of licenses to them and administration.

description: Amendment of the Land Acquisition Act, No.9 of 1950
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - The long period of time taken to follow the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, No.9 of 1950 presently being in force, has caused impediments for various accelerated development activities implemented by the Government. The absence of following an unitary methodology in paying compensation for the lands acquired under the provisions of the said Act and having to spend a lot of time for paying compensation are the leading factors from among them. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Lands to take necessary action to amend the said Act to suit to the present day requirements enabling to acquire lands following a simple procedure and to pay compensation under an unitary methodology accordingly by minimizing the time taken to acquire lands, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the maximum limit of compensation of the compensation formula implemented under the Termination of Employment of Workman (Special Provisions) Act, No.45 of 1971
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - Termination of Employment of Workman (Special Provisions) Act, No.45 of 1971 amended by the Act No.12 of 2003 has been enacted to grant relief in terminating the service of workmen.
