In terms of the provisions of the said Act, a formula has been introduced to determine the compensation to be paid to the workmen when terminating their service. Accordingly, based on the Regulations imposed by the Minister of Labour, the amount will be determined, considering their period of service. Since, a provision to the effect that the compensation computed in terms of the aforesaid formula shall not exceed Rs.1,250,00 has also been incorporated into the Regulations, it has been found that, the compensation entitled to workmen receiving higher monthly salaries in the event of unfair dismissal from service or the closure of institutions remains at a lower level. Taking those issues into consideration, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour to increase the maximum limit of compensation from Rs.1,250,000 to Rs.2,500,00, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Marketing Pure Ceylon Tea through Online or Offline Platform in China
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - A proposal is made to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Sri Lanka Tea Board (SLTB) and Fujian Starchina International Trade Company Limited, Fujian Province, China, a subsidiary of Benny Tea Industry Company Ltd which is mainly engaged in tea imports, exports, e-business in clearing operations for marketing Pure Ceylon Tea through Online or Offline Platform in China. In terms of the said MoU, the said company has extended its willingness to set up a 5 G Online marketing platform which assists for warehousing and delivery network of China for online promotion and marketing of Ceylon Tea Brand name, in addition to the normal delivery of Ceylon Tea to China. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Plantation to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Sri Lanka Tea Board (SLTB) and Starchina International Trade Company Limited for marketing Pure Ceylon Tea through Online or Offline Platform in China, taking the advantage of potential opportunities for Ceylon Tea within the China tea market, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Importation of frozen coconut kernel to use for coconut kernel based industries
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2017‑12‑12 to import coconut kernel, subject to certain conditions, upon the insufficient supply of local coconut production for the coconut kernel based industries. Accordingly, 2,542 metric tons of coconut kernel have been imported during a period of 08 months. However, it has been estimated that there would be a shortage of 250 million nuts during this year. Therefore, the Cabinet decided to grant its concurrence for the proposals made by the Minister of Plantation for taking necessary action to import coconut kernel, subject to the same terms and conditions adopted previously, if the bi-monthly production of coconut remains less than 400 million continuously for 04 months.

description: Allocating a land on long term lease basis to the Pelwatte Diary Industries Ltd.
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by the Minister of Lands to allocate a state owned land in extent of 22 hectares located at Buttala Divisional Secretariat Division to Pelwatte Diary Industries Ltd on long term lease basis for a period of 30 years, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Standard Operating Procedures for automobile manufacturing, assembling and manufacturing of spare parts in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - A high potential exists to develop automobile industry in Sri Lanka which is rapidly developing in the world and there is an urgency for a clear guidance on existing rules/ regulations and procedures related to the same. Accordingly, the proposed “Standard Operating Procedure which includes domestic value addition formula and matrix” has been developed with the consent of the relevant government agencies and the industrialists and with the assistance of the professionals of the sector as well, having done a lengthy study on the relevant procedures of the automobile industry. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries to implement the provisions containing the said Operating Procedure, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Gazette Notifications published under Sri Lanka Export 	Development Act, No.40 of 1979 to Parliament for approval
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - The Gazette Notification dated 2020‑10‑28 was issued to amend the CESS Levy applicable to the import of footwear under the provisions of Sri Lanka Export Development Act, No.40 of 1979. Subsequently, the Gazette Notification dated 2020‑10‑29 was issued to further amend the provisions coming under the said Gazette and to revise the CESS Levy applicable to another few commodities. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade to submit the said Gazette Notification to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Research Project called “Multi-intervention strategy to improve Hypertension prevention and management within Sri Lanka's integrated primary care service delivery model”
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body:
- Excessive consumption of salt exceeding the daily prescribed quantities causes hypertension and other cardiovascular diseases. At present, Sri Lanka makes use of the WHO - PEN package for diagnosis and control of cardiovascular diseases when supplying primary health care services and HEARTS package was recently introduced by the World Health Organization (WHO) as an extension of the same package. When moving to the new package, number of requirements have to be accomplished such as utilizing a protocol for the management of hypertension, improving the required technology, developing algorithms for treatment, training staff, preparation of training manuals, updating the health information systems as well as provision of required information through formulating a communication package for minimizing the usage of salt at home.

It has been scheduled to obtain the required funds for the purpose from an organization called Resolve to Save Lives, an international non - government organization as a research grant and an Agreement should be entered into with the institution called Vital Strategies to carry out relevant research under the grant. Accordingly, proposal made by the Minister of Health to enter into the relevant Agreement for the implementation of the research project called “Multi-intervention strategy to improve Hypertension prevention and management within Sri Lanka's integrated primary care service delivery model”, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Allocation of lands from State Plantations managed by companies to develop estate schools
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - With a view to developing 354 estate schools belonging to 07 districts, the Cabinet decided at its meeting held on 2018‑04‑10, to allocate maximum 02 acres from the State lands with low productivity managed by the Plantation Companies located adjacent to aforesaid schools. In addition to the above schools, there are another 491 schools and a maximum of 02 acres of land should be allocated for those schools as well upon the necessity. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to allocate blocks of land for the said schools from the State Plantations managed by the Plantation Companies, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Extension of the grace period agreed for the payment of salaries to employees of the private sector in the wake of Covid - 19 triggered crisis
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body:
- At a meeting of the Task Force established with the participation of employers, trade unions, the National Labour Advisory Council, the Ministry of Labour and the Department of Labour on the payment of salaries to the employees of the private sector in the wake of crisis situation caused by the Covid-19 pandemic, it has been agreed to grant relief such as retaining job of employees, providing each employee with proportionate opportunities enabling all employees to serve, payment of 50% from his/her last drawn monthly salary or Rs.14,500/-, whichever is more favorable to the employee if employees are requested stay at home and payment of EPF and ETF contributions by the employer according to the so paid salary. 

	Accordingly, taking into account the serious crisis faced by the tourism sector on the restrictions of movement and travel due to the Covid - 19 outbreak, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour to extend the period of the above relief measures up to the end of March, 2020 to grant the same for the institutions in the tourism sector and also for the institutions of other sectors which are unable to maintain their businesses due to the Covid - 19 pandemic, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Sultanate of Oman on mutual visa exemption for holders of Diplomatic, Special, Service and Official Passports
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by the Minister of Irrigation and State Minister of National Security, Home Affairs and Disaster Management to enter into an MoU between the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Sultanate of Oman on mutual visa exemption for holders of Diplomatic, Special, Service and Official Passports with a view to facilitating citizens of these two countries to travel between two countries and further strengthening their mutual corporation, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Humanitarian Demining Programme with Demining Organizations
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-11
decision_details_body: - The Humanitarian Demining Programme has been in operation since 2002 and at present, 02 foreign NGOs and two local NGOs are involved in this process. In addition, Sri Lanka Army Humanitarian Demining Unit is also in these operations. The demining organizations are supervised and guided by the National Mine Action Centre. 197.66 sq km has been cleared so far and 15.39 km remains to be cleared. For this purpose, the National Mine Action Centre enters into MoUs annually with the local and foreign NGOs and accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development and Housing to sign the relevant MoUs up to 2023, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Vaccine application by Sri Lanka to Covax facility
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body:
- Covax facility is a global initiative that brings governments and manufactures together to ensure the equitable access and distribution of the COVID-19 vaccine when a safe and efficient vaccine is produced. Under this, the manufacture and the development of COVID - 19 vaccine is accelerated and a fair and equitable access for every country in the World is guaranteed. 

Sri Lanka has already entered into Covax mechanism and GAVI (Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunization) which includes also the World Health Organization, has confirmed that Sri Lanka is eligible for the official development assistance to receive doses of Covid-19 vaccine through the Covax facility.

In order to obtain the vaccine facility, countries were invited to submit vaccine request application form in two phases and the first and part A of the Vaccine application form containing technical details of the target group and vaccine storage capacity has to be submitted before 2020‑12‑07. Sri Lanka has submitted the said forms on time. Applications are required to be submitted before 2021‑01‑08 for the part two of the vaccine request to obtain the vaccines and for entering into relevant indemnification agreement. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health to submit the part B of the vaccine request to Covax and to enter into an Agreement with the manufacturer at the time when the vaccines are allocated by Covax facility, following the instructions of the Attorney General, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Detailed Report of the Five Member Committee appointed to probe the tense situation erupted at the Mahara Prison on 2020-11-29
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body: - The Minister of Justice appointed a Five Member Committee to conduct a formal investigation on the tense situation erupted at the Mahara Prision on 2020‑11‑29. The said committee has submitted its report under three main facts, i.e. the prevention of the prison congestion, welfare of the prison inmates and the prison administration. Accordingly, the Cabinet considered the information of the aforesaid report submitted by the Minister of Justice.

description: Paddy purchasing programme during 2020/21 Maha Season
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body:
- Arrangements have been made by the the Paddy Marketing Board to purchase paddy at a guaranteed price to minimize the unexpected fall in prices for paddy, since the harvest for the 2020/21 Maha Season is scheduled to begin from the second week of January. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture to implement the Paddy Purchasing Programme during 2020/21 Maha season as follows, was approved by the Cabinet.
    • To purchase a kilogram of standard Nadu paddy with 14% moisture at 	Rs. 50.00 per kg and paddy with 14%-22% moisture at Rs. 44.00 per 	kg.
    • To purchase a kilogram of standard Samba paddy with 14% moisture at Rs. 52.00 per kg and paddy with 14% -22% moisture at Rs. 46.00 per kg.
    • To purchase paddy by the Paddy Marketing Board from farmers in minor and major irrigation who receive fertilizer subsidy, according to the cultivation extent; 1000 kg from farmers with at least 1-1.5 hectare and 1500 kg from farmers with more than 1.5 and up to 2 hectare.

description: Proposed Colombo Port City Commission Law
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body: - Attention has been drawn on converting the Colombo Port City a Special Economic Zone with a wider scope and a Regional Centre of Excellence focusing on the service economy serving the Indian sub-continent and South-East Asia in line with the “Vistas of Prosperity and Splendour” the policy statement of the present Government. For this purpose, it has been found necessary to create an active environment that can compete with the investment hubs such as Dubai, Singapore, and Hong Kong by attracting investors, entrepreneurs, innovators, companies, financial institutions through a well-structured and competitive legal, tax and regulatory, and dispute resolution regime. Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E. the President to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft legislation for the Colombo Port City Commission Law to be on par with the structure expected by the government so as to attract international investors and with the national requirement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Publishing 'National Gem and Jewellery (Gem Mining License) 	Regulations 	2020'
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body: - In terms of the provisions of State Gem Corporation by-law imposed 	under the provisions of the State Gem Corporation Act No. 3 of 1971, a 	license for gem industry could be obtained for the lands with clear and 	individual ownership and / or freehold ownership only. Accordingly, a person 	who acquires a land on a lease basis for gem mining cannot apply for a gem 	mining license . However, it has been observed that approximately 20% of 	the applications submitted are for the lands owned on shared rights and/or 	leasehold rights. As such, the proposal for the submission of regulations 	published in the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No. 2165/1 dated 	2020‑03‑02 by the Minister of Industries as per the provisions of the National 	Gem and Jewellery Authority Act No.50 of 1993 in Parliament for approval so 	as to issue license for such applicants as well, was approved by the 	Cabinet.

description: Establishment of a Facilitation Centre for Hambantota Port related Industrial Zones and Industrial Development in the Southern Province
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body: - In terms of the provisions of the Industrial Promotion Act No. 46 of 1991, it is possible to establish the Industrial Zones/ Science Parks and provide necessary facilities for the same. Action has been taken to establish several Industrial Zones inline with the infrastructure development carried out in Southern Province recently. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries to establish a Smart One Stop Shop in the vicinity of the Hambanthota Port comprising of representatives of all relevant institutions enabling to provide the local and foreign investors who are interested to invest in such Industrial Zones with the necessary approvals and facilities at a single location and to carry out the activities of the said office with the direction of the Regional Industrial Service Centre in the Southern Province under the direct supervision of the Ministry of Industries, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Sri Lanka Rupavahini Corporation Act, No.6 of 1982
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Rupavahini Corporation established under the Sri Lanka Rupavahini Corporation Act, No.6 of 1982 has preformed a significant duty in the field of media in Sri Lanka for the period of past 38 years. However, it has identified the necessity to change the composition of the Board of Directors of the Sri Lanka Rupavahini Corporation which has been vested with the power to make decisions and implement them in order to deal appropriately with the current intense media competition. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Mass Media to amend the said Act enabling to increase the composition of the Board of Directors which currently consists of 07 members up to 09 members including a representative from the Treasury and Secretary of the Line Ministry in charge of the subject or any other representative of that Ministry nominated by him, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Sri Lanka Press Council Act, No.5 of 1973
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Press Council has been established by the Sri Lanka Press Council Act No 5 of 1973 with the objective of preventing any prejudice to the public by the media reporting of the newspaper media and to create a benevolent relationship between the journalists and the public. Since the provisions of that Act are restricted only to the newspaper, it has been identified that the Press Council should be structurally reformed as a Tribunal for journalists and media institutions covering electronic, print and new media and organized as a Centre for upgrading media education as well. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Mass Media, to appoint a committee comprising of intellects to obtain recommendations for amending the Sri Lanka Press Council Act so as to suit to the present day requirements and to obtain comments and suggestions from the general public and the civil organizations and accordingly, to draft amending legislation,was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the Media Centre for National Development
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body: - It has been found that the Government Policy contained in the the Government Policy Frame Work“Vistas of Prosperity and Splendor”, the strategies to be achieved therein and and their actual progress are not properly communicated to the public. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Mass Media to establish a unit called " Media Centre for National Development" under the Ministry of Mass Media, enabling to disseminate accurate information on Government policies and development efforts to the public, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Key Foreign Policy Directives for 2020 and beyond
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body: - Considering the National Policy Frame Work “Vistas of Prosperity and Splendor” and its Sectoral Policies and the activities under Sri Lanka Foreign Policy, the Foreign Ministry and the Presidential Secretariat have jointly formulated key foreign policy directives consisted with 20 points to be followed in the year 2020 and beyond. This document which enshrines the Foreign Policy vision of the Government will amalgamate the National Security and Economic development with the foreign policy and will guide to play the role within the international arena as a sovereign Nation. Accordingly, the Cabinet considered the information furnished by the Foreign Minister that the aforesaid Key Foreign Policy Directives to be used as the guiding Policy Document for the Foreign Ministry, the State Ministry of Regional Co‑operation and the Sri Lanka Missions Abroad.

description: Appointing a Steering Committee for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body: - At the the General Assembly session of the United Nations held in September 2015, 193 countries including Sri Lanka endorsed the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The World Sustainable Development Report 2020 has shown that several challenges are there to achieve the majority of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals introduced by the said agenda. In order to examine the said situation, the Foreign Minister with the concurrence of the Hon. Prime Minister has appointed a Working Group and the said Group has pointed out the need to have a high - level political leadership to steer the process of achieving Sustainable Development Goals. Accordingly, the joint proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister and the Foreign Minister to appoint a Steering Committee comprising of the relevant Ministers/ State Ministers and the Secretaries to the relevant Ministries, under the chairmanship of the Hon. Prime Minister to steer and guide the process of implementing the Sustainable Development Goals, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Memorandum of Understanding on the Establishment of a Political Consultation Mechanism between Sri Lanka and Afghanistan
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body: - It has been proposed to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Foreign Ministry of Sri Lanka and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan to establish a consultation mechanism with a view to improving the bilateral affairs and cooperation, covering political, security, economic, cultural, education, health, social, people-to-people relations, human resources development and other areas of common interest. As such, the proposal made by the Foreign Minister to enter into the said agreement between the Foreign Ministry of Sri Lanka and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Recognizing 'e-Thaksalawa' as the National Official Learning Contents Management System
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body: - The Ministry of Education has taken action to implement the 'e-Thaksalawa' as an online programme for an uninterrupted school education system against the COVID-19 pandemic situation. Under this program, the students may refer to learning resources such as text books, syllabuses, learning contents, video lessons, question papers and multiple choice questions relevant to the syllabuses from Grade 1 to Grade 13. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education, to recognize the 'e-Thaksalawa' online program as the Official Online Learning Contents Management System in the schools where general education system is in operation and in the other education institutes under the Ministry of Education, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of Regulations issued under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, No.1 of 1969 for approval in Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body: - Considering the recommendations made by the Tariff Determination Committee appointed for the purpose of rationlaizing the importation of goods in response to the pressure on foreign exchange due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, to present two Gazette notifications published for the enactment of relevant regulations under the Import and Export (Control) Act, No.1 of 1969, in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Framework Arrangement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka for securing funds from the Economic Development Cooperation Fund of the EXIM Bank of Korea for the implementation of recognized projects
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body: - With a view to further strengthening the economic cooperation between two countries, the Republic of Korea and the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka entered into a Framework Agreement in 2017 for the implementation of projects mutually agreed and the said agreement has expired in 2019. The Republic of Korea has agreed to grant funds not exceeding US$ 500 million for the implementation of projects recognized within the period of 2020-2022. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, to enter into a new Framework Agreement between the two parties, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of Buildings for advance training and administration, and accommodation for the Coast Guard Sailors at the Sri Lanka Coast Guard Headquarters in Mirissa
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2021-01-04
decision_details_body: - Even though the construction activities of a four storied Advance Training and Administration Building with facilities required for more systematic and efficient operation of the Department Sri Lanka Coast Guard and a five storied Accommodation Building for the purpose of accommodating the Coast Guard Sailors deployed for duty and training have been initiated, the said construction activities have thereafter been suspended as it was decided to transfer the said land to the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA). However, the said Authority has not yet started any development activity on the said land and those buildings are supposed to be constructed as immediately as possible for the operation and administration activities of the Department of the Sri Lanka Coast Guard. As such, the proposal made by H.E.the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence, to restart the construction activities of the said two buildings as immeidately as possible, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Enticing the Airlines to the Mattala Rajapaksa International Airport and the Colombo International Airport, Ratmalana
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - It has been planned to open the Airports for the tourists and accordingly, as a pilot project, necessary actions have been taken to open the Airports for tourists during the period from 2020‑12‑26 to 2021‑01‑19, by following the recommendations of the Health Authorities. As such, the International Airlines will operate according to specific schedules prepared by the Ministry of Tourism and the Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka. Therefore, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Tourism for waiving off the landing and parking fees for the period from 2020‑12‑26 to 2021‑01‑19 from the Airlines to be operated flights to Sri Lanka in order to encourage such Airlines amidsts the crisis presently being faced by the International Aviation sector.

description: Procurement of Food Items for the Tri-Forces for the year 2021
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - National competitive bids have been called for the procurement of food items for the Tri-Forces for the year 2021. Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence to award the contracts for the supply of food items required by the Tri - Forces for the year 2021, to the responsive bidders, as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: House of Justice Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body:
- Provisions have been allocated in the Budget 2021 for the implementation of this project and therefore, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to proceed with the project as follows, enabling to initiate project activities at the beginning of the year 2021:

* 	To award the Consultancy Services Contract of this project to the Central Engineering Consultancy Bureau.
* 	Implementing the project as 04 sub projects and awarding of the contract for the construction of the Magistrate's Court Complex as its first sub-project to the Central Engineering Consultancy Bureau, subject to the price recommendation of the Standing Technical Evaluation Committee of the Ministry of Housing.
* 	Awarding of Contracts for the remaining 3 sub-projects of the project following the competitive bidding procedure.

description: Entering into Memoranda of Understanding on Bilateral Youth Development Programs
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body:
- The proposal made by the Minister of Youth and Sports, to enter into the following Memoranda of Understanding on Youth Development to promote mutually beneficial and long lasting cooperation in the formulation of policies aimed at the development of the youth community was approved by the Cabinet

* 	Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in the field of Youth Development between the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Republic of Tajikistan.
* 	Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in the field of Youth  Development between the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Russian Federation.

description: Expansion of the Kandy Industrial Park
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - The Kandy Industrial Park owned by the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka was established in 1994 and covers an area of 195 acres. Out of this about 120 acres of land which can be utilized for setting up industries have been allotted for 26 industries. It has been proposed to expand the industrial park using the nearby 5.65 hectares of government owned land and accordingly the proposal made by the Minister of Tourism to transfer the said plot of land to the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka as a free grant, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Sri Lanka and South Africa on Cooperation in the Field of Tourism
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - The Memorandum of Understanding between Sri Lanka and South Africa on Cooperation in the field of Tourism was expired in 2017 and at the Sixth Session of the Sri Lanka - South Africa Partnership Forum in 2018, it was proposed to enter into a new Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in the field of Tourism between the two parties. Accordingly the proposal made by the Minister of Tourism to sign a new MoU between the two parties, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of an Inter-Ministerial Committee for Sustainable Environment Management
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - Implementation of a Sustainable Environment Policy in line with the Government Manifesto, “Vistas of Prosperity and Splendor” is the leading responsibility of the Ministries and Institutions related to the subject of Environment including the Ministry of Environment. It has been found the necessity to act collaboratively by all the institutions related to the subject of environment to make aware the public as well as to provide accurate information on facts presented in print, electronic and social media when performing the said task. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to establish an Inter-Ministerial Coordinating Committee under the coordination of the of the Ministry of Environment together with the participation of the relevant Ministries and Institutes, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Conducting a Feasibility Study in order to implement a Urea Fertilizer Manufacturing Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - Annual Fertilizer Requirement in Sri Lanka is about 340,000 metric tons. The entire quantity is currently being imported. In 2019,  Rs.26 billion have been spent for importation of urea fertilizer. However, it is possible to save the foreign exchange spent on the importation of urea fertilizer through manufacturing of urea within the country itself and the Paranthan Chemicals Company Ltd. which is operated under the Ministry of Industries has focused its attention in that regard. Accordingly, considering the proposal made by the Minister of Industries with regard to the conduct of a feasibility study for the production of urea fertilizer in Sri Lanka, the Cabinet decided to entrust the Sri Lanka Institute of Nano Technology (Pvt) Ltd. to conduct the above feasibility study.

description: Protecting the local coconut oil manufacturers and the Sri Lankan coconut oil brand by developing a coconut based industrial system
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body:
- Industrialists and experts in the field of coconut industry have pointed out that if more attention is paid to the coconut industry in Sri Lanka, production can be increased by 50%. Investigations carried out by the Consumer Affairs Authority have confirmed that the coconut oil imported into the country contains nearly 70% of non-coconut oils. Due to the insufficient number of coconuts produced in the country, the continuation of production activities of about 500 factories of coconut and allied products are currently in crisis. As the export income of Sri Lankan coconut oil and coconut related products have increased by 16.6% in 2019 when compared to 2018, it seems that there is a possibility of creating a new trend in the coconut industry with the Government sponsorship.

Accordingly, the following joint proposals submitted by the Minister of Industry and the Minister of Plantation for the development of the coconut related industries were approved by the Cabinet-

*	Importation of broken copra for a period of three months instead of importing coconut oil, in order to encourage the local coconut oil producers.
*	Importation of broken copra with testa by BCC Company, which is a 	state owned institute.
	*	Strictly prohibition the mixing of palm oil or any other type of oil with 		coconut oil and sell them in order to protect consumer rights and Sri 		Lankan brand for coconut oil.
*	Recognizing that discouraging the consumption of palm oil within the country by popularizing coconut oil as a 	fundamental 	policy of the Government and granting permission to import only refined palm oil concerning consumer rights and public health issues. 	
*	Granting concessions to repay loans of coconut industrialists. 
*	Introducing relief packages to increase the productivity of coconut 	plantations such as under planting, dairy farming and water supply to 	encourage the coconut cultivation.
	*	 Establishment of an Inter-Ministerial Task Force representing the 			relevant Ministries and Institutions to implement and monitor this 			program.

description: Amendment to the Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Act No.02 of 1996
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2016‑04‑26 to amend the Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Act No. 2 of 1996 so as to increase the penalties against obstructions caused to the authorized officers in the implementation of the provisions of the said Act and at the meeting held on 2019‑07‑07, approval has also been granted to amend the said Act incorporating the provisions to regulate the illegal activities. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Fisheries, to instruct the Legal Draftsman to drat a bill incorporating the proposed amendments, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Enforcement of Trade Remedies Laws
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - The Anti- Dumping and Countervailing Duties Act No. 2 of 2018 and the Safeguard Measures Act, No. 3 of 2018 have been enforced to act against the unfair trade practices and importation of goods in large scale that harm local industries. The effective dates of the said Acts should be published by Gazette Notifications by the Minister in charge of the subject and accordingly, the relevant gazette notification has been issued informing that the said Acts are effective from 19th October 2020. Accordingly, the Cabinet considered the information furnished by the Foreign Minister and the Minister of Industries that the Director General of Commerce is eligible to act as the authorized officer for taking necessary measures to avoid any unfavourable circumstances caused to the local industries under the said two Acts.

description: Updating the Partnership Agreement on the Pilot Project conducted using Wolbachia bacteria to control Dengue in the Colombo District
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - An international research corporation programme named “World Mosquito Programme” is being implemented by the University of Monash with the objective of protecting global population from the deceases such as Dengue, Zika, Chikungunya and Hepatitis spread by mosquitoes through new biological control methods. ‘Wolbachia’ bacteria has been introduced under this programme to minimize the spread of dengue virus by reducing its replication within the Aedes mosquito that spread Dengue. Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2018‑01‑09 to use the bacteria within the areas under the areas of Nugegoda MOH and a selected division in the Colombo Municipal Council. A Collaborative Agreement has been signed between the Ministry of Health and the University of Monash to implement the said pilot programme and its valid period has already been expired by now. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Health for amending the said agreement enabling to continue the supervision and evaluation activities of that programme up to 2021, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: National Mental Health Policy 2020-2030
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - A Mental Health Policy formulates the strategic framework for the prevention of mental illnesses, healing, rehabilitation and mental health promotion within the community. The previous Mental Health Policy in Sri Lanka has been formulated in the year 2005 and it was effective for 10 years. Therefore, the need to update the said policy has been recognized for the coordination and supervision of the progress of those strategies so as to suit to the present day requirements. Accordingly, the National Mental Health Policy has been formulated under the major sectors of strengthening leadership and research activities, provision of extended mental health services, human resources development and empowering the community and the proposal made by the Minister of Health for the implementation of the said Mental Health Policy 2020 – 2030, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing a Protective Overall Kit for the students who undergo vocational training in the workshops
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - A considerable amount of provisions have been allocated by the budget 2021 for expanding the vocational education field by increasing the number of students annually enrolled from 100,000 to 200,000 giving priority to the sectors with a blooming market demand. Already 09 institutions are being operated for the provision of training related to the workshops and construction sites implemented under the State Ministry of Skills Development, Vocational Education, Research and Innovation at present. Approximately 30,000 apprentices are undergoing the training at present under the purview of these institutions and the said amount is expected to be increased up to a 40,000 with the enrolment for the year 2021. It has been planned to provide an overall kit for each trainee so that their security during the training is ensured as well as to engage in the relevant training as a modern vocational craftsman better than a traditional worker. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to provide a protective overall kit to those students enrolled in the vocational education institutes and undergo trainings in the workshops from the month of January 2021 and the said overall kit to be manufactured and ordered from “Ranaviru Apparels Institute” of the Sri Lanka Army, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Declaring Devagiri Rajamaha Viharaya as a Pooja Bhoomi (Sacred Place) by a Gazette Notification
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - The historical background of Devagiri Raja MahaViharaya in the Bingiriya Divisional Secretariat Division of Kurunegala district goes back to 204 - 207 BC and several ruins with an archaeological value have been identified within that premises. The Department of National Physical Planning has started to prepare a development plan for the premises coincident with the National Vesak festival in the year 2018, and some of the development activities have been initiated to be implemented with the provisions of the Ministry of Buddhasasana under the consultation of the above Department. Accordingly, the Cabinet considered the information furnished by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing that actions have been taken to declare the “Sacred Premises of Devagiri Raja Maha Viiharaya” by the Gazette Notification in terms of the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Ordinance No. 13 of 194, enabling to prepare the said development plan and implement the same.

description: Declaring the Kolawenigama Rajamaha Viharaya as a Pooja Bhoomi (Sacred Place) by a Gazette Notification
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - Kolawenigama Raja MahaViharaya situated in Kotapola Divisional Secretariat division in Matara consists of numerous factors reflecting historical values along with a Stupa of more than 400 years old and an ancient Bo tree. The sacred area situated within a land in extent of 05 acres is governed under section 4(11) of Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance No. 19 of 1931. Therefore, it is found necessary to focus attention on the unidentified heritages within the temple land premises. Accordingly, the Cabinet considered the information furnished by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing that the Department of National Physical Planning has taken initiatives to prepare a development plan in relation to the conservation of the Raja Maha Viharaya and accordingly, actions have been taken to declare the “Sacred premises of the Kolawenigama Raja Maha Viiharaya” by the Gazette Notification in terms of the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Ordinance No. 13 of 1946.

description: Alienation of a plot of land at Ratnapura New Town to the Sabaragamuwa Provincial Council to set up an Office Complex
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - The land called Palm Garden in extent of 348 acres at Ratnapura has been taken over by the Urban Development Authority for the Ratnapura New Town Development Project. The Chief Secretary of the Sabaragamuwa Province has requested the Urban Development Authority to allocate a plot of land for Sabaragamuwa Provincial Council Office Complex. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing to allocate a plot of land in extent of 04 acres and 02 roods from Palm Garden land to the Sabaragamuwa Provincial Council for a lease period of 50 years, subject to payment of an estimated value imposed by the Government Chief Valuer, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Support to Justice Sector in Sri Lanka Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-21
decision_details_body: - The European Union has extended its willingness to provide a grant of Euro 18 million to implement a project by the name of “Support to Justice Sector in Sri Lanka Project”, with a view to setting up an improved and responsive justice system in Sri Lanka by improving the accessibility and quality of service delivery. The said project will be implemented by the Ministry of Justice and the total estimated cost is Euro 19.27 million. Balance provisions for the project will be financed by the United Nations Childeren's Fund (UNICEF) and the United Nations Development Programme in addition to the provisions granted by the European Union. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, to enter into a Grant Agreement with the European Union to obtain that grant, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of the International Gem and Jewellery Trade Centre
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body:
- It has been planned to construct the International Gem and Jewellery Trade Centre at Demuwawatha, Ratnapura by investing the funds of the National Gem and Jewellery Authority to enable to provide all the services and facilities under one roof, such as independent quality testing services, laboratory services and banking services, export services and required services for the sellers and buyers as in Bangkok and Hong Kong, the leading sales centres for Gem and Jewellery in Asia. Accordingly, it has been planned to construct a 05 storey building with a floor area of 17,550 square feet at a cost of Rs. 365 Million, in a land in extent of  22 perches in Demuwawatha, Ratnapura as the first phase of the project and to acquire the adjacent plot of land to the aforementioned plot of land and build a modern building with 14 stories as the second phase.

	As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries to award the contract for the design and construction of the proposed building as the first phase of the project as a direct contract to the Central Engineering Consultancy Bureau, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs Ordinance
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - The Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs Ordinance has been amended in the years 1984 and 1986. However, several people in the field of legal profession have pointed out that the provisions therein are not sufficient for present day requirements. Various parties have pointed out the need to reconsider the  provisions in the Act, especially, on the fact that some of the drugs currently in the circulation are not covered by this Act and on the existing provisions of giving equal punishments for drug addicts, persons who inadvertently involved in such activities and persons involved in large – scale drug trafficking. Accordingly, taking into consideration the proposal made by the Minister of Justice, the Cabinet granted approval to appoint a Committee comprising of the representation of the parties including Religious Leaders, Experts in the field of legal profession, Members of the  Security Forces, Conductors of Rehabilitation programmes for drug addicts for the purpose of obtaining recommendations to amend the said Ordinance in accordance with the present requirements and to amend the Ordinance based on the recommendations made by the aforesaid Committee.

description: Amendment to the Registration of Documents Ordinance (Caveat)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - At present no buyer will buy a land with a Caveat and a land of that type can not be mortgaged to any  lending institution. Certain fraudulent people are found to have obtained Caveat orders from courts for certain lands which they have no legal right to claim ownership or interest and used such Caveat Orders as a tactical means of taking extortion from the actual owner.  In order to prevent the occurrence of such incidents, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to amend the Registration of Documents Ordinance as proposed by the Law Commission and to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft a bill for the purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Convention against Torture and other Cruel, Inhuman and Degrading Treatment or Punishment Act, No.22 of 1994
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - Torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment is explicitly prohibited by Article 11 of the Constitution. Such people should be condemned and punished in the strongest possible manner. Therefore, it has been identified that fines in the Convention against Torture and other Cruel, Inhuman and Degrading Treatment or Punishment Act, No.22 of 1994 should be revised to suite to the present day requirement. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft a bill for the purpose of amending the said Act, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the National Transport Commission  Act, No. 37 of 1991
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - It has been identified that certain provisions in the National Transport Commission Act No 37 of 1991 are not applicable to meet the complexity in present transport system. Therefore, it has been identified that it is appropriate to amend the said Act and accordingly the proposal made by the Minister of Justice to instruct the Legal Draftsman to draft a bill to amend the said Act, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of the Universities Act, No.16 of 1978 for inclusion of provisions required for the establishment of Universities with specific purposes in this country in order to convert Colleges of Nursing and Teacher Training Colleges into Universities
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - It has been identified the need to create globally competitive professionals with high professional recognition and proficiency, enhancing the quality of Nursing and Teaching professions in order to build a knowledge based economy through human resource development within the Government Policy Framework “Vistas of Prosperity”. At present, there is a high demand for nursing and teaching professionals in global competitive job market. The need to improve the quality of Nursing Colleges operating under the supervision and regulation of the Ministry of Health and Teacher Training Colleges which produce teaching professionals functioning under the Ministry of Education has also been identified and it is observed that establishing of two separate universities for the said purpose is appropriate. Therefore, the joint proposal made by the Minister of Education and the Minister of Health to amend the Universities Act, No.16 of 1978, enabling to establish the proposed two universities as universities with specific purposes, deviating from the traditional modal universities, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submitting the General Sir John Kotelawala National Defence University Bill in Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2013‑03‑01 to repeal the existing  General Sir John Kotelawala National Defence University Act and to introduce a new Act to further expand the academic activities of the General Sir John Kotelawala National Defence University for the purpose of enhancing its role and functions as a National Defence University. Accordingly, the Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman has been published in the Government Gazette and the proposal made by H.E. the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence to present the said Gazette Notification in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Kithul Crop' to be nominated as a major plantation crop in Sri Lanka and establishment of the Kithul Development Board
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - Kithul related production industry which is endemic to Sri Lanka is recognized as a highly potential industry for earning foreign exchange and various actions have been taken to uplift the Kithul industry during the previous periods. It has been found that expansion of Kithul related industry under the programme to create a public centred economy across the promotion of local products implemented by the present government is appropriate. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Plantation to nominate Kithul crop as a major plantation crop and to establish the Kithul Development Board, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: National Policy on Access to Biological Material and Fair and Equitable Benefit Sharing
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka is considered to be the leading country in Asia in is bio-diversity and  the country is also internationally recognized as a country which is abundant  with fertile marshy lands / wet lands, coastal belts and marine bio – diversity. Despite the actions have been taken to conserve the bio – diversity and to  prevent bio-theft and bio-piracy, it seems that such misappropriations continuous occur. It is also observed that, Sri Lanka would lose the benefits to be accrued to the country, if  the specimens that are sent out of the country for taxonomic identification, would be used by the developed countries for making new products without having obtanied the consent of Sri Lanka. As a remedy for the problem, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment, pertaining to the “National Policy on Access to Biological Material and Fair and Equitable Benefit Sharing” which has been drafted with the participation of all stakeholders under the guidance of the Special Committee on the  National Policy on Access to Biological Material and Fair and Equitable Benefit Sharing, functioning under the Ministry of Environment and its implementation mechanism by the State Institutions, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Gem and Jewellery (License Fee) Regulations No.1 of 2020 for approval in Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - Each regulation made by the Minister in charge as per the provisions of Section 53 of the National Gem and Jewellery Authority Act No. 50 of 1993, should be published in the Government Gazette and thereafter present the same in Parliament for approval. Accordingly,  the proposal made by the Minister of Industries to present the “Gem and Jewellery (License Fee) Regulations No.1 of 2020” published by the Gazette Notification 2020‑03‑01 by the Minister in charge of the subject for the purpose of formalizing the fees charged for the services provided by the said Authority, in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Application of Land Acquisition (Compensation) Regulations 2013 for the Road Projects of Ruwanpura Expressway Project and the Port City Elevated Expressway Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - Measures have been taken to compensate for the lands acquired for 18 projects implemented under the Ministry of Highways, in terms of the provisions of the “Land Acquisition (Compensation) Regulations 2013” published under the Extraordinary Gazette Notification No.1864/54. Under those provisions, the affected parties may possible to presence themselves to the Land Acquisition and Resettlement Committee and obtain concessions in addition to the statutory compensation. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Highways to make apply the Land Acquisition (Compensation) Regulations 2013 also for the Road Projects of Ruwanpura Expressway Project and the Port City Elevated Expressway Project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: “Irrigation Prosperity” Accelerated Irrigation Rehabilitation Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - Since there is not any specific financial source for maintaining approximately 50,000 rural small scale rural tanks, anicuts and canal systems and cascade systems scattered throughout the island, it has been found difficult to maintain them. Due to this situation, it is observed that approximately 1,000 rural irrigation systems are destroyed at the end of monsoon rains of each year and  as a result of that, around 150,000 acres of cultivable paddy lands have been turned baron. As a remedy for the issue, an accelerated two year programme named ‘Irrigation Prosperity’ has been planned to be implemented in order to re - activate 5,000 small scale rural irrigation and drinking water systems under the guidance of the Presidential Task Force on Economic Revival and Poverty Alleviation with the objective of increasing the national food production. The proposed programme has been planned to be implemented deviating from the contract procedure and using human resources and machines owned by the Government with the participation of rural level religious leadership, farmer community, school system, youth community as well as the contribution of the Private sector, subject to obtaining labour from the rural farmer community  on daily payment basis as far as possible. Accordingly, the Cabinet considered the information submitted by the Minister of Irrigation, that the initiatives pertaining to the inauguration of the said programme for 1000 rural reservoirs, on 2021‑02‑04 has been organized.

description: Designing of the Vehicle Number Plate Issuance Process in a way that is convenient for clients by removing the provincial letter
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - In the process of vehicle registration, Provincial identification letters are added to vehicle number plates, thereby making ease the process of the vehicular emission test and in the issuance of annual revenue licenses. However, both the customers as well as the Department of Motor Traffic have  encountered many difficulties since the number plates have to be changed at each instance the right of ownership of the vehicles are transferred between provinces. Since a unique number is issued to each registered vehicle at the time of registration, the identity of each vehicle can be easily recognized via the departmental data base. Considering those facts, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport to remove the provincial letters at time of issuance of vehicle number plates, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining approval to adopt the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi - Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC)  Charter
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi - Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) was established in the year 1997 as a forum to stimulate corporation in the Bay of Bengal region. The cooperation is comprised of seven (07) countries namely Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Myanmar, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand. As decided at the Fourth Summit held in Kathmandu in 2018, initiatives have been taken to prepare a draft Charter  for the purpose of formulating institutional guidelines for the cooperation and the formulation of the said Charter has been completed at the 21st Session of the Senior Official's Meeting of the BIMSTEC. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Foreign Minister to adopt the said Charter as a member state at the 5th Summit of BIMSTEC scheduled to be held in Sri Lanka in early 2021, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of a Sri Lanka Consulate General Office in Antananarivo, Madagascar
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - The diplomatic relations between Sri Lanka and Madagascar have been initiated in the year 2001 and Sri Lanka High Commission in Victoria, Seashells is concurrently accredited to Madagascar. Considering the enormous economic opportunities available for Sri Lanka as well as the requirements of migrant Sri Lankans and businessmen residing in Madagascar, it seems appropriate to set up a Consulate General Office in Madagascar. Accordingly, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Foreign Minister   for opening a Sri Lanka Consulate General Office in Madagascar.

description: Amendment of the project period and number of houses constructed under the 'Virusumithuru Housing Project'
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - In terms of the Cabinet decision dated 2017‑04‑04, the 'Virusumithuru Housing Project' is implemented by the National Housing Development Authority together with the Ranaviru Sewa Authority for the families of the war heroes who have sacrificed their lives and injured at the battle field operations. The project duration is 04 years and it was scheduled to be completed by 2020. However, another 346 beneficiaries for the construction of new houses and 2,454 beneficiaries for completion of constructions of the partially constructed houses have been selected under the project. Therefore, the Cabinet approved the joint proposal made by H.E the President and the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing to amend the scope of the said project enabling to complete 4000 partially built houses since there is a rising demand for the completion of such houses and to build 450 new houses as well as to extend the project duration until the end of 2022.

description: Making a Free Grant for the land where the Faculty of Graduate Studies of the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University has been located
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-14
decision_details_body: - The Faculty of Graduate Studies of the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University has been established in a plot of land in extent of 01 rood and 37.2 perches. The said land plot has been taken over by the Government in terms of the interim provision 38(A) of the Land Acquisition Act. Accordingly, the proposal made by H.E the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence to vest the said plot of land with General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University as a free grant under the Section 6(1) of the State Lands Ordinance, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the contract of 10MW Wind Power Plant for the Trincomalee Grid Substation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - It has been decided to add  a wind power capacity 60 MW for the electricity supply system through Trincomalee, Mannar, Bolawatta, Madampe and Kappalthure Grid Substations with the view to increase the usage of renewable energy sources. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Power to award the contract for the purchase of 10MW wind power capacity for a time period of 20 years for Trincomalee Grid Substation at the rate of Rs.14.52 per unit (14.52 LKR/Kwh)and to construct the above mentioned power plant inter connectedly to the transmission network for the Capital City Holdings (Pvt)Ltd., by following the international competitive bidding procedure and as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Negotiating, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the 100 MW Siyambalanduwa Solar Power Plant under the Private Sector Investment
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - The necessary preliminary steps such as feasibility study, allocation of lands, environmental impact assessment etc., have been taken at present to implement the Siyabalanduwa Solar Power Plant. The assistance of the Asian Development Bank has been received to conduct an implementation method on the development of that power plant and the financial analysis. The said analysis has proved that the single power plant of 100MW and transmission facilities should be implemented as a single procument of 100 MW single power plant and transmission facilities, if it is to obtain the lowest charge for power purchase for the generation and transmission of a unit of electricity according to the various capacity opportunities that could be implemented. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Power to initiate the procurement procedure by the Ceylon Electricity Board, the licensee of transmission, to implement the proposed project through private sector investments and to construct the power line from Medagama to Ampara by the Ceylon Electricity Board under the aforementioned project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding of the Contract for the Supply, Installation and Supervision of two 132/33kV, 45MVA Power Transformers for the Wagawatta Grid Substation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - Competitive Bids have been called to award the contract for the Supply, Installation and Supervision of two 132/33kV, 45MVA Power Transformers for the Wagawatta Grid Substation. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Power to award the said contract to  M/s PT.CG. Power Systems, Indonesia to a sum of Rs.245.62 million (Excluding VAT), as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the Contract for the construction of the Engineering Faculty Building of the University of Sri Jayawardenepura
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - International Competitive Bids have been called for construction of the Engineering Faculty Building of the University of Sri Jayawardhanapura under the Science and Technology Human Resources Development Project on design and build basis. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to award the said contract to M/s Sanken Constructions (Pvt) Ltd., to a sum of Rs.3,624.96 million (Excluding VAT), as recommended by the Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee , was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Yakkala, Werellawatta Middle Income Housing Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - The Urban Development Authority has planned to implement a middle income housing project with 500 houses in the Werellawatta area in Yakkala under 03 phases. Preliminary work is prepared to construct 154 houses under its first phase as a 12-storey building comprising of 132 houses of 600 square feet and 22 houses of 900 square feet. The total estimated cost of the project is Rs.1503.30 million and the cost of construction is expected to be secured through pre-sales. Accordingly the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing for the implementation of the proposed project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of two buildings consisting of 30 houses under the Soyzapura Relocation Housing Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2014‑10‑16 to implement the Soysapura Relocation Housing Project for the construction of 05 buildings consisting 20 houses each to relocate 48 dilapidated two-storey, half-rented houses and 24 dilapidated shanties located within the premises of the Soysapura Housing Scheme. Accordingly, the relevant families have been resettled in 60 houses constructed in 3 buildings. Though, 40 houses on a pre-sale basis were planned to be built in the remaining two buildings it has been observed that only 30 houses can be constructed under the existing provisions. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing to construct 30 houses each consisting of 550 square feet on pre-sale basis, as a building consisting of 20 houses and a building consisting of 10 houses under the Soysapura Housing Project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of a Building for the proposed Army Base Hospital at Pallekale
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - A new base hospital is designed to be constructed at Pallekele, Kandy to provide basic medical treatment to army personnel serving and residing in Kandy and surrounding districts. For the purpose, it is expected to construct a 3 storey building and the estimated cost is Rs.376.22 million. Accordingly the proposal made by H.E the President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence  to complete the construction of the proposed hospital within a year using the labour of other ranks of the Sri Lanka Army Professionals and to secure provisions required for the purpose from the General Treasury, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Increase the quality seed production required to enhance the availability of crop production in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - The "Food Production National Program", launched in the Yala season 2020 to reduce imports by cultivating locally grown crops, is now being successfully implemented. Since it is difficult for the Department of Agriculture alone to provide quality seeds to increase harvests and the area of cultivated lands the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture to implement a formal program in collaboration with the Provincial and Inter-Provincial Departments of Agriculture and the Seed Producers' Institutions in the Mahaweli areas, enabling the farmers to produce their own  seed requirements in respective areas.

description: Establishment of the 1000 Acre Fodder Silage Baling Project  at the Polonnaruwa Farm of the National Livestock Development Board
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - Lack of quality roughage has been identified as a major issue in large scale dairy farms belonging to the National Livestock Development Board and generally, one dairy cow should be fed with roughage of about 10% of her body weight. As a remedy to this situation, it has been planned to commence a Fodder Silage Baling Project within 1000 acres  of the Polonnaruwa farm of the National Livestock Development Board. As its initial stage, it has been planned to cultivate 1000 acres of nutritive maize and sorghum and produce mechanized baled silage and to import 2000 dairy cows and keep them in the farms as the second phase of the project, Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agricultur to obtain 60% of the total capital expenditure estimated for the project as a government contribution, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Securing necessary financial support for the working capital requirement of the Laksala
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - Revenue earned by Laksala  has dropped by 90% due to the absence of foreign tourists due to the Covid-19 pandemic, making it difficult to run the institution. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Industries to secure the necessary provisions from the General Treasury for salaries and working capital requirements including other essential expenses required to function the Laksala, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Formulating a Long-Term 'Human Resource Development Plan' for the Public Service
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - Formulation and implementation of a long-term "Human Resource Development Plan" has been identified as an urgent programme for enhancing the performance and productivity of the public sector. Public Administration Circular No. 02/2018 dated 2018‑01‑24, emphasizes the need of preparing a Human Resource Development Plan by every State Institution. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Public Services, Provincial Councils and Local Government to formulate a long term "Human Resource Development Plan" with the participation of all relevant parties to enhance the efficiency and productivity of the public service, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Increasing the number of National Schools to 1000
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - Policy approval has been granted by the Cabinet at its meeting held on 2019‑12‑10 to implement an appropriate program to establish 1000 new National Schools covering all Divisional Secretariat Divisions. Accordingly, the program is planned to be implemented in three phases and the proposal made by the Minister of Education to implement the relevant programme to develop one selected Provincial Council School as a National School in each of the 123 Divisional Secretariat Divisions in which there are no National Schools as the first phase, to upgrade 673 schools selected on the basis of identified criteria as National Schools under the second phase and to further develop the existing 373 National Schools under the third phase,was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of the Institutional Name of the Children's Secretariat as the 'National Secretariat for Early Childhood Development'
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - The "Children's Secretariat" which has been established in the year 1979, functions as the central institution that executes the National Policy on Early Childhood Care and Development. Though the institute also plays a special role in the field of early childhood education, it seems that, the current institutional name of the said Secretariat does not imply that role. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Education to amend the institutional name of “Children's Secretariat” as “National Secretariat for Early Childhood Development”, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of the method of payment of four housing projects implemented with the Indian Government Aid
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - The Government of India has granted an award of Rs.300 million each for implementing 04 projects for the construction of houses for low – income families and the relevant projects are being implemented by the National Housing Development Authority. Steps will be taken to release applicable funds followed by a progress report submitted to the Indian High Commission by National Housing Development Authority upon the completion of the relevant construction by the beneficiaries with their cost. However, since the house owners do not have sufficient funds to complete the construction as supposed that the progress of the project lies at a lower level. Therefore the Indian High Commission has agreed to release the initial payment required for the construction at the inauguration of work and continue to release the rest of the instalments on the progress of the construction. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing for taking necessary action to implement the said projects,  was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Sri Lanka Land Development Corporation Act, No.15 of 1968
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2015‑12‑02 for further amendment of the Sri Lanka Land Development Corporation Act, No. 15 of 1968 (Amended) as amended by the Acts, No. 27 of 1976, No. 52 of 1982, No. 35 of 2006 and No. 11 of 2019. Accordingly, clearance from the Attorney General has been received for the draft bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in his capacity as the Minister of Urban Development & Housing to publish the said draft bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter present the same in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Performing essential renovation and rehabilitation activities of the Mahinda Rajapaksa National Tele Cinema Park
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2020-12-07
